title: 6pm Planning Board Public Hearing (subdivision application for The Campus at Pineland Farms) @ MH (televised)
html:
Town of New Gloucester

NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING

The New Gloucester Planning Board will hold a public hearing on Tuesday October 6 at 6:00 p.m. regarding a major subdivision application for The Campus at Pineland Farms. The public hearing will be held at the New Gloucester Meetinghouse at 389 Intervale Road, New Gloucester, Maine.

If you have additional questions or would like to review the application, please contact the Town Planner at 207-926-4126 ext. 4 or townplanner@newgloucester.com

html:
NEW GLOUCESTER PLANNING BOARD

Minutes of May 6, 2008

Members Present: Wanda Brissette, Laurie Brady, Jean Libby, Sue Robitaille & Ruth Waterhouse

Members Absent: Lisa Lemont, unexcused

Vacancies: 1

Town Staff: Rebeccah Schaffner, Planner; Amanda Lessard, Assistant Planner

Others Present: Gary Sacco, Fire Chief; Jim Pelsor, Bunker & Savage Architects; Bruce Hilfrank, Zachau Construction; Deb Cluchey, Linda Liberty, Sean Chayer; Roger Levasseur; Harold Bartlett, Richard Cadigan

  1. Call to Order

Meeting called to order at 7:04 p.m.

  1. Approval of Minutes: April 15, 2008

a. A motion to approve the minutes was made by R.Waterhouse; seconded by L.Brady; approved 4-0-1. S.Robitaille abstained.

  1. Elect Planning Board Vice Chair

A motion to nominate W.Brisette as Vice Chair was made by R.Waterhouse; seconded by S.Robitaille; approved 5-0.

  1. Public Hearing

New Gloucester Public Safety Building

Map/Lot 0007-0014

611 Lewiston Road

J.Libby asked J.Pelsor to describe the project to the public as had previously been presented to the Planning Board. He explained the major features and also handed out an architectural rendering of the proposed public safety building.

J.Libby opened the Public Hearing at 7:15 pm.

Linda Liberty, abutting property owner, asked for additional information on the drainage and where it is being directed. J.Pelsor described the topography of the natural runoff and the approved Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) and Cumberland County Soil and Water Conservation District (CCSWCD) plan where water runs into large stone swales. They hold the increased runoff difference from pre-development to post-development so that in a 24 hour, 2-year storm there is no net increase in the runoff. The water is slowed allowing it to have time to infiltrate the buffer.

Deb Cluchey, speaking on behalf of her mother Ann Philips, an abutter, asked if runoff is anticipated to run towards Route 100. J.Pelsor replied no, the stormwater plan is to replicate natural runoff at pre-development conditions. D.Cluchey also expressed concern for the use of hazardous training materials. G.Sacco said the firefighting foam is biodegradable and not toxic. She then asked about materials that will be burned. G.Sacco said it will be the same traditional burns that are currently conducted down behind the public works building. They may in the future consider a concrete pad that would collect water for expanded training opportunities.

Richard Cadigan, abutter, asked about future plans for the rest of the site and asked why the site survey of wetlands was done in the winter. He also commented that the first draft of the plan cited the location as Route 26. G.Sacco said Owen Haskell did a preliminary wetland evaluation right after the land was purchased. The Town then realized it needed additional site evaluation and hired Mark Hampton in October 2007. The Planning Board has also requested the vernal pool assessment be submitted, and the Town has entered into an agreement with Mark Hampton to conduct that study. R.Cadigan asked for a wetland survey of the rest of property. G.Sacco said that it is not in the scope of work.

L.Liberty asked if the rangeway use will be discontinued. R.Schaffner said that legally the public doesn’t have use of the rangeway. The Town reserves the right to take over a rangeway and use it for a public way. Rangeways are currently reserved but on private land. A requirement of the DEP permit was that the rangeway on this property not be developed and the 100 foot buffer must be maintained.

D.Cluchey asked for further clarification of the 25% of development permissible within the vernal pool setback. J.Pelsor explained that within a 250 foot radius from the edge of the wetland that may have a vernal pool of significance there can only be disturbance of up to 25% of the land that the town controls. Originally the development was planned to be closer to the wetland to reduce costs and site disturbance but was revised in case the vernal pool was deemed significant.

D.Cluchey asked if there would be sound abatement for emergency vehicles leaving the site. G.Sacco said the sirens are needed on the street, but there will be a policy that they won’t be run in the bay. The Maine Department of Transportation (DOT) permit requires that there are warning signs that signal emergency vehicles are entering the roadway. There is occasion that the siren is accidentally engaged entering and exiting the truck since the siren is activated by a foot pedal.

J.Libby closed the public hearing at 7:30pm.

  1. Project Reviews

Site Plan

New Gloucester Public Safety Building

Map/Lot 0007-0014

611 Lewiston Road

W.Brissette asked for clarification since the March 18, 2008 Planning Board meeting minutes referred to the Convalt tank as 350 gallons. J.Pelsor said it is 250 gallons. It is above ground on a concrete pad. W.Brissette asked about the 1000 gallon septic tank. J.Pelsor said it is below ground and a primary treatment for shower and toilet water that is then sent to a 4000 gallon underground chambered septic tank. J.Pelsor said it will be wired and have an alarm to alert the fire station when it needs to be pumped.

J.Libby went through a list of submission requirements, performance standards, and approval criteria as outlined in the zoning ordinance. The DEP permit has been received. A vernal pool assessment submitted by July 15, 2008 was a condition of application completeness and will also be a condition of approval. The Town will contract a clerk of the works for the development process. All other criteria have been met.

D.Cadigan asked if the 250 gallon diesel fuel tank causes risk of contamination since there is concern for the ones at the public garage. W.Brissette asked if the proposed tank is the same as those at the public works garage. G.Sacco said it is a better system since it is a tank within a tank to prevent leaks. J.Libby responded that if the Fire Station Committee wants to include it on the plan, it is allowed.

R.Levasseur asked if the requirement of a vernal pool assessment would delay the approval process since DEP no longer has an issue with the vernal pools. W.Brissette said it won’t affect the permit and it was a recommendation of the DEP that the assessment be carried out.

A motion to approve the public safety building with the condition that the vernal pool assessment be completed by July 15, 2008 was made by R.Waterhouse; seconded by S.Robitaille; Site Plan approved 5-0.

R.Schaffner asked the applicant to submit copies of the final plan with the conditions printed on them so that they can be signed at the next meeting.

  1. Other Business

None

  1. Plan Signing

None

  1. Adjournment

R.Waterhouse moved to adjourn; seconded by S.Robitaille; approved 5-0. Meeting adjourned at 7:47 p.m.

  1. Future Meetings

a. Regular Meeting – Tuesday, May 20, 2008.

Minutes prepared by A.Lessard

title: March 21, 2006
html:
NEW GLOUCESTER PLANNING BOARD

Minutes of March 21, 2006

Members Present: Others Present:

Jean Libby, Chairman Ann Strout

Karen Asselin, Vice Chairman Larry Strout

Wanda Brissette Steve Chandler

Ruth Waterhouse Roger Levasseur

Janet Smaldon Gary Sacco, Fire Chief

Sue Robitaille Vinal Zegouros

Ellie Fellers

Absent: Jeff Hamilton, Sr.

Laurie Brady (excused) Debbie Parks

Beth Fontaine

Jean welcomed Wanda Brissette as a new member of the New Gloucester Planning Board.

Motion: To review and approve the Minutes of March 7, 2006 as written, with the correction of the spelling of Vinal Zegouros’ last name. The correct spelling is “Zegouros.” Ruth, second Karen. 6-0.

Sabbathday Road Commercial Subdivision

The Planning Board is meeting to approve two lots, no buildings, that Vinal Zegouros will be selling. Jean opened the Public Hearing on this matter at 7:35 p.m. and invited anyone with questions to come forward.

Ann Strout, resident of Mayall Road requested an explanation of the businesses for these lots and where they will be accessed from - Mayall Road or Sabbathday Road? Jean explained that any businesses buying the land will have to come before the Planning Board for review and stated there will not be access for the businesses on Mayall Road. There may be access for another piece of land that is owned by Zegouros, but not for the businesses.

Jean asked for other questions. There being none the Public Hearing was closed at 7:38 p.m.

Karen raised a question concerning Mayall Road access to the land. Jean’s understanding is that it is not on the Plan at this time because Zegouros did not want to hold up approval tonight. Zegouros will come back with an amendment unless it is agreed on tonight and then have it added to the plan. Zegouros has met with Kevin Doyle the Public Works Director. Kevin said in a memo that there is “a 420’ site distance and in more detail there are no issues with site distance because of reduced speed in connection with the intersection. Any drainage issues will be addressed by the property owner. I have changed my opinion on the driveway opening, and I now have no objections to approve an entrance at the location specified on the plan.” As Jean told the abutter, Ann Strout, this is not considered an entrance for a business. If this is what is intended it would need to be brought back to the Planning Board to be looked at. It was confirmed that this was for Zegouros personally and not a business. Zegouros confirmed that he understood that anything that was put on this property would need to come before the Planning Board for site plan review.

Karen confirmed with regard to drainage the public works director said it should be addressed by owner. Jean said that the drainage issues are the ditching and culverts to be checked by the public works director. Debby Parks confirmed that this would be addressed as an entrance permit which would be checked by the Public Works Director and when it is put in it will go through the normal channels.

Karen noted that the location of the entrance was different from the previous location submitted. Jean’s understanding was that it was moved down quite a bit further from the intersection. Zegouros confirmed that it was first put in arbitrarily without a lot of forethought for the actual location. After review it was moved to the end of the property line away from any potential drainage issues. It is not put on the plan at this time, but will be added as an amendment at a later date if and when he needs it. Karen stated that the Planning Board could not sign the plan without the driveway being on the plan. Zegouros said if it is approved tonight he would bring back a new Mylar showing the location to be signed by the Planning Board. The new Mylar would add the curb cut on the Mayall Road where it is agreed upon by the Planning Board.

Janet asked if the driveway was different from the other roadway going into the subdivision. Jean confirmed that this is a driveway and not a road. Zegouros further clarified that this was a driveway and not a road.

Jean asked if everyone on the Board had seen the note signed by Rosemary in lieu of a performance bond or letter of credit. Karen asked if there is no requirement of a performance bond because the road is done the way it is required to be. Jean stated that the required improvements for the road and the fire pond will be done to the plan prior to the selling of the two lots. Jean asked for votes.

Motion: To approve in lieu of the performance guarantee that the improvements to the road and the fire pond be completed on the Plan prior to the sale of the lots as approved by the Town Manager, and on the condition that the Plan be changed to reflect the driveway entrance on Mayall Road. Karen, second Ruth. 6-0

Zegouros’ original Mylar was returned to him for corrections. Jean gave Debby Parks the Fire Pond Easement presented by Zegouros to be signed by the Town.

Other Business

  • Jean requested other business for the Planning Board. Sue made a comment about using a checklist according to the Ordinances mentioned at the last meeting. Jean said that this is a procedure that has been followed by the New Gloucester Planning Board for some time. This has been filled out by the Town Planner previously. Debby said she will have checklists for the next meeting.
  • Jean said the Planning Board has been invited to a meeting by the Shakers on April 27, 2006 at 7:00 p.m. at the Shaker Library to discuss what the Shakers are doing with their land. The Zoning Committee is attending this meeting in lieu of their regularly scheduled meeting.
  • The Public Hearing for Amendments to the Ordinance was opened at 7:55 p.m. Beginning with the Amendment for Fire Protection there were no comments.

Regarding Proposed Changes to the Zoning Ordinance Regarding Accessory Apartments Roger Levasseur addressed the Board to ask about the definition of “gross floor area” and what that includes. Sue said that this is living space. He asked what the starting point would be for the 40% or 800 square feet of the single family structure. Debby Parks said this includes the actual, everyday living area, not to include attics, porches or garages. Debby said that “habitable area” may be more descriptive. Jean said there are other conditions that need to be considered as well as square footage, such as “the accessory apartment . . . shall not detract from the single-family appearance of the principal structure.”

Jeff Hamilton addressed the Board concerning the Accessory Apartment proposed changes, first an explanation of the change from “in-law” to “accessory” apartments. Jean said that the tenants do not need to be family members. Hamilton then asked if the apartment could be the maximum size of 800 square feet if the single family home was less than 2000 square feet. Debby explained that the change was written that the “accessory apartment shall be a maximum of 40% of the gross floor area of the single family structure, but no greater than 800 square feet.” Discussion continued about the definition of “gross floor area.” Jean explained that this was more than the present conditions of 540 square foot in-law apartment for family members only. Hamilton stressed that the new changes prohibit smaller homes from adding on useable accessory apartments. Sue stated that this formula was the only way to prohibit the apartment from becoming larger than the principal residence. Debby said the idea was not to create a duplex; it was to create an accessory apartment to a principal residence. Hamilton said the smaller homes in New Gloucester would not be able to build adequate accessory apartments with the new formula.

Karen agreed that unfortunately some smaller homes will now be limited to an accessory apartment less than what was previously acceptable, which was 540 square feet. Debby stated that the need for the guidelines is to allow an accessory apartment to bend space standards by putting two living units on a two acre minimum space. There is a need for a base or a limit such as these new proposed changes and they have been determined by the Zoning Board and the others who have created this change.

Ellie Fellers addressed the Board to clarify again that the presently acceptable 540 square foot in-law apartment would now be abolished. She calculated the following primary residence sizes and their acceptable accessory apartment sizes allowed with the new changes: 1000 square feet living space allows a 400 square foot apartment; 1200 square feet living space allows a 480 square foot apartment; 1500 square feet living space allows 600 square foot apartment; and the threshold being 2000 square feet living space allows 800 square foot apartment. She also asked for confirmation that the tenant could now be related or not related. This was confirmed. Finally Ellie asked for confirmation under Section 5.1.1.F that the new provisions allow an accessory apartment to be built attached to the garage or barn even if the garage or barn was not attached to the house. Jean confirmed that this was how it was written.

Karen asked where the public’s comments go from this point. Jean said she will prepare a memo to present to the Selectmen with notes of these comments. Jean said the point of the Accessory Apartments was to provide affordable housing.

Jean closed the Public Hearing at 8:20 p.m.

Jean asked for comments from the Planning Board and stated she will send a memo to the Selectmen stating concerns from the people at the Public Hearing. The Selectmen’s meeting is March 27th.

Motion: To adjourn the meeting at 8:25 p.m. Karen, second Sue. 6-0.

Minutes prepared by _______________________

Beth Fontaine

Signed and acknowledged by _____________________

Jean Libby, Board Chair

NEW GLOUCESTER PLANNING BOARD

Minutes of February 7, 2006

Members Present: Others Present:

Jean Libby, Chairman Marc A. Levesque

Karen Asselin, Vice Chairman Gary Sacco, Fire Chief

James Isaacson, Town Planner Mark A. Simond

Ruth Waterhouse Rick Valentine

Laurie Brady Ellie Fellers

Sue Robitaille Norm Chamberlain

Janet Smaldon Vinal Zigouras

Matthew Trudel

Debbie Parks

Beth Fontaine

Absent:

Susan Doyle

Motion: To review and approve the Minutes of January 3, 2006 as written.

Ruth, second Karen. 5-1-0. Janet Smaldon abstained due to absence at January 3, 2006 meeting.

Sabbathday Road Commercial Subdivision

James explained that Vinal Zigouras is proposing to subdivide a 22-acre parcel on Sabbathday Road into four commercial lots. It is located in the RC District along the old Route 26 across from Buddy’s Store. There is currently a commercial building on the lot and a new boat storage business is under construction that the Planning Board approved a few months ago. Jean asks if on the road profile on the upper right corner of the plan stating the aggregate sub-base course should be 18”, it currently says 8”. Jean asked Zigouras to correct that on the Plan. Ruth said that she had not seen the deed for the boat storage business. James said that it had been presented as a condition. Jean asked for further questions and she questioned the curb cut on the property. She thought it had been addressed that there would not be another curb cut on this property. Jean asked at this time if the road name, Osway (Oz Drive - corrected 3/7/06), had been submitted for approval. Zigouras said that he thought it had. Regarding the curb cut Zigouras said it was not a curb cut, but that it was for driveway access to the viable piece of property on the Mayall Road. He said this was the only way to access this lot because of the wetland. Karen questioned what they are planning on for that piece of property. Zigouras said at this time there is nothing planned, but perhaps a shed or small garage would be built at some point and they need to be able to access it. Karen said the first time this plan was presented this curb cut was not on the plan. She asked what changed. Zigouras said that in looking at the plan they realized there was no access to this piece of property. James explained briefly the DEP’s standards for crossing a wetland. James said the issue was whether they balance the effect on the wetland versus what the traffic impact would be with the curb cut. Jean said if she was going to bend at all she would go to Public Works for review of what is going on on Mayall Road. Karen agreed with that. Zigouras said it is about 300 feet from Mayall intersection. Jean asked for confirmation that there is no curb cut now. Karen agreed that he may need Public Works approval.

Discussion continued regarding a fire pond or storage tanks. Jean said there are no standards in the Ordinance at this time for storage tanks. She cannot bend the rules and set a precedent by approving the tanks for this project. Jean states there are too many questions without standards for the tanks, such as who is responsible for them and who maintains them. Jean asked Gary Sacco what he feels about them. Zigouras said he spoke with James and the Fire Chief about this issue. Zigouras said Sacco said either 30,000 gallon tanks could be used or a 120,000 gallon pond. Sacco said he did meet with him and they had originally talked about cisterns. However, going by the Ordinance tonight Sacco said the Board would have to say that Zigouras needs to build the fire pond because the paper they have says that the soils will hold water. Jean said the location of the fire pond that was offered was terrible unless Zigouras wants to build a road. The pond has to be accessible for the fire trucks. Karen asked if they could go back to Dick Sweet for a new location for the fire pond. Jean said either that or peer review. Jean repeated that there are no standards for the tanks, size, materials, etc. Discussion was raised by Sue Robitaille about value of something, such as the tanks, being better than nothing if a fire pond could not be put in. Karen agreed with Jean that because of no standards or guidance we could not dictate what should be put in. James said he thinks what should be done because of the limitations of the Ordinance, for this instance we should not consider the tanks, but strongly reconsider the pond in a different location. James noted that a location that has potential is at the end of the road as shown on the plan where the culvert crosses the road, there is a low area on Lot No. 4. To ensure that it holds water the Board could require a lining of clay, with a culvert for drainage. James feels that is a feasible option that should be explored. Zigouras agreed that they would look at it, although he feels the Board is making a mistake. Jean agreed, but stated the Ordinance needs to be changed and will be changed in May if he wants to wait. Zigouras asked if the Board had issue with anything else.

Jean said underground utilities are already over ground, but the Board will need a written request for a waiver. They also need a waiver for the monuments unless they want to put in stone monuments. The road name needs to be submitted. It was suggested that Zigouras call Debbie Parks, the Code Enforcement Officer. The road name needs to go before Code Enforcement Officer, 911 and the Selectmen. A buffer is needed for the chicken barns, Zigouras asked if that is an issue for site plan review and Jean said yes. We do need two waivers in writing for stone monuments and underground utilities. Zigouras said he will bring them when he comes back regarding fire pond. Decision was made to wait and vote at next meeting when Zigouras will bring information on fire pond, waivers for underground utilities and monuments, road name approval, plan corrected as mentioned 8” should read 18”, and there has to be a section on the plan that says “notes and conditions.”

Bailey Farm Minor Subdivision

James explained that Wade Trudel is proposing to subdivide a 4-acre parcel into two lots on Sabbathday Road. This was originally brought to the Board last year by Doug McIntey (McAtee – corrected 3/7/06), Old Bailey Farm Property next to Buddy’s Store. The old farmhouse in middle was sold and that left two pieces, one on each side of the farmhouse, but it is still considered one lot. In order to split one from the other, it requires subdivision approval because it is 3 lots in a five year period. That is why they are here. Planning Board had a net acreage calculation done under previous application. That shows not enough acreage for 3 house lots on what was 6 acres. They do have enough acreage for the two homes that are there and a commercial lot. That is what they are proposing because a commercial lot can go down to one acre. Matthew Trudel, Wade Trudel’s son, spoke and said before too much work is done they want to make sure it is a viable lot, they have not decided what they will do with the lot. Jean asked if they had talked with Public Works about a curb cut for commercial business. Trudel said there is a driveway. It is a two acre lot, but because of wetness of the property it can only be considered one acre. There is limited use of the lot due to wetness. Something small with low impact on traffic would be suitable. Approval of a subdivision is being requested at this time. Someone will need to return once a use is decided. Jean asked Trudel how they intend to cross the wetland. Trudel said it will be through DEP, but he believes it will be a permanent body of water. Jean advised Trudel to have Kevin look at the curb cut off 26, because of traffic and exiting and the Mayall Road there. Karen said that because the State had reviewed this spot she feels it should be deferred to their review. James suggested the Planning Board should do another site walk because it had been some time since the last site walk. Jean asked if abutters were notified. Trudel said yes. Site walk was scheduled for Saturday, February 11 at 9:00 a.m. This will need to be put on the website. Discussion of a fire pond. Either need one or letter that says the soils will not support one. James said the Ordinance says the developer shall construct fire ponds, but does not say where, it says it has to be in the vicinity. It was suggested that Trudel talk with Vinal Zigouras to work together to use the same fire pond as the properties are across the street from one another.

Simond Trucking Site Plan Review

Rick Valentine from Survey Works spoke representing Mark Simond who was also present and Norm Chamberlain. To clarify confusion in name of project new handouts were prepared and passed out to the Board members. The only change in the packet was the name change. James explained that Mark Simond is proposing to operate a trucking service facility on Route 122 near the Poland town line on Ricker Road in the RB2 zoning district. He has actually been at this location for a while and has finally submitted his application for approval. It is proposed to be a large maintenance facility with office and gravel area surrounding it, along with some paved surface. Karen questioned the building size as there are a couple of different references to the size. Valentine explained the building detail was just a proposal of what they were looking at and since that time they have looked at other options. The 7490 square feet includes the office space on the side.

Valentine offered a brief summary. He said Simonds was operating a trucking facility at another location in New Gloucester when they were unexpectedly asked to move. The approximately 42 acres on Route 122 was purchased and they gained a MDOT entrance permit. There were 3 acres of trees cleared, they put in 1-1/2 acres of gravel and started moving the trailers in there. Simonds met with Debbie Parks who informed him of a site review and what was needed to bring it into compliance. After that they decided on some of the project area. They proposed to break about 8 acres out of the 42 acres - 3 acres cleared of trees and pave approximately ½ acre around the building, with the remaining 1-1/2 acres being gravel. He currently owns about 30 trailers and about 15 trucks. At any one time there will only be about 15 trailers at the site and 7 trucks that will be entering and leaving per day, they will not all be at the site at the same time. There will be approximately 4-6 employees that will be in the structure, which is a one story, 3 bay garage with office area which as stated before is about 7400 square feet. No waste product will be stored for any length of time. A dumpster will be picked up every two weeks. Waste oil will be stored inside in 55 gallon drums and when they are full Clean Harbors will come in and pick them up. Jean asked for a copy of the contract that this will be done. Valentine said they are proposing to use a waste oil furnace. Jean said we will need to have this submitted in writing. Valentine continued saying any tires of no value will be picked up by a company out of Norridgewock they are currently using on as needed basis or every two weeks. There are two storage trailers that are dedicated for the purpose of storing tires. No tires will be stored externally. Jean asked about storing diesel on the premises. Valentine said they get that offsite. He explained this is not a trucking terminal. The only service to the trucks is basic maintenance. Jean asked about washing. Valentine said there is no washing on the site, that is was done offsite. Karen asked what basic servicing entails, and if it would just be oil changes. No response to this question. Valentine said at this time they are open for questions.

Karen asked if there was anything else that would be stored out there, such as other vehicles, other than the trailers themselves. Valentine said there may be employee vehicles, but not overnight residential vehicles, unless they are part of the business such as a small pick-up. Typically there are two trucks as parts vehicles that will be stored on the back side of the property. Jean asked if they would be leaking fluids and Valentine said no. Karen asked if the lighting in the area would be exterior lighting or a sign with lighting. Valentine said no signs were proposed and on the proposed site plan there is a symbol for lights on the corners of the buildings which would be low profile lighting pointed down to illuminate the yard. Jean asked if the trucks were coming and going all night. Valentine said no, only when they return from their trip. Jean asked if trucks would be left idling all night. Valentine said that it is not necessary to leave any trucks running all night, unless in an emergency situation. Jean asked for clarification that they would only be repairing their own vehicles. Valentine said if this was a condition that would be okay, but they do not want to restrict future business. Jean proposed a site walk.

Jean asked for height of building and said it needs to be less than 35 feet. She asked Gary Sacco if the State Fire Marshall needs to approve this sized building. Sacco said he is going to make a call tomorrow to get a clarification on this and could not say definitely tonight. Sacco did say they need to know the use of the building. In terms of the style of the building Jean said they have no problem with style of building, but the Ordinance says it cannot be over 35 feet. Norm Chamberlain said it will be about 27 feet.

Janet asked for clarification of services of business. Valentine said they go to businesses, such as Poland Springs, with their empty trucks and have them filled, make the deliveries and return to the business empty. Jean asked if there are floor drains and Valentine said no. Jean asked Valentine to send their Erosion and Sediment Control off to Cumberland County Soil. Jean said she noticed on one of the plans that recording data says Androscoggin County; it should be changed to Cumberland County. Jean said they need to notify the abutters and the Town of Poland because they are on the town line. Valentine said they have not at this point. Jean said they need to put “Notes and Conditions” on the plan, not just “Notes.”

Norm Chamberlain spoke on stormwater and soil erosion control. This project has over one acre of new and pervious so needs to go to the State for a Stormwater Permit under the new rules. He went on to explain the new rules. He said they will have an infiltration basin in a corner of the gravel area. He felt because of this permit they would not need to go to Cumberland County Soil. Jean agreed as long as there was a peer review of some kind. Jean planned a site visit for Saturday, February 11th at 9:30-9:45 a.m.

Jean again addressed storage of tires per the application section “Description of raw furnished waste materials to be stored outside the buildings and any stored in the fields.” She wants to make sure we address it now so there is no question. Jean said she needs to see the site before addressing the subject of buffer or hours of operation. This is a business going into a residential so she needs to see how close the residences are on the site walk. Need to make sure we are protecting water quality. Service to own vehicles could affect water quality if something was dropped or spilled by mistake. Jean asked Sacco if they should look at anything in regard to Fire Department on the site walk. Jean explained that no decisions are made on the site walk; they take notes regarding concerns that will be addressed at next meeting.

In review: Jean wants something in writing about how oil is stored and disposed of. Also regarding tire storage she needs an estimate in writing of what will be on site at any one time, for example 25 tires or 100. Jean’s understanding is that there are no set hours of operation, no floor drains, height is less than 35 feet, there will be low profile lighting, and no truck washing. Jean said they need to contact Fire Marshall for what is required by Fire Department. She asked if there would be any water sitting overnight (if there would be any undelivered Poland Spring water sitting overnight – corrected 3/6/06). Simonds said only on an exception basis, if a delivery was cancelled. Jean asked if they were hauling gasoline or oil. Simonds said there was no hazmat being handled. Jean said when they are ready to go back to the Planning Board they should contact Debbie Parks, the Code Enforcement Officer, and arrange to be put on the agenda.

Long Range Facilities Plan

Jean explained that Steve Libby has drafted a Long Range Facilities Plan for all town-owned facilities and has asked for comments from the Planning Board. She stressed that the Plan is a draft at this point. It is a starting point for the Selectmen. She has reviewed it and based on Planning Board she has made the following comments will go through them so suggestions from the Board for additions or deletions can be made.

Lewiston Road Land – this location will help meet the long range plan of the Town of New Gloucester. First the construction of a central Fire Rescue Station, then add Public Works Dept. and maybe if possible add the municipal buildings. This parcel was already zoned RB1 and with careful planning these departments could be placed on a lot without compromising the abutting property. Entering and exiting the property on Route 202, 4 and 100 will need to be planned with the DOT. Other communities have fire rescue departments located on arterial highways such as Route 302 and 26. Jean asked for additions.

Fire Station/Rescue – space needs make it necessary to construct a new Fire/Rescue. The location on the Lewiston Road will make it possible for all Fire/Rescue equipment to be in one location and still provide access to all locations in New Gloucester. This will help the Fire/Rescue Department with their service to the citizens. Good planning of this facility to address the current needs of the NG residents with the ability to expand as NG continues to grow is very important. Jean asked for additions.

Public Works – present location is at full capacity. They have met maximum 30% impervious cover section of the NG Ordinance and the members of the capital improvement committee are well aware the present building needs major repairs and improvement. Moving this to the new Lewiston Road location could address two issues: one could be financial, two departments could combine items such as fuel stations and wash bays; second would allow present public works area in Upper Gloucester to be used for something that better fits the Village area. Members that are on the Zoning Committee have been working on the Upper Village plan for 2 plus years. Moving Public Works from this area would improve the area making it easier and safer to create a village area. Good planning on a new lot is a must. The placements of these 2 facilities must be planned so both departments can be functional and safe. The lot appears to be large enough for the Town to place both of these facilities on the site and still have room for municipal offices in the future if that should become the desire of the citizens and allowed by the State.

Town Hall Expansion – the taxpayers of NG voted a number of years ago to continue to upgrade the Town Hall. The complex is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and is in the NG Historic Recess Overlay District. The purpose of this section of the Zoning Ordinance is to protect and enhance our historic resources. If the building can be renovated by expanding the upstairs for additional office space while still preserving the structure’s historic value it makes financial sense and continues the use for which this structure was designed. It would give the town additional room and provide a number of additional years before the citizens would again decide if this structure and site is still the best place for municipal offices. The town hall parking he presented would be a great improvement and much safer. The lower fire station would add more space than we now have for a meeting house if designed with partitions that would slide open or close, so rooms could be made larger when needed for public hearings and other meetings. Renovating this building would be a good addition to the Town complex. The Meeting House and the old fire station really have nothing to do with us, except turning it over to the Historic Society, that’s a vote of the Town. They would not own it but they would be able to use it.

Karen asked if the rest of it would come before the Board as a site plan review. Jean said the Town Hall renovation upstairs she was not sure of, unless you did something to the outside of the building and that would be up to the Code Enforcement Officer. The other items would all be for Planning Board review.

Water for Fire Protection – This is an item that the Planning Board and Zoning Committee are working on at this time to improve the zoning regulations. THE TOWN NEEDS A PLAN.

Library – from info received from the Capital Improvements Committee the Library Trustees are already trying to plan ahead for expansion.

Transfer Station - nothing to review.

Recreation Facilities including Fairgrounds – unless the Town can find a way to secure this site from vandalism it may not be in the best interest of taxpayers to continue this site for recreation. The Town may have to look to another site for ball fields and then consider what the best plan is for the reuse of the Rowe station site. It is zoned rural residential and includes wetlands so would not be a great location for public works. In regard to the Fairgrounds - to continue to implement the long range plan they are already working on.

Jean asked for any comments or additions from Board members. She stated they need to send their comments on to the Selectmen soon. It was agreed they should be sent. James stated he had already given the Selectmen his comments.

Other Business

Signing of Schran Minor Subdivision Plan.

Jean announced the Local Planning Boards and Boards of Appeals workshop, on March 8, 2006 in Lewiston. The workshop is designed as a basic introduction to various legal rules governing decisions made by Planning Boards and Land Use Appeal Boards. If anyone from the Planning Board would like to go the Town has money for it. Arrangements should be made with Debbie Parks.

Janet asked James to review the meeting at Pineland. James said there were a lot of comments and insight on Upper Village, Lower Village, Route 26 and Route 100, these were the four areas that they focused on. There is a follow-up meeting on the 16th. Discussion will be policy issues as opposed to geographic areas.

Karen mentioned to Debbie Parks that there had been a discussion about fire ponds earlier in the evening. Someone had been led to believe there was an option for use of tanks. Karen said she would ask Debbie and/or the new Town Planner not to offer any options to fire ponds because at this time there are no other options.

Jean thanked James for his service as Town Planner. She said he has done a very good job, always being fair and supportive, and he will be missed. She said that James has had a tremendous working relationship with the people.

Motion: To adjourn the meeting at 9:15 p.m. Ruth, second Karen. 6-0.

Minutes prepared by _______________________

Beth Fontaine

Signed and acknowledged by _____________________

Jean Libby, Board Chair

title: January 3, 2006
html:
NEW GLOUCESTER PLANNING BOARD

Minutes of January 3, 2006

Members Present: Others Present:

Jean Libby, Chairman Stephen Schran

Karen Asselin, Vice Chairman Gary Sacco, Fire Chief

James Isaacson, Town Planner Chris Branch

Ruth Waterhouse Alfred M. Berquist

Laurie Brady Ellie Fellers

Tim Joy

Beth Fontaine

Absent:

Susan Doyle (excused)

Sue Robitaille (excused)

Janet Smaldon

Motion: To review and approve the Minutes of December 6, 2005 as written.

Ruth, second Karen. 4-0.

Public Hearing – Schran Minor Subdivision Amendment

James explained that Stephen Schran is proposing to subdivide one lot out of his parcel in the Schran Minor Subdivision on Romans Road. Romans Road will be extended about 250 feet to provide access to this lot. Mr. Schran brought in a revised plan. Jean reviewed the plan before the public hearing was commenced. She was concerned that the new plan does not show the corrected curve in the road. Schran said he did not think it was specified as necessary. Karen said it was specified, but perhaps not clear enough. James said the Board could require by condition that the road be widened to accommodate a fire truck maneuvering around the corner. Karen asked if this would be without showing it on the plan. James said the condition would have to be placed in writing on the plan, but it would not require an additional meeting. Jean asked Gary Sacco to comment. Sacco said they had taken an engine to the road and said as long as they can make the swing it does not matter where it is widened. Sacco looked at the plan and clarified where it needs to be widened, he said that when they went down with the engine he showed Schran how much was needed to make the swing. Sacco agreed that to the left of Schran’s home would be fine. Jean agreed we do not need another meeting, but wants to be clear on whether the widening should be on the plan in the comments or shown on the drawing. Karen said it was not unclear at the last meeting that it needed to be on the drawing, but she could live with it in writing. Ruth prefers it be on the drawing because she is not sure the notes and conditions are looked at as carefully as the drawing.

Jean opened the Public Hearing at 7:45 p.m. and asked for comments. Al Berquist of 10 Cottage Lane wanted clarification of what Schran was planning on building. Being from out of state Berquist was concerned the subdivision could be large. Jean explained the subdivision had already been approved in 1998 and now it was a matter of an oversized lot being divided for one more house lot. Schran said there is nothing planned for the lot at this time. Berquist wanted assurance that a commercial business would not be built on this site and Jean confirmed that would not be possible. Jean asked for any other comments, being none Jean closed the public hearing at 7:49 p.m.

Referring back to the earlier discussion, Jean confirmed that there was a motion at the December 6, 2005 meeting as follows: “To deem application complete subject to receipt of a road plan and profile on the plan including the location of the turnaround and showing the widening. Karen, second Ruth. 6-0.” Karen said that since we made a motion at the last meeting we do not need to go back on that. She apologized if it was not clear to Mr. Schran what was needed.

Motion: To approve it subject to receipt of a revised plan showing the widening of the road on the diagram, the angles and all the other related material to that, based on the findings of fact. Karen, Ruth second 4-0.

Jean told Schran to bring the revised plan into James and as long as James approves it, he is all set.

Tobey Pines Major Subdivision

James explained that Robert Hale is proposing to subdivide 81.71 acres of land off Tobey Road into 12 lots in the Farm & Forest District. A site walk was done in the summer and a fire pond has been constructed. The fire pond was flow tested by Fire Chief Sacco. Jean asked for comments from the Board before proceeding. Karen asked what had changed and Jean said Lot 1. Karen asked in what way Lot 1 was new. Chris Branch of Technical Services Inc. explained Lot 1 was not there before and showed the changes to the plan involving Lot 1. He showed the layout of the lots and the remaining property that is wetland and the logging area. Jean asked Sacco to talk about the fire pond. Sacco said he had been up 2 or 3 times to review it with James and recently hooked the fire pond to a hydrant and flow tested it. Although there was ice there they could move substantial water. Also it is close to a bog so hopefully it will regenerate itself. Jean asked if there was going to be an easement and Sacco said that he hoped that is what the Board intended to request. Sacco said the pond worked out very nice. Branch said the submitted plan shows a note in the area where the fire pond is and that the easement note indicates “a pond easement 0.39 acres.” There will be an easement included on the subdivision plan for the next round of approvals. Jean asked for clarification of the small roads at top of plan, Branch explained they are logging roads used for logging and by ATV’s. Karen asked for clarification of a discussion at time of the site walk where the road connects with Bald Hill. Tim Joy explained the area at the foot of Bald Hill and that it has two bogs and intersects with other property owners. Branch said we can take a look at it. He felt if it was a private road then ATV’s would not be allowed, but they would take a look at relocating trails.

Jean asked if they have notified abutters. Branch said they have not at this time. Jean said that is the next step. Also necessary would be a road maintenance agreement as well as home association agreement. Karen said if there is no common open space with restrictions then there may not be a necessity for a home association agreement. Jean said a submission for a preliminary plan is needed. She asked if the road has a name. Branch said it does not at this time. Jean said the name has to be approved by the 911 committee, the Code Enforcement Officer and also Town Selectmen. Name needs to be given to James so he can see that it goes through the appropriate people. They need to have all of the submissions stated in Article 7.1 Preliminary Plan for Major Subdivisions. Branch said fine, we will do that. Branch said that basically they were here tonight to get direction from Planning Board based on what we heard at the onsite for a traditional subdivision. Being here with standard subdivision schematic to make sure we are heading in right direction before we go for preliminary approval. Also to let you know that we have worked with the Fire Chief and it is Branch’s understanding that Mr. Hale has been in contact with the Public Works with regard to the road. Jean said when they are doing the submittals they need to take in consideration they are in the Groundwater Protection Overlay District. Karen said please refresh her if the road is private and if there is an existing Road Maintenance Agreement. Branch said that part of the road would have to be included as part of the Road Maintenance Agreement. It is a deeded right of access. Jean said there is a right of way across two different property owners. Ruth said there are no conditions with the notes. Branch said they will be included when we submit preliminary subdivision plan. Jean said you need to show building envelopes on these and Branch agreed they will. James said we also have setbacks from wetland areas basically 100’ but the Board can reduce that. James noted Lot 2 and Lot 3 have a few spots of wetlands scattered and that needed to be taken into consideration. James asked if DEP had any concerns. Branch said as far as he knows DEP has no jurisdiction in this project. Branch’s understanding is that 14-15 lots is when you need to go to site plan review. James agreed that it is 15 lots. If you exceed 15 lots in the future then the entire subdivision is subject to DEP site plan review. Jean asked if Mr. Hale is aware of that and Branch said he was.

Jean asked if any other questions. Jean repeated that they have to notify abutters and complete section 7 of subdivision regs to start with. Branch said yes, the next submittal the Board receives will be bigger than this one. Jean said if we have had snowmobilers using this area the applicant needs to let them know. Branch said that Mr. Hale has been cooperative with the folks in the area about snowmobile and ATV use. We will discuss what is going on with the subdivision lots. Branch asked if there is a snowmobile club in New Gloucester that they can contact. Jean said there was. Other than seeing how the houses will fit around the wetlands Jean does not have any problem with this one. Ruth wants to make sure there is a deed to the right-of-way.

Jean said if there are any questions about the submission to call James. The fire issue part has been taken care of. The ordinance says to have underground utilities. If it remains a private road there is a section of the ordinance that needs to be on every plan. It is section 8.1(e) as follows: “All roads in the subdivision shall remain private roads to be maintained by the developers or lot owners and shall not be accepted or maintained by the Town.” That has to be on the plan in writing.

Other Business

Karen asked if there was any movement on a fire committee. Jean said the committee is Jean, Janet, James, and Gary. Jean suggested the meetings be at James’ office on Monday nights at 6:00 p.m., not necessarily every Monday. Jean asked if James had done the backup on that and he said he will go to Rosie to get it. Karen offered to be part of the committee.

Ruth and Jean went to the Pineland meeting with James and found it very interesting. Jean felt good with what came out of the meeting.

Jean said they had received a copy of a letter from Karen Strout of Town of Raymond to Rosemary Kulow, New Gloucester Town Clerk, to advise that Pat Cayer of Land Services Inc. is presenting an application for mineral extraction at property abutting land in Gray, Notched Pond (James said also New Gloucester) at the January 11, 2006 Planning Board Meeting. This would be a public hearing. Jean said it is in our Groundwater Protection Overlay if it is abutting us. Jean said they need to be sure we are protected. James said our Ordinance cannot dictate this. Jean asked James if they could supply us with the minutes of the meeting as it is not in our Town. Karen wanted to know if someone from Planning Board should be at the hearing. James feels a copy of the minutes will be sufficient. He also said we could send some comments in writing that could be read into the record.

James said we will be signing Gabriel Woods Subdivision Plan after tonight’s meeting.

Motion: To adjourn the meeting at 8:25 p.m. Karen, second Ruth. 4-0.

Minutes prepared by _______________________

Beth Fontaine

Signed and acknowledged by _____________________

Jean Libby, Board Chair

title: December 6, 2005
html:
NEW GLOUCESTER PLANNING BOARD

Minutes of December 6, 2005

Members Present: Others Present:

Jean Libby, Chairman Stephen Schran

Karen Asselin, Vice Chairman Beth Fontaine

James Isaacson, Town Planner

Ruth Waterhouse

Janet Smaldon

Sue Robitaille

Laurie Brady

Absent:

Susan Doyle (excused)

James started the meeting by introducing Beth Fontaine who will be the new minute taker at the Planning Board meetings.

Motion: To approve the Minutes of November 16, 2005 as written with the following 3 corrections:

(1) Correct spelling of Laurie Brady’s first name from Lori to Laurie.

(2) Correct 18” to 18’ plow width; and

(3) Correct last motion approved 50-0 needs to be corrected to 5-0.

Ruth, second Janet. 6-0.

Schran Minor Subdivision Amendment

Stephen Schran introduced himself. James said that Gary Sacco, New Gloucester Fire Chief, and Stephen Schran had met to discuss the road issue. Mr. Schran said the Fire Chief came and basically looked over the entire road and said that what was needed was to widen the road by 3 to 4 feet the section as you come around and face Schran’s home. Sacco said it needed to be wide enough for the fire truck to turn around. Karen asked if the curve could be straightened out and Schran said it would be. Schran stated Sacco felt it would be wide enough to turn the truck around. Karen asked about a turnaround. Schran said he mentioned a turnaround, but Sacco did not say anything. James said the first plan showed a turnaround. Jean asked if we would get a corrected plan to show us the corrected road? Schran said he needs to see the surveyor to have the plan changed.

Jean said when the Plan is filed it needs to have on it the section of Ordinance 8.1(e) as follows: “All roads in the subdivision shall remain private roads to be maintained by the developers or lot owners and shall not be accepted or maintained by the Town.” James will let Mr. Schran know exactly what language needs to be on the plan.

Janet wants to see a legitimate turnaround at the end of Lot 1B. There are 4 houses designated now and the potential for more. Discussion continued about the end of the road whether or not it is a private driveway. There were problems addressed that might occur using a driveway as a turnaround. Two examples stated were future owners may not agree to the turnaround for emergency vehicles; or a car may be parked in the driveway when it is necessary for an emergency vehicle to turn around.

James could not think of other subdivisions where driveways came off the hammerhead, but felt it could be done on a private road. James said it was not acceptable on town roads. Karen is leery of setting a precedent by using a private driveway as a turnaround. Ruth said that a school bus may not recognize the driveway as the turnaround. Karen felt other things were being waived and the issue of a turnaround should not be waived. Mr. Schran said he is not opposed to a turnaround, but needs to have his excavator return to plan it.

Motion: To waive: (1) contour lines; (2) the hydrogeologic study; (3) stormwater plan; (4) stone monuments; (5) underground utilities; and (6) the fire pond. Karen, second Janet. 6-0

Janet questioned about the water supply for the well and fire pond with regard to the bedrock issue. Karen agrees with Jean that because of adding only one home it is not the issue it would be if it were a 20 lot subdivision. Discussion regarding drilling depths for wells varying from one spot to another. Discussion continued of the profile needing to be put on the plan and the language of Section 8.1(e) needing to be on the plan. Schran asked if it was possible for the Fire Chief to return to suggest what is going to work for the fire trucks. Jean said that it was the Planning Board’s decision to where the turnaround will be, but the Fire Chief could see how the trucks would use it.

Motion: To require change for turnaround from private driveway to be located at the end of the private road between Lot 1A and 1B, as either a “T” or a “hammerhead.” Karen, second Janet. 6-0.

Motion: To deem application complete subject to receipt of a road plan and profile on the plan including the location of the turnaround and showing the widening. Karen, second Ruth. 6-0

Karen mentioned that the neighbors need to be apprised of the situation. Mr. Schran said a letter had been sent.

Motion: Move to schedule a public hearing on January 3, 2006, at 7:30 p.m. Karen, second Janet. 6-0.

Jean asked Mr. Schran to bring the updated plan with him to the next meeting.

Other Business

December 20, 2005 meeting cancelled due to Special Town Meeting. Topics that affect the Planning Board at that meeting include Fire Station engineering and the purchase of land for the new municipal building.

Thursday, December 8, 2005 at 7:00 p.m., meeting at Pineland Conference Center. This is a Business and Economic Development study that the Town is holding. It will be a visioning session. All business owners in town are invited to discuss the future of the town.

Sue Robitaille brought up a discussion of sprinklers and fire ponds. Jean agrees with fire sprinklers, but not that they should be mandatory for homeowners. Laurie stated she felt a subcommittee should be formed to work on fire protection. Janet felt it should be a priority.

Jean felt that there should be a warning to developers that the Planning Board has the right for peer review.

Jean said it should be added to the application for developers that Section 8.1(e) is required to be on the plan, so there is no question in the town that a plan showing a private road is required to have this.

Motion: To adjourn the meeting at 8:20 p.m. Jean, second Karen. 6-0.

Minutes prepared by _______________________

Beth Fontaine

Signed and acknowledged by _____________________

Jean Libby, Board Chair

title: November 15, 2005
html:
NEW GLOUCESTER PLANNING BOARD

Minutes of November 15, 2005

Members Present Others Present

Jean Libby, Chairman William Gabriel

Karen Asselin, Vice Chairman Mr. and Mrs. Stephen Schran

James Isaacson, Town Planner Grace Bragdon

Ruth Waterhouse Debbie Parks, CEO

Janet Smaldon Gary Sacco, Fire Chief

Sue Robitaille

Absent:

Lori Brady and Susan Doyle (both excused)

Motion: to approve the Minutes of November 1, 2005 as written. Ruth, second Karen. 5-0-0.

Gabriel Woods Subdivision

James gave a brief summary of the project. A public hearing was opened at 7:35. There were no comments received from the audience and the hearing was closed at 7:36.

Karen expressed a concern with the width of the existing road. James and the code enforcement officer have talked with the contractor for the road and he is going to certify in writing that the road was built to private road standards. Janet said she was concerned about the precedent being set by the road having two different surfaces. Jean commented that if the entire road was left as gravel it would be fine so the paved surface should not make a difference. Jean also stated that a turnaround was needed for emergency vehicles to use. The applicant would like to put the turnaround at the end of the area to be subdivided and leave the rest of the road as his private driveway. Karen asked about the plowing of the road and the applicant suggested putting some language in the association agreement requiring that the road be plowed 18 feet wide.

Motion: to waive the need for a fire pond based on a letter stating that the soils would not support it, and to waive underground utilities, stone monuments and contour lines. Karen, second Susan R. 5-0-0.

Motion: to deem the application complete. Karen, second Janet R. 5-0-0.

Motion: to approve the application subject to the following conditions:

1) a “T” or “L” turnaround be built at the end of the area to be developed

2) language being added to the association agreement requiring an 18” plow width for the road

3) a phosphorus analysis being completed and any recommendations of the analysis to be followed

4) add the request for the waiver of the fire pond to the plan

5) access to lot 1 must come off from Gabriel Woods Road

6) monumentation to be added to the plan

Karen, second Janet. 5-0-0.

Schran Minor Subdivision Amendment

James summarized that the applicant is proposing to add 1 additional lot to his subdivision on Romans Road. This will be the third lot in the subdivision and the 4th lot on the road. Jean asked about the septic design and stated that that information, as well as the soil test logs needs to be submitted. Jean also indicated that there were issues with the road due to the sharp corners and no turnaround for emergency vehicles. The fire chief stated that emergency vehicles could probably only reach the first house on the road. Jean also stated that we needed something from a well driller stating that there was adequate water in the area. The issue of adequate water was questioned at the public hearing for the original subdivision. Finally, Jean stated that we needed a fire pond or a letter stating that the soils could not support a pond.

Bragdon Home Site Plan Review

Janet stated that the site plan provided for the home was confusing and difficult to follow. Debbie Parks, the Town CEO, explained that this is an existing, non-conforming lot. The placement of the new lot will bring it into compliance with the required setbacks. She and James have visited the site and see no issues with the proposal.

Motion: to review the request under expedited review. Ruth, Karen. 5-0-0

Motion: to approve the request as presented. Karen, Ruth. 5-0-0.

Other Business

Karen asked about the changes that were proposed to the section in the ordinance on fire protection. Jean stated that the Zoning Committee voted down the changes and that it was not likely to proceed for some time due to some concerns about the sprinkler provision and the provision requiring the fire protection to be in place prior to home occupancy permits being granted. Karen stated that she would like to still try to move forward with something for fire protection because the existing language was difficult to work with. Janet stated that she felt that the fire protection issue should be addressed on a town wide basis, rather than subdivision by subdivision. She recommended asking the Zoning Committee to set up a group to do that. Gary Sacco, the Fire Chief, said he favors moving forward with the changes as slowly as necessary to get them right. He is not in favor of dropping out the provisions on sprinklers because he feels that would put the fire fighters in greater danger. He agreed that it would be good to come up with something on a Town wide basis if possible.

Motion: To adjourn the meeting at 9:00 p.m. Ruth, second Karen. 5-0.

1. Motion: To accept the minutes of October 18, 2005 as read was made by Ruth W., second by Janet S. Board voted to accept 6-0.

2. Gabriel Woods Minor Subdivision-Continued Discussion of proposed 20 acre subdivision on Quarry Road into 4 cluster lots.

Jean asked for discussion regarding site walk at the Gabriel Woods Subdivision held on 10/27/05 at 4:30 pm (rescheduled from original date of 10/25/05 due to inclement weather).

Ruth commented that is is very rocky.

Jean concerned about road width (ordinance requires 18 ft minimum), pavement appears to be approximately 12 ft.

Bill stated that road is actually wider, at least three ft on either side of pavement.

Jean concerned about stability and durability of road since road consists of two materials, pavement and grassy gravel.

Susan asked how it might be effected when needing to be plowed or used by fire/rescue equipment in early Spring.

All parties agreed that Director of Public Works, Kevin, would be asked by James to assess road to determine if it meets town ordinance. If Kevin had any concerns, James would schedule a 3-way meeting.

Bill will be getting the deed corrected (typo "0" ft) as discussed at Planning Board meeting October 18, 2005.

Jean confirmed with Wayne that Sweet Associates packet (received by Planning Board at beginning of this meeting) be added to Gabriel Woods plan.

Wayne will get R. Sweets' "indication of water supply" and contour lines to James by November 7, 2005.

Jean asked if Bill was to be part of the road association and if so, would he not be able to use the off road vehicle present at site walk.

Bill stated he was to be part of the road association (both of his houses). The vehicle he uses is considered a RTV not ATV. It is used for farming not as recreational. It would be acceptable in the existing Covenants, restrictions and Easements.

Jean asked if "open space" portion of subdivision was allowing horses on the trail system, additional verbiage needed to be added to associations by-laws to make provisions regarding erosion prevention.

Janet concerned about fire pond not being in subdivision, as required by town ordinance, even though there is fire pond across road in town of Raymond.

Bill is asking for (but nothing in writing as yet) waiver on fire pond issues as well as underground utilities requirements.

Board unable to act on application until previously discussed information received (i.e. contour lines).

Jean recommended moving forward without completed application.

Motion: To schedule public hearing for Gabriel Woods Minor Subdivision November 15, 2005 at 7:30 PM made by Janet, second Sue R. Board voted to accept 6-0.

3. Schran Subdivision Amendment of proposed 1 lot amendment to Schran Subdivision, originally approved 1998.

Jean asked if neighbor who had concerns of water supply problems at time of original subdivision was experiencing water supply problems or if any one in the immediate area had any problems with water supply.

Steve reported no one having water problems as result of subdivision of 1998.

Jean asked if originally required road work had been completed, i.e. rip rap installed by lower culvert.

Steve reported that it had been done in 1998 as required and road has been maintained each year.

Jean confirmed number of homes currently there.

Jean asked if the road met town ordinance requirement of 18 ft minimum.

Steve said he didn't know.

Janet asked about Notes and Condition referring to "lot 2A to be conveyed"-she couldn't see a lot 2A on the map given in packet.

Steve stated there is no lot 2A, probably a typo.

Ruth asked if lot 1B was going to be divided.

Steve said no. Currently Steve's lot is lot 1, which he proposes to create lot 1B from that.

Sue R. asked what the zoning was in this area.

James confirmed that it is residential.

Jean asked which home owners actually use the road.

Steve said Bartlett, Bouchard, Almy and himself.

Janet asked about waivers' regarding water supply on minutes of meeting on August 15, 2005.

Jean proposed a site walk be scheduled to see road width as well as lot.

Janet asked about fire protection, specifically term used previously as "other tanker". Was there a fire pond waiver given previously?

James stated none given because it was at a time when ordinance was not actively being enforced.

Cottage Woods development nearby does not have a fire pond.

Ruth asked if road was paved.

Steve said no.

Jean asked if there is an association now.

Steve said yes, he gathers about $1k annually.

Site walk scheduled for 8:30 AM Saturday, November 5, 2005 at the Schran Subdivision site off Town Farm Road.

Jean stated that a fire pond can't be put close to "main" road and it can't be waived.

Steve is to asked Sweet Associates if there is a water supply near road.

James reported to Steve that the Sweet Association report portion of proposal was incomplete. It only included front pages of two sided pages.

Steve will recopy and get them to James.

4. Other Business:

Jean reported that amended ordinance proposal was not accepted by Selectmen. They had concerns about how it was written in respect to occupancy, sprinklers, accessory apartments, easements for future fire ponds. Another joint meeting scheduled for November 9, 2005.

Motion: To adjourn was made by Ruth, second Janet. Board voted to accept 6-0.

After meeting adjourned, Planning Board signed Wooded Creek Plan.

title: September 20, 2005
html:
NEW GLOUCESTER PLANNING BOARD

Minutes of September 20, 2005

Members Present Others Present

Jean Libby, Chairman Omer Morin

Karen Asselin, Vice Chairman Steve Morse

James Isaacson, Town Planner

Ruth Waterhouse

Janet Smaldon

Sue Robitaille

Susan Doyle

Absent:

Lori Brady (excused)

Motion: to approve the Minutes of September 6, 2005 with corrections. Ruth, second Janet. 6-0-0.

Sabbathday Road Commercial Subdivision

James informed the Board that the applicant would like us to table further review of the request pending the outcome of ongoing meetings with respect to road paving which could effect the placement of the fire pond.

Morin Sunroom & Deck Additions

James explained that the applicant would like to add a 14’x 20’ sunroom and a 10’x 28’ deck. The sunroom will be in the same area where a deck was previously. The project is in the lake district and on land leased from the shakers, however it is more than 100 feet from the lake so it is not in the shoreland zone. Jean asked how big the lot was. The applicant, Omer Morin, informed her that it was about ½ acre. Jean then asked if all the setbacks will be met and James said that they would be. It was pointed out that Cumberland County Soil and Water District has been to the site and a letter with their recommendations for using Best Management Practices was in the packet. Sue D. asked whether there would be a foundation under the sunroom and was told by the applicant that it would rest on the same posts that were already there for the deck. Sue D. then asked if there were propane tanks being stored under the deck currently. The applicant responded that there were some tanks there, but they would be moved.

Motion: to waive site walk based on the fact that James visited the site and some of the Board members have been there in the past and there did not appear to be any issues. Karen, second Susan R. 6-0-0.

Motion: to deem the application complete. Karen, second Ruth. 6-0-0.

Motion: to waive a public hearing since there did not appear to be any issues and since the applicant stated that he had informed his neighbors of what he was doing. Karen, second Ruth. 6-0-0.

Motion: to approve the application subject to the applicant following the recommendations from Cumberland County Soil and Water for using Best Management Practices for soil erosion control. Karen, second Ruth. 6-0-0.

Morse Boat Storage Site Plan Review

James gave a summary of the project stating that it was to be located on Lot 2 of the pending Sabbathday Road Subdivision. The applicant is proposing to occupy ½ of a 4,800 square foot building and lease out the remainder of the building. Steve Morse, the applicant, provided additional detail, stating that he will not be doing any repairs on site. He intends to store approximately 25 boats or less on the property and he will store his truck and trailer there inside in the winter. Jean asked if he would be storing any oil above 50 gallons and he said that he would not be. Jean then asked about lighting. The applicant said he would like to use motion detector lighting rather than keep a light on all of the time. Jean then asked about the sign. Mr. Morse said he will probably have a sign along with the other businesses out on Sabbathday Road. Jean asked about fire protection and Mr. Morse said that the State Fire Marshall had been contacted and he said that sprinklers were not necessary for the building. James commented that that could change, depending what businesses go in on the other side of the building and Mr. Morse responded that he will have the other tenants take care of those items themselves and they will have to come before the planning board for additional approval. Jean stated that landscaping on the property needs to be addressed and that there should be adequate buffers from neighboring residential areas. Mr. Morse said that he would have no problem leaving a 50’ buffer of trees/fields on the Chandler property side and he commented that an embankment on the Sabbathday Road side would be loamed and seeded as a buffer in that direction. The placement of the septic system on the property was discussed and the applicant stated that it could not be sited specifically until a hill on the property was excavated and the placement of the building was located. Jean asked James to discuss how that could be handled by the Board with the Town Code Enforcement Officer. Jean commented that we will need to receive a 25-year storm water management plan as well as a soil erosion plan. There is already a dug well on the property and the applicant intends to rely on that for water supply. Jean asked about the height of the property and was told it would be about 26 feet high. Karen asked about parking for the proposed tenants. The applicant responded that there should be space for about 3 parking spaces for each tenant and he does not expect more than that to be needed because of the type of businesses that he would like to have in there. Jean said that the issue of the surface where the boats will be stored needs to be addressed. The applicant is proposing grass not gravel. Jean felt that the grass would provide adequate drainage and Karen and Ruth agreed. Jean then asked that the parking area be mapped out on the plan so it is clear what area they intend to use for that purpose.

Wooded Creek Minor Subdivision Waiver Request

James informed the Board that the applicants for the Wooded Creek Minor Subdivision would like to request waivers for the front, rear and side setbacks, for underground utilities and for a reduction in the road width from 24 feet to 18 feet. There was nobody present to represent the applicant. Members of the Board expressed their concern that the applicant was not present to discuss these issues and Jean commented that we also have not received the Bank Letter of Credit that is required to proceed with this subdivision.

Motion: to table the requests until the applicant is present and until the Letter of Credit is provided. Karen, second Sue D. 6-0-0.

Other Business

Jean reported that the fire ordinance has gone before the zoning committee and they had some good suggestions. It will go back to them on September 29th.

Motion: To adjourn the meeting at 8:45 p.m. Ruth, second Janet. 6-0-0.

Signed and acknowledged by_____________________
