title: September 6, 2005
html:
NEW GLOUCESTER PLANNING BOARD

Minutes of September 6, 2005

Members Present Others Present

Jean Libby, Chairman Ellie Fellers

Karen Asselin, Vice Chairman Laura McCann

James Isaacson, Town Planner Steve McCann

Ruth Waterhouse Ellen Kornetsky

Janet Smaldon Tom Saucier

Laurie Brady ????? Decker

Sue Robitaille

Susan Doyle

Motion: to approve the Minutes of August 16, 2005. Ruth, second Janet.

7-0-0.

Public Hearing – Wooded Creek Subdivision

James gave a brief summary of the proposal and then the public hearing was opened at 7:35. There were no comments by the public so the public hearing was closed at 7:36.

Janet asked what the meaning of “rip rap” was and James answered that it was various rocks, etc. to help prevent runoff. Karen asked whether the special septic designs applicable to the subdivision need to be a condition of approval and James responded that it is already a condition on the plan. Jean commented that the existing ditch on Jason road needs additional work and pointed out that we still need to receive a letter of credit from a Bank. Jean also asked about the covenants and declarations item #26 which reserves the right to change lot lines. Tom Saucier, the representative for the subdivision, said that any changes would have to be subject to planning board review. Jean commented that we should put a note on the plan indicating that so the public is aware. Jean then asked who owns the right-of-way. Mr. Saucier said the owner is John Palmiter and his partner. They have granted the access to DBD. Sue Robitaille asked about the access to the open space and Mr. Saucier responded that there is no public access to the open space because the subdivision in on a private road. Jean commented that the fire chief has agreed to the developer doing sprinklers instead of a fire pond.

Motion: to approve the request for a waiver of stone monuments and the waiver for a fire pond based on the letter from the fire chief and the letter from the soils specialist stating the soils would not support a pond. Karen, second Janet. 7-0-0.

Jean commented that the road maintenance agreement needs to apply to future homeowners also. James pointed out that paragraph 1 of the road maintenance agreement already covers that. James suggested that the developer make a change to the covenants to be sure that the open space is permanently tied up. A question then arose regarding who needs to approve the letter of credit that the developer needs to provide. James said that the Town Manager approves it and the planning board accepts it. Janet and Karen both felt that the Planning Board could approve the subdivision based on the “form” of the guaranty that would be provided and if the Town Manager has any issues with the letter of credit it would have to come back to the Planning Board.

Motion: to approve the Wooded Creek Subdivision based on the findings of fact in the record subject to:

1) Improving the ditches along Jason Road, per the Public Works Director’s recommendations.

2) Submission of a letter of credit acceptable to the Town Manager.

3) No changes in the subdivision without Planning Board approval.

4) Waivers to be indicated on the plan.

Karen, second Janet. 7-0-0.

Sabbathday Road Commercial Subdivision

Tom Saucier came as a representative for the developer. Jean asked about the likelihood of the fire pond holding water given the very sandy soil in the area. Mr. Saucier responded that Dick Sweet has already done an analysis that indicates that there will be adequate water even in drought conditions. That analysis will be provided in the final package. Jean commented that there are a couple of inconsistencies about acreage and lot line dimensions that will need to be fixed for the final plan. Ruth pointed out that the final plan should contain the heading “Notes and Conditions”. Janet mentioned that she was pleased to see that the road was going to be paved. Mr. Saucier said that they still hadn’t decided that officially. He said that they don’t believe that pavement is necessary because they don’t anticipate high volumes of traffic for the businesses. Susan Doyle asked whether the volume of traffic per day would be impacted by the types of vehicles used such as trucks or heavy equipment and Mr. Saucier agreed that that would make a difference. The owner of the land then stated that it doesn’t make sense to pave the whole road because the last 150 feet were only created to make the lot legal as far as road frontage and it is unlikely that anyone would ever need to drive down that portion of the road. Jean asked that the developer and the owner work with the Town Planner to see if they can come up with a creative solution to the paving issue. She also commented that it would be likely that the findings on the fire pond would have to be reviewed.

McCann Garage Addition

Everyone commented that this application was very well done and that there did not appear to be any issues.

Motion: to review under expedited review. Karen, second Ruth. 7-0-0.

Motion: to approve the application. Karen, second Ruth. 7-0-0.


Other Business

James reported that the fire ordinance is going to the zoning committee next week.

Motion: To adjourn the meeting at 8:50 p.m. Ruth, second Susan R. 7-0-0.

Minutes prepared by_______________________

Karen Asselin

Signed and acknowledged by_____________________

Jean Libby, Board Chair

html:
NEW GLOUCESTER PLANNING BOARD

?

Motion: to approve the Minutes of August 2, 2005, as written. Ruth, second Karen. 7-0

Jean welcomed a new member, Susan Doyle. She’ll be filling a year’s term with the Planning Board.

Wooded Creek Minor Subdivision

James talked about how this is an 8-acre parcel off Penny Road that will be 3 cluster lots. The topography looks to be a little steep. Also, five acres of open space are located in the rear, and this will be a private drive. A site walk has already been done.

Karen wanted to know if the steepness is a good enough reason to waive the fire pond. Jean has it written down to mention. The buildings will have sprinklers. In order to waive the fire pond, a letter will be needed from an engineer saying that a fire pond would not work. From there, Jean told Scott how Section 8.1.E of the ordinance must be added to the plan. This states that it will be a private road not maintained by the Town of New Gloucester. The specific designs needed for the lots need to be recorded in the deed.

Jean confirmed that the utilities are indeed underground. A waiver for the stone monuments will need to be given in writing. The fire pond will become a waiver when the letter is submitted. Karen reminded that Board that a letter will be needed from the Fire Chief on the fire pond as well. She did not see anywhere on the plan that the road will be privately maintained, and it must be added.

Concerns were brought up regarding the septics. Janet also mentioned that the availability of water may be an issue. Karen suggested that they do a revised submission. Questions were raised about the road name. Apparently the road as already been named and approved, but someone vandalized the road sign. Jean then asked if the turn around was suitable to the Fire Chief and James is to get something in writing.

The types of homes will be modular ones. Sprinkler systems will already be installed at time of delivery. Jean then asked what the Board thought regarding the application. Laurie mentioned that she thought it was very complete.

Motion: to deem the application complete, subject to written waivers for the fire pond and stone monument, letter from Fire Chief regarding the turn around and sprinkler systems are satisfactory, the addition of the note to the plan regarding the roads, the home association is corrected in regards to road maintenance, and receiving a letter from an engineer stating that the topography will not support a fire pond. Septic systems need to be put on the plan and deed. Karen, second Laurie. 6-1 (Ruth opposed)

Motion: move to schedule a Public Hearing for September 6, 2005 at 7:30 p.m.

Karen, second Janet. 6-1 (Ruth abstains)

Oz Associates Commercial Subdivision

James gave a synopsis regarding the proposition of subdividing a 24-acre parcel on Sabbathday Road into 4 commercial lots. James noticed that they had changed it to 5 lots. Scott then told the Board that if it was going to be changed from a minor subdivision to a major, they would combine two lots to keep it at the four. There is also an existing gravel road.

Jean said that they try to avoid curb cuts. They need to be careful because this is commercial. It doesn’t look like a fire pond will be able to be put in. The sand wouldn’t hold the water. Scott said that he’ll have a test pit dug. If a pond is put in, water will be piped to the road for fire protection access. Jean questioned Scott on the road cuts. He told her why they had drawn out the plan as they did. The curves have to be far enough apart. They have no plan to super elevate the curbs and the speed limit will be low. Karen felt reluctant to waive the two feet.

This is a commercial and industrial road. James does not think it is necessary to require sidewalks.

Lionel, the landowner, stood up to say that lot 2 has been sold. The gentleman who bought it plans to use it to store boats.

Jean told everyone that he’s asked for a waiver. The Board will need something saying there’s adequate water. Scott needs to talk to Gary about the fire pond and there will need to be a road association. They will need to wait before the application is complete.

Scott wanted to know how much time he has to submit information to be in the next meeting. James checked and the deadline is August 30th.

Other Business

There is a workshop with the attorney at the next meeting. It starts at 6:30 p.m.

Fire protection is going to the Zoning Committee

Sue and Susan are going with James tomorrow for a site walk.

Motion: move to adjourn. Karen, second Janet. 7-0.

X____________________________

Jean Libby, Chairman

Jean stated that a letter was submitted by the Leighton family. Should the proper funding not be met, they would give the rest. She said that there would need to be a letter of credit from the bank stating that the money is there to use if needed. Mr. Fitch was not pleased that he had not been informed of this before, and Jean mentioned that the Board could easily make it a condition of approval.

Janet then asked if the Board needed to know who is paying for what and how much. Jean said that hopefully it will all be donated. The Planning Board just needs proof that it can be financially taken care of if all the money is not donated.

Jean said that the Board already approved that trees will be replaced if damaged. She then said that Mr. Fitch will need to submit the letter of credit from the bank to James. Jean then reminded Mr. Fitch that this is a one year permit based on the ordinance.

Karen wanted to know that should they need a longer permit, would the Board allow for that now? Jean said that they could come back in a year if needed, although the one year should be enough time. Mr. Fitch stated that it is not his intent to go beyond the one year.

title: June 21, 2005
html:
NEW GLOUCESTER PLANNING BOARD

Minutes of June 21, 2005

Members Present Others Present

Jean Libby, Chairman Barry Webb

Karen Asselin, Vice Chairman John Palmiter

James Isaacson, Town Planner Don Leavitt

Ruth Waterhouse Dennis Waterman

Janet Smaldon Steve Roberge

Laurie Brady Jim Vadas, Jr.

Hal Phillips

Members Absent Sue Robitaille

John Sumner (unexcused)

Motion: to approve the Minutes of June 7, 2005 with corrections. Ruth, second Karen.

5-0-0.

Sabbathday Heights Major Subdivision

James gave a summary of the application, stating that it was for a 10-lot cluster

subdivision on just over 25 acres. The applicant has proposed to build a 1,400 foot private road. Nine acres in the rear of the property will be set aside as open space. Since the application was last reviewed by the Board, the applicant has obtained the DEP permit and the review of Cumberland County Soil and Water.

Jean pointed out that the applicant still needs to have their road name approved by the

Town. She then asked if note 22 on the topographic site plan referencing underground utilities had been updated and she was told that it had been. Finally, she asked if the applicant was intending to apply for a waiver of the front, rear and side setback requirements. If not, the note on the plan marked by (*) needed to be changed. Steve Roberge responded that they would like to request a waiver of the setbacks and he submitted the request in writing to the Board.

Motion: to reduce the front, side and rear setbacks except in the buffered areas to 25 feet.

Karen, second Ruth. 5-0-0.

Motion: to deem the application complete. Karen, second Ruth. 5-0-0.

Motion: to waive the public hearing since one has already been conducted on this

subdivision and all of the concerns have been addressed. Karen, second Ruth.

5-0-0.

Motion: to approve the subdivision based on the finding of facts presented that shows

that the subdivision meets all of the standards of the ordinance. The approval is subject to the following conditions:

1) Limit on the sale of lots (other than lot 1) to four until all required improvements and road construction is complete, or until another performance guarantee is submitted and accepted by the Board.

2) Access for Lot 1 shall be from the new road only.

3) The well on Lot 2 shall be constructed with steel casing for the first 50 feet.

4) The road name shall be approved by the Town.

Karen, second Ruth. 5-0-0.

Waterman Major Subdivision – Preapplication Sketch Plan

James explained that the Board recently approved a 3-lot after-the-fact subdivision on

this property. Now Dennis Waterman would like to add 8 additional lots to that subdivision. James noted that there is land on the other side of the Royal River that is not useable. Karen then asked whether it was appropriate to do a net residential calculation right away and James said that that would be a good idea.

Steve Roberge, as representative for the applicant, stated that the main purpose for

coming before the Board right now was to get a feel from the Board as to whether they will be required, as stated in the ordinance, to add a second street connection for houses that would cause the traffic level to exceed 200 trips per day. He stated that Mr. Waterman has contacted Don Belanger, an abutter, about possibly connecting a road to his land. Mr. Roberge pointed out that there are already 18 house lots on the road, some of which are vacant, and that the road they would use for the additional 8 homes is already in place due to a lot that has already been split off. They would simply be improving on that existing road.

Jean said that she would like an interpretation by the CEO on the provision in the

ordinance regarding the 200 trips per day because it is not clear whether it applies to just subdivisions and it is unclear in circumstances where some of the houses on the road are in a subdivision and some are not. It is also unclear whether vacant lots should be included in the calculation. Other members of the Board agreed so James will talk to the CEO and get back to the Board with her interpretation.

Barry Webb Cluster Subdivision

James summarized the project stating that Barry Webb is proposing a 3-lot, cluster

subdivision on Church Road. One of the three lots is his home, which is already built. Mr. Webb owns his land and has the option to purchase some additional land, which will bring the total acreage for the project to 6 acres.

Jean informed the applicant that the Board needs to see a submission for a conventional

subdivision also. She also commented that the property is wet and she asked how much wetlands disturbance is expected. The applicant was unsure. Jean then stated that she thinks a site walk is needed before much action can be taken on the request. The site walk was set-up for Tuesday, June 28th at 5:15 p.m.

Hal Phillips of 77 Gloucester Hill Road asked the Board what the impact of the septic

systems would be. James responded by stating that the Board will discuss whether there is a need for a hydro geological survey for this property after the site walk has occurred.

Vadas Self Storage Site Plan Revision

Jim Vadas requested a change to a previously approved site plan for three Self Storage

Buildings. Two of the buildings have already been built and he would like to change the location of the third building to be perpendicular with the first two rather than parallel with them. He feels the change will allow more sun on the building which will help with winter clean up of the area.

Motion: to waive the site walk. Karen, second Ruth, 5-0-0.

Motion: to deem the application complete. Karen, second Ruth. 5-0-0.

Motion: to waive the public hearing. Karen, second Ruth. 5-0-0.

Motion: to approve the application. Karen, second Ruth. 5-0-0.

Other Business

James reported that he had received a copy of a $75,000 letter of credit for Briarwood

Subdivision. The Town Manager has already approved the letter of credit and the Board must accept it.

Motion: To accept the letter of credit performance guarantee. Ruth, second Karen.

5-0-0.

Motion: To adjourn the meeting at 8:30 p.m. Karen, second Ruth. 5-0-0.

Motion: to approve the Minutes of May 17, 2005, with corrections. Ruth, second Karen. 4-0-1 (Janet Abstained)

Public Hearing – Robert Leighton Memorial Gazebo Site Plan

The Town of New Gloucester is proposing to construct a 24’ diameter gazebo behind the New Gloucester Library, in the Historic Lower Village. It will consist of eight sides and granite steps.

Jean stated that the Planning Boards major concern is the funding. She then asked for questions or concerns. Janet wanted to know if the size was suitable for the location. Jean thought it to be a little too big. Karen then mentioned that a tree or two will have to be moved.

Ruth had a list of concerns as follows: why cement foundation, why so large, why not up to the fairgrounds, how much will be donated, who will perform any needed maintenance, why not in honor of more than one person, and what about parking?

Karen’s concerns were with the funding and why it couldn’t be at the fairgrounds. Apparently there is already one planned for the fairgrounds, so that takes care of that.

From there, Jean told everyone that the ordinance clearly states that there must be a sufficient amount of funding before that Planning Board can approve it.

Mr. Fitch asked to speak regarding the gazebo before the Public Hearing was opened. When the library was originally started at the old high school, many planned to eventually put in a gazebo on the natural slope behind it. Since that point, people set up a committee to start reviewing gazebos in surrounding areas. It is their intent to gather information to construct a lasting structure by developing an idea and moving forward with it. He mentioned that they are more than happy to get volunteer labor along with donated money and materials. There is a restriction in the ordinance that doesn’t allow them to start building until a certain amount of money is available. Right now, they do have enough for the foundation. Also, Mr. Fitch wanted to clarify that they would not be cutting down any trees, but taking them up and replanting them elsewhere. Should the trees become damaged in the process of moving them back, they would be more than happy to buy new ones to replace them. Over time, the gazebo should nest within the maples. They want a place where friends can meet.

This gazebo is smaller than the one in Falmouth, and a little larger than a few others. Mr. Fitch also recognized the parking issue. He doesn’t believe that it will add above and beyond to the activities that take place in the area. As for the cement foundation, they want it to last, and think a poured foundation would be best. Wire mesh would be used to go around the foundation to ensure that it stays together for a very long time.

A detailed list of costs has been made by breaking down all that needs to be done. He would like the town’s support so that people will get more involved. So far, the gazebo’s committee has raised $8500 in cash and approximately $4000 in site work. The members of the committee also plan to help out any way they can, and that has not yet been added in. They would probably need $12,000 to $15,000 cash to be able to do the work. This is assuming that donations will be given and people will give of their time to help this happen. If too much money is given, good things will be done with it, and the people of the town will be notified that the goal was reached.

Jean had said that they need significant financial backing. She defined that as being when they can show significant financial backing to the Planning Board, proving that there is enough money to finish the project in the given time. The Code Enforcement Officer will decide in the end if there is enough. Mr. Fitch will need to talk to James and Debbie.

Steve said that after Bob passed, the Board of Selectmen wanted to do something permanent. The first thing they did was give a scholarship. Something that seemed the most appropriate was to build a gazebo behind the library. Brief discussions were made about other locations, but this seemed to be the best one. The gazebo was thought to be the best for Bob, and no one had mentioned anything before about this being in honor of more than one person. This will be considered a town building which means that it will be maintained by the Town of New Gloucester. There may only be minor touch ups on paint or other small maintenance repairs needed from time to time over the years.

It is their intention and hope to keep this place well maintained through funds that will develop over time. Plastic decking timbers will be put in, pressure treated wood will be used, a firm base placed in, and cedar shakes used on the roof to ensure a long lasting gazebo for the community.

Karen mentioned that she knew they would be putting in outlets for bands to use yet asked if they plan to use lights. Would they stay on all the time? Mr. Fitch thought it would be a good idea to have the light switch be in the library, and have the light kept on when a request was made to the librarian.

Public Hearing Opened at 8:05 p.m.

Laurie Fowler: lives right next door at 369 Intervale Road. She thinks it would be a beautiful addition to the town.

Mark Leighton: Bob’s son. His father had once mentioned that he’d like a gazebo behind the library.

Brian Thompson: close friend. Talked about how much Bob had given to this town, the Food bank, and other things. This would be a great tribute to him. Thompson’s Apple Orchard will be supporting and donating to this cause.

Kathy Ramsdell: Bob’s daughter. She wanted to know exactly how much money was needed in order for them to start. Jean said that the Planning Board must be shown the amount they have at any given time to assure that it can and will be completed. Kathy then stated that if it comes to this, the family will commit to the remaining funds that do not get raised. The funds can be provided.

Maurice Ellis: considers himself to be like Bob’s adopted son. He’s so glad that everyone came to recognize Bob and respect his decision to put the gazebo in.

Public Hearing closed at 8:11 p.m.

Jean stated that the Committee will need to talk to James to see if everything is ready in order to come before the Planning Board again. She then said that James suggested the Board table the application until further information is given.

Motion: move to table the application until the funding issue has been resolved with the Code Enforcement Officer or the Town Planner. Karen, second Ruth. 5-0

Karen then asked Mr. Fitch if there was a list of materials. It would be good to post it for people to look at. They might have something they’re not using that they’d like to donate. Jean suggested that it be posted on the public’s channel. Someone else thought they should put it on the Town’s website.

Public Hearing – Chandler House Bed & Breakfast Site Plan

Alton Warren and Shannon Ehrich are proposing to open a 7 guestroom bed & breakfast at 337 Intervale Road, in the Historic Lower Village. They also propose to use the barn for wedding receptions, etc. Since the last meeting, they have added a proposal for a 10’x 10’ gardening shed. There are no changes to the structure other than the additions of railings and a sign near the road. All parking will be in the back field, where there is plenty of room.

Karen asked about the goats that were mentioned for visitors. Al said that they have goats on their farm in Vermont, and the goats might visit from time to time.

Jean wanted to know what the silhouette was located on the top of the sign. Alton clarified by stating it is a silhouette of the old truck in the driveway.

Alton said that the receptions will only take place during the summer, noon to 9 p.m., and on Saturdays.

Vaughn Hardesty: neighbor. He is concerned about noise that would come with having receptions in the barn. James told him that the decibels must be controlled. Shannon went on to say that they are setting time limits for the banquets so that the noise doesn’t go too late. He wanted to know if they planned to allow alcohol to be served, and Jean said that they would need to go through the Town for a permit before anything like that could happen. Mr. Hardesty then commented on the probable increase in traffic and a speed concern. He then questioned as to whether or not they planned to put up a lighted sign. Alton explained how the lights will be placed to only illuminate the sign and nothing more. All in all, he is not opposed to the Bed & Breakfast, but is concerned about what will take place for banquets.

Judy Coggerhall: neighbor. She does not want to look out her window and see cars covering the fields every Saturday. Ms. Coggerhall is not opposed to the Bed & Breakfast at all, but she too, is concerned about the banquets.

Heather Heston: lives across the street. Ms. Heston got up to state that she shares the same concerns about traffic, noise, etc.

Patrick Munsell: neighbor. He is located right next door and would like the consideration of a buffer. Shannon and Alton said they would be happy to work with him on either an evergreen buffer or fencing. Mr. Munsell made it clear that he is not fully in favor of the banquet hall and would like everything to be given more consideration. Patrick questioned gravel parking, but Alton said it would just be grass, and they don’t plan to have many banquets throughout the summer. He too is concerned about noises and traffic. Jean stated that this plan would be approved or disapproved tonight.

Louis Novac: former owner of Chandler House. Ms. Novac stood up to talk about how good Alton and Shannon are. She stated that they will do a great job turning this into a Bed & Breakfast, which will add to its property value. She gave her word that these people will be very good neighbors.

Beth Ellingson: neighbor. Mrs. Ellingson questioned as to whether this would be a permanent parking permit. This couple might have good integrity, but will future owners have the same level of integrity? Everyone needs to think long term and that approach. The liquor license must be approved by the state according to what was stated by someone else.

Daniel Ellingson: Beth’s husband and also a neighbor. He really likes the idea and was quick to welcome the new neighbors. He too voiced his concerns about noise and any use of liquor. He believes vegetation would be great to cut down on noise and was glad for this opportunity to have input.

Beverly Cadigan: lives in the Historic District of the Lower Village. She asked that James read from the Ordinance, the approved uses for the Village District. Karen found it and read as follow: “It allows public and semipublic recreation facilities. This allows for Restaurants and Bed & Breakfasts. Jean said that the Board doesn’t have anything listed right now as to how many people will be allowed. James said the fire marshal will review everything and set a limit. Beverly is in favor of the Bed & Breakfast, yet not for or opposed to the banquet hall. She then urged the Board to listen and act well according to what was voiced by the abutters. From there she asked that the Board address whether the permit for parking would be permanent, once the public hearing was closed.

Patrick Munsell: had one last question. He wanted to know about the tent that was mentioned. Would it be put out back? Shannon said that they wouldn’t necessarily use both. The tent would most likely be placed in the field.

Shannon Ehrich: wanted to address the liquor situation. Alton and she only intend at this time to get a license for Bed & Breakfast only and do not plan to get a liquor license in the near future.

Public Hearing Closed at 8:50 p.m.

Jean went on to say that if a meal at a banquet is catered and liquor is brought onto the property, a license of some sort will be required. This will protect the abutting land owners. James stated that he realizes that they do not plan to serve it, therefore, they might need something like a catering license. Shannon said that they do not plan to have banquets all the time. There may only be a few through out the entire summer.

From there Jean went on to talk about the buffering

“All parking shall be located to the side and rear of structures with vegetative screening, fences, and other methods used to create visual barriers.” Jean said that the buffering could be evergreens. Also, the main parking will be down in the back. Part of the approval will consist of making 9 p.m. the time to stop everything (especially noise) and leave. There is a process and they must comply with what the ordinance states concerning noise. Karen found a section where it says that the sounds must go down 10 decibels after 8 p.m.

Beverly Cadigan: not only should they be concerned about the neighbors, but also the customers staying at the Bed & Breakfast. If she was a paying customer, she’s not sure that she would be too happy if something was going on in the back.

Jean wanted to protect abutters from a new owner. Laurie said that in most places, people have to reapply for the use of things as a new owner. Every town is a little different. In some places the use does not get carried on to the new owner. James said that the conditional uses to not exist in New Gloucester any more. Janet wanted to know if there would be an appeal process if things did not go well. James said that would be up to the Code Enforcement Officer. Ruth wanted to know if it had to be sold as a Bed & Breakfast and she was told no. Karen said you should know what is permitted in the surrounding area if you’re moving in nearby.

Jean then wanted to know about the traffic. Shannon said that the receptions would take place any where between June and September. James then asked Louise to step up to the microphone. He asked her what kind of business she had run. She talked about how she had owned an old antique shop from 1985 to 1995. Many cars had come in and out of the driveway. She played music a lot without any complaints, and had large amounts of people at one time through yard sales for the library, etc.

Karen clarified that the months of operation were actually set from June to October. Hours would be from 11 a.m. to 9 p.m. There would be no more than 100 persons at any given time. This would give the towns people something to work with. There seemed to be a concern about the location of the sign and Shannon said they’d be happy to place it on the other side of the driveway if there was a problem.

From there Karen wanted to know if the wood siding would need to be made a condition.

Motion: to approve the application for the Bed & Breakfast and recreation facility (1) subject to their meeting the buffering requirement of Section 5.1.5, (2) subject to the recreation facility being limited in time to 11 a.m. to 9 p.m. June through October, (3) being limited in number to 100 people or less if it’s determined that the capacity is less, (4) subject to the railings that are being replaced be made from wood and in character with what is already there, (5) the sign being in compliance with the sign ordinance, particularly that that light shine on the sign and not in any other direction, and (6) the noise for the recreation facility must comply with the ordinance as well. Karen, second Ruth. 5-0

Peacock Deck Expedited Site Plan Review

Alexander Peacock is proposing to build a 10’ x 16’ wood deck on the rear of his home at 124 Gloucester Hill Road, in the Historic Lower Village. James and Debbie visited the site and did not see any problems. Alex would build the deck himself. Jean asked if there were any questions, and Beverly said she did not have any and that it was very complete.

Motion: move to review under expedited review. Karen, second Janet. 5-0.

Jean was glad that a picture was given.

Motion: move to approve this. Karen, second Ruth. 5-0.

Other Business

After adjournment the Planning Board Members must stay to sign the plans of Briarwood Estates, Cobb’s Bridge Commons, and Waterman’s Subdivision.

Jean said that the Planning Board is still looking for one member.

Motion: to adjourn. Ruth, second Karen. 5-0.

title: May 17, 2005
html:
NEW GLOUCESTER PLANNING BOARD

Minutes of May 17, 2005

Members Present

Jean Libby, Chairman

Karen Asselin, Vice Chairman

James Isaacson, Town Planner

Angie Elvin, Secretary

Ruth Waterhouse

John Sumner

Members Absent

Janet Smaldon

Laurie Brady

Others Present

Don Douglas

Alton Warren

Shannon Ehrich

Cameron Sloan

Beverly Cadigan

Dale Maschino

Ellie Fellers

Tim Nolan

Kevin Sullivan

Jim Fitch

Ann?

Sue?


Motion: to approve the Minutes of May 4, 2005, with corrections. Ruth, second Karen. 4-0

Chandler House Bed & Breakfast Site Plan Review

James gave a synopsis on how Shannon Ehrich is proposing to open a 7 guest room bed & breakfast at 337 Intervale Road, in the Historic Lower Village. She came earlier before the Board, along with Alton Warren. They had submitted a site plan and septic design. The Board was able to do a site walk a few weeks ago. Karen commented how she saw the adequacy for parking on the site walk. She mentioned that they had discussed the lighting and septic location and believes it to be a good site.

Jean asked them if they’ve spoken to the Fire Chief regarding state laws for this type of project. Alton told her that they just started researching. She then wanted to know if they are required to have sprinklers, and Mr. Warren said yes. Jean asked if they planned to have a dug or artisan well, and Shannon said that they are not sure yet. Alton stated that it might be best to have a dug well, seeing as they have a 600 gallon storage tank in the basement for the sprinklers. There was a concern about the quality of the water, but it was tested fine. Jean asked what they planned on for the material for the rails. Alton commented that it would be either wood or vinyl. (Mr. Warren presented a brochure and a piece of vinyl for the Board.)

From there, Jean asked where the sign location would be. Shannon told the Board that it will go where the “For Sale” sign is. The sign will be made by Tom McDermott and it be approximately 2’x 3’. Karen mentioned that the exact size must be submitted. Also, the lights will shine only on the sign. Jean told them that it must be within the ordinance requirements. A shield is mandatory. She asked what material they plan to use, and was told it would be wood. Jean then wanted to know if they plan to use pressure treated wood. Alton said if they do, it would just be the posts. The lights will come one foot or so off the ground, angled to hit the sign alone. Jean warned them to be careful as to the placement of the sign. People pulling out of the driveway must have a clear view of the road.

On a side note, Ruth wanted to know if the tulip tree was still there, because she believes it to be the only one in town. Shannon thinks it still is, but on its last leg. They will do what they can to save it, but it might be too late.

Jean stated that sprinklers must be installed before they can proceed any further. Karen asked if there was a need for fire escapes. She was told by Alton that the sprinklers would take care of that. John wanted to know if there would be any landscaping changes to the roadside. Shannon may replace the tulip tree, should it fail, with a cherry tree.

Beverly did not see the original package size of the sign and wanted to make sure James was okay with it. He said that according to the performance standards in Article 5, it is fine. She then asked if it would be carved wood, and Alton commented that it would be leaf etched. Beverly then went on to say that she doesn’t think the public hearing should be optional. The water supply is sufficient for a Bed & Breakfast, but what about water for a banquet? Jean said that she isn’t sure as to how much would be needed then. (She mentioned something about how the parking lot won’t be paved.) Alton said that Porto Toilets would be brought in for banquets during the summer. Karen thought that if the banquets were catered that bottled water would be brought in as well. Beverly talked about the checklist being applicable or non-applicable. She is not in favor of the vinyl, and is glad that pressure treated wood no longer contains arsenic. All in all, she believes this to be a great idea and it would be a nice addition to the town.

The members of the Board were then asked for their opinion on the vinyl by Jean. John asked how long it lasts, and Mr. Warren supposed it to be lifetime. Karen thought the vinyl looked classic, but Ruth did not like it at all. Beverly commented on the fact that nothing else on the house in vinyl, so she would hate to see it added now. There are other places nearby that have it. Ruth did agree that it would save a lot of painting and it does look nice. Karen questioned as to why exactly they wanted the vinyl. Alton said it’s quicker with less maintenance. John lived in the historic district. He said that if you say yes to one, you’ll have to let more people do the same thing. Personally, he’d like to see the place looking really nice, so if that’s what it takes, then so be it. Jean wants things to be kept consistent. Alton said they don’t mind doing wood.

Jean asked that everything be given to the Board in writing, from the person performing the tasks. James stated that there are no waivers, although Jean mentioned that the application is not complete yet.

Motion: to deem application complete subject to receiving the decision on railings, description of sign size, material, and location, changes to landscape of property and details of the sprinkler system. Karen, second Ruth. 4-0.

Motion: to schedule a Public Hearing for the next meeting. John, second Karen. 4-0.

Shannon asked if the sign location needed to be on the plan, and Jean said yes.

Briarwood Estates Major Subdivision Amendment

James talked about how Fortin Construction has received DEP approval for the storm water permit on the 23-lot subdivision on the Penny Road, right near the Morrison Ball Field. The retention basin will be maintained by the homeowner’s association.

Jean asked if this would take away from the Little League, and she was told it would be fine. There used to be an easement between two lots, but its been reconfigured. Tim Nolan said they can still gain access to the back part. The detention pond will be mostly dry. There will be lots of room to get to the existing back field. Also, the DEP has their own storm water management plan. Jean wanted to know if Little League has seen it, and Kevin Sullivan said that he hasn’t seen it, but doesn’t feel the need to. He was asked by Jean to add the road not maintained by the Town of New Gloucester be added to the “Notes and Conditions.” It must be put on by the surveyor. It must say “Road(s)” because there are two roads. Everything else seems to be ready. Tim asked if it could be approved subject to Keith putting that on the plan.

Motion: to approve the revision of plans subject to receipt of Article 8 Section 8.1E. Also, to resubmit the homeowner’s agreement showing the changes made. Karen, second John. 3-1 (Ruth opposed)

Waterman Minor Subdivision

James explained how this is a 3-lot minor subdivision. One lot was split off in 1995 and another in 1996. From there, another was split off in 2003. The Board needs to approve this after the fact. It’s been before the Board for about two years now. The road was in bad shape and needed to be improved, and changes have been made to it. According to James, Debbie Parks has approved the road. James saw it last week and commented that it could still use a little work on the shoulders. It is a good road now that it is basically finished.

Karen wanted to know where things had been left off. Jean told her that they just wanted the road fixed, and James told her how the people had just gone ahead and done the work. Jean wanted to know if there is an easement now, and James said yes. There is one for each home on the three lots. Further development cannot be done unless they come before the Planning Board.

Don asked if this requirement was in the ordinance, regarding the road. Yes, because there was no real road there. Any plans to subdivide must come before the Board. Ruth asked if it would be any different if a relative that they wanted to add. Jean said that they would still need to come back. Karen asked how people were supposed to find these houses, and Don said it would be up to the people who live there. She then wanted to know if it was all private road, and Jean said it was. From there Karen commented on how the road includes more than just Don’s three lots. Others should be joined in on this. James said that making other landowners join is out of the Board’s hands. Jean mentioned that they are on a legal right-of-way. Karen assumed it would all be taken care of, according to state law, and Jean said it would. Jean then asked if the application was complete. She did say that Article 8.1E. needed to be put onto the plan.

Motion: to deem the application complete. Karen, second Ruth. 4-0.

Jean told Don to bring back the plans with the items added.

Motion: to waive the Public Hearing. Karen, second Ruth. 4-0.

Motion: to approve the application subject to any further coming before the Board, and a note added to the plan regarding the road being maintained by the homeowners. Karen, second Ruth. 4-0.

Robert Leighton Memorial Gazebo Site Plan Review

James talked about the 24’ diameter gazebo that is wanted to be placed behind the New Gloucester Library. It will be made of wood with cedar shingles, granite steps, and artificial deck timbers.

Jim said that he moved it further away from the library. It would be nice to have an organized gathering at the location. Trees will need to be moved, and if they fall, new ones will be put in. There will be four trees in all that need to be moved. Karen asked if the functions would be related to the library, or geared more towards things that go on at Trotter’s Park. Jim said it is a completely different type of function. It would not be so much as geared towards the library, but as a town center. (i.e. the Strawberry Festival. It wouldn’t happen at Fairgrounds, but this would be a good place for it.)

He then mentioned that the septic system location was near 3.278 on the plan.

Jean said that she’d rather not approach this too quickly. Jim reminded everyone that this has been going on for four years now, just trying to get the process going. Jean wanted to know what he meant by process, and he told her it was about getting workers and materials together, to last a long time. If it doesn’t happen right away, people lose interest, or just forget about it. Jean told him that once he starts, he needs to be able to finish, but Jim said that they do not have all the money yet. Karen wondered if a condition could be made to have at least 50% to start. In that case, Jim felt that he would have to withdraw the application were that to become a condition. Right now he has the $7,600 to break ground with and put the foundation in. Beverly asked if he could get a kit from Made in Maine, yet Jim said they were not large enough. Karen could see that Jim feels very strongly about breaking ground soon. He said they’ve been trying to get people to donate, but there have been very little donations at this time. Jean said that the Board needs a performance guarantee. There’s no leverage here. She thinks the gazebo would look beautiful, but believes it to be too big.

Karen was not aware of the money situation before. Should they send something out to everyone now asking for donations? Jim thought that by starting, people will be more apt to give. He would appreciate it if the Town would help fund it. Adding this asset will not raise the taxes of the townspeople. Jean wanted to know if this can be completed in a reasonable amount of time. Ann commented that donations are coming in and would like the project to be activated again. People are seeing the thermometer that has been put out, and they’ll start giving more. Karen asked what time frame they are looking at here-six months? Jean said that it would be a year from approval. They have $7,600 of the needed $30,000. Jim said this amount is estimated without volunteer labor or donated materials. Jean told him that he needs to educate the people about this project. Karen thought they should wait until they have $10,000.He needs to be able to start building as soon as he gets assets. Beverly asked if the concrete was donated, and Jim didn’t imagine that it would be. He’s not sure of the exact cost right now, but he’d be glad to find out. Beverly then mentioned that the Planning Board has the option of extending this to one year. Everybody has to be held to the same standards. They could extend it to the two year time frame, although money to begin isn’t even accounted for on the thermometer. Jean thinks the gazebo is too big, and they need to be careful. Jim commented that the gazebos at Thompson’s Orchard and Pineland are private. This certainly is not duplication, and it will be for public use.

Jean felt that a site walk was not necessary.

Motion: to waive request for boundary survey and contour lines. Karen, second Ruth. 4-0.

Motion: to deem the application complete. Karen, second Ruth. 4-0.

Motion: to have a Public Hearing at the next meeting. John, second Karen. 4-0.

Other Business

Jean said they would not be signing any subdivision plans tonight.

Pineland Tour – Jean and Ruth are going to the Conference Center before 6 p.m. James mentioned that the Board helped approve Pineland.

Motion: to adjourn. Ruth, second Karen. 4-0.

X____________________________

Jean Libby, Chairman

title: May 4, 2005
html:
NEW GLOUCESTER PLANNING BOARD

Minutes of May 4, 2005

Members Present

Jean Libby, Chairman

Karen Asselin, Vice Chairman

James Isaacson, Town Planner

Angie Elvin, Secretary

Ruth Waterhouse

Janet Smaldon

Members Absent

John Sumner (excused)

Laurie Brady (excused)

Others Present

Pat Anderson

David Anderson

John Foley

Janet Foley

Stephanie Bryan

John Palmiter

Norma Walsh

Robert Walsh

Donald Leavitt

Wayne Cobb

Steve Roberge

Steven Cobb

Beverly Cadigan

Anne McCormack


Motion: to approve the Minutes of April 19, 2005, with corrections. Ruth, second Karen. 4-0

Public Hearing – Sabbathday Heights Major Subdivision

James gave a synopsis on how Don Leavitt and John Palmiter are planning to build a 10 lot cluster subdivision on the east side of Snow Hill Road. A new private road has been proposed along with a retention pond.

Jean then asked Mr. Roberge to speak on behalf of the project. He has presented a cluster subdivision, which has an advantage of less environmental impact. He’s put together an eight page report. They plan to build a private road and would like it to hopefully become a public one at some point. Steve also requested a wavier of underground utilities. The only thing keeping it from becoming public is the grade. There will be a homeowner’s association which will keep track of the maintenance and the land’s state. A storm water study has been done, showing the water to drain from the top of the hill to the bottom. Mapping has been done of the wetlands. Water would drain down and empty into the fire pond. Any pollution would then settle to the bottom of it. Some water would eventually drain to the 18” culvert beneath Snow Hill Road. Mr. Roberge mentioned that he had taken notes at the last meeting regarding concerns from abutters, etc. and action was taken. There is a right of way along the existing road in open space for timber management only. Norm Chamberlain had concerns about the driveway on the existing lot. The driveway will be moved to the proposed road. All buffers will be stated and enforced by the homeowner’s association.

The new proposed name for this cluster subdivision is “Sabbathday Heights Road”. James said that the Board of Selectman would be having a meeting later on in the week, and that would be discussed.

All of the abutters have been notified by certified mail. A document has also been submitted to the DEP for the wetlands alteration permit, main general construction permit, and storm water permit. They have also submitted documents to the Cumberland County Storm Water Conservation District, for their review. They’ve yet to hear back from them.

Public Hearing Opened at 7:50 p.m.

John Foley stepped forward. He owns property at 641 Snow Hill Rd. He’s concerned about oil, grease, and other properties that are emitted from tar, etc. The lake could be hurt by this, and there’s nothing to tell him that this won’t affect it. Nothing was really said about the runoff, and what’s going to be put into the lake. John voiced that he strongly dislikes the name they’ve chosen to hopefully call it. Steve replied by telling him how they plan to have wooded buffers which will encourage water to go straight into the ground. The water will then enter a small culvert which will become wetland. This water will settle. Any solids will then settle to the bottom of the pond. As far as the existing pond, half of it is part of one of the properties, and half is on another. John said that he knows grease in water will float, so you can’t tell him that it will settle. Steve said that most of it will not make it to the pond, due to the wooded buffer. The driveway will be made to send the water to the buffers, as opposed to traveling down the road itself. This is acceptable by DEP. Every road that you make is made out of asphalt, but what you try to do is see that the water runs off in the right direction. John had questioned about how much more water will be flowing down there. He was told by Steve that even less will be flowing down due to their wooded areas.

David Anderson of 27 Allen Road then got up to speak. He wanted to question the project along the same vein. Would the water become a mosquito bog? Steve said it would be no different than the lake, but Mr. Anderson didn’t seem to think so, due to the fact that the lake moves. Then the size of the pond was brought up, and Mr. Roberge stated that it will be approximately 60’ x 80’. The pond will stay exactly where it is. David mentioned that the water in the culvert freezes in the during the winter and as it starts to melt, water continuously goes through.

Public Hearing Closed at 8:00 p.m.

Jean stated (regarding the Public Hearing) that both DEP and Cumberland County Soil are checking the soil runoff. As far as the pond issue and culvert, the New Gloucester Public Works has checked the plan. James said that one concern was whether or not the culvert was sized properly and if it should be changed or not. Steve explained that the 18” culvert might not be large enough to service up to a 25 year storm. The water would rise and start to go over the road. The other method would provide more peak flow to leave the site. You could either increase the size of the culvert to allow for more drainage, or just add another one. As David Anderson said, the water will freeze up in the winter. Karen then wanted to know if increases were made at all, if this would increase the amount of water that would run to the lake. Steve explained how it would benefit the flow. The same amount of water would need to go through, but it would flow faster, to keep it from building up. Karen wanted to know if there were any reasons not to add the second culvert. Steve said the reason to put it in would be for safety aspects. Those creating the plan are really working hard to loop it all together.

Jean told Steve that James will talk to Kevin to see where things can go with this. She also wanted to know where the restrictions for lots 2, 4, and 5 came from. Steve said that it was an error on his part. Karen mentioned that everything was very well done. She’d picked up within the homeowner’s association (Page 2, Sec. 6) where it stated there are to be eleven lots when only 10 have been proposed. Steve will check on it to make sure that it is changed, if it isn’t already. Jean wanted to know if there would be one curb cut per lot, and Steve said that was correct. Janet and Ruth were asked if they had any questions, and they did not. Karen had another question regarding the Town being the 3rd party in the maintenance agreement, but the DEP is now involved. Steve said that that does not mean that the Town can not be involved. James mentioned that the neighbors are the first in line of enforcement, although the DEP are well versed in this. Anybody can complain for action to be taken, but that first step must take place in order for the Town to react.

Jean then thanked Don & John for working with the abutters and listening to their concerns. Most of her questions were answered. The Board is still waiting on Cumberland County Soil. Steve said that he should hear back by next week. James has submitted the plans for the fire pond to the fire chief and he is reviewing them. The list that Jean has for which the Board is waiting for would be as follows: public work, Cumberland County Soil, and fire chief. This is pretty much out of Steve’s hands; although he must make sure the CCS gets back with information as soon as possible.

Motion: to waive the underground utilities and stone monuments, under the condition that the stone monument be replaced with the capped rebar. Karen, second Ruth. 4-0.

Motion: move to deem the Preliminary Application Complete. Karen, second Ruth. 4-0.

Steve will fix the things that the DEP requires. Jean wants to see the application and all other information. James will make sure that everything is done in a timely manner. Jean appreciated his patience and great job on the application. Steve will let James know anything that he hears.

Bryan Sunroom Rehab Expedited Site Plan Review

Jean started out by stating that there was a problem with an abutter (Janet). Stephanie voiced her concern about things taking a while. Janet stated clearly that she is not prejudice in any way and would vote fairly. The Board was agreeable, and Janet was permitted to stay and give her input and vote. James then gave a synopsis on how Stephanie Bryan is proposing to replace a sunroom addition on her home at 143 Cobbs Bridge Road, in the Historic Overlay District. They will fix the walls, but the size will not change. Debbie and James both checked it and they found no issues. Stephanie explained how Thomas Moser had put this addition on the house back in the 1970s. Jean wanted to know if there would be any change in the landscaping, and Ms. Bryan said no. Janet wanted to know what the windows would look like. It will look more like a colonial window as opposed to the average new window. Jean asked for input from the Historic Society, and the woman representing said she would vote yes.

Motion: move to review under expedited review. Karen, second Ruth. 4-0.

Jean went on to say that everything is there and all set.

Motion: move to approve the application. Karen, second Ruth. 4-0.

Cobb Garage Replacement Site Plan Review

James talked about how Wayne Cobb is proposing to construct a 25’x 40’ garage at his home at 279 Lewiston Road, in the Village District. This garage will be replacing the one the burned down a couple of years ago. It’ll be in the same spot as the original garage. (Reminder: this is in the Village Distract, not the Historic District) This being a residential garage in the Village District qualifies it for expedited review. James wanted to know if he planned to put in a new foundation, and Wayne said yes, because the old one was very rough. Jean asked if it would be one story, and she was told yes. This is a non-conforming lot.

Motion: move to go with the expedited review. Ruth, second Janet. 4-0.

Jean asked for any questions, and there were none.

Motion: move to approve the application. Karen, second Ruth. 4-0.

McCormack Apartment Conversion
James gave a synopsis on how Ann McCormack is proposing to convert the former Village Bake House into an apartment on Peacock Hill Road. The change is from commercial to residential. It lies within the Historic Overlay District. The only changes will be interior, and it will become a place for two family housing. Jean mentioned that there is land enough for two. James wanted to know what she has to submit. The well and septic are appropriately sized. Ann intends to paint the building eventually, but nothing will be added to the exterior. Everything will remain the same. Karen said that there will definitely be less traffic. Jean said that it must meet the fire safety standards. The woman from the Historic Society questioned Ann as to how many bedroom there would be. She was told there would be two. She said there were no problems, and she sees less of an impact than what was there before. Karen wanted to know if it would be located on the first floor and Ann told her yes.

Motion: move to change the building from retail use to an apartment, subject to the condition of coming back before the Board for review of any changes. Karen, second Ruth. 4-0.

Other Business

Karen read in the “Findings of Fact” a statement that the Town has found no impact on the solid wastes of this Town. Jean said it is the same way with the schools. Based on James findings, there is not significant impact. Karen stated that the Board is supposed to receive letters regarding these issues. She feels that she can not affirm what it says, unless reviewed by the Board. There is an impact, and it needs to be discussed. Jean felt that the solid waste in a minor issue. Your effects will take place where your tax dollars are. James said that you need to find out where there will be adverse effects. Karen really feels that these things need to be discussed, in order to be able to vote with a full knowledge of the situation. She suggested that the wording be changed, after discussion. James wanted to know if there is a certain capacity of which the transfer station is at. No one really knew. Karen wanted to remove it from the “Findings of Fact”, but James said that it could not be. Where the schools are concerned, the Superintendent must write a letter to inform the Town as to whether or not it can handle more students. As far as the transfer station, waste is constantly increasing, due to properties. Another compactor is needed, but the Town must save up for it. Things would be a lot easier to know if New Gloucester had curb side pickup.

Motion: move to adjourn. Ruth, second Janet. 4-0.

X____________________________

Jean Libby, Chairman

title: April 19, 2005
html:
NEW GLOUCESTER PLANNING BOARD

Minutes of April 19, 2005

Members Present:

Jean Libby, Chairman

Karen Asselin, Vice Chairman

James Isaacson, Town Planner

Angie Elvin, Secretary

Ruth Waterhouse

Janet Smaldon

John Sumner - excused

Laurie Brady

Others Present:

Ellie Fellers

Daniel Fortin

Pat Lowe

David & Pat Anderson

Hilary Elvin

Linda Chase

Laura Leavitt

Donald Leavitt

John Palmiter

Clifton Foster

Steve Chandler

Keith Morse

Steve Roberge

Review and Approval of Minutes for April 5, 2005

Motion: to accept the Minutes of April 5, 2005 as is. Ruth, second Janet. Karen made one minor change. 5-0

Sabbathday Heights Major Subdivision

James gave a synopsis on how Donald Leavitt and John Palmiter are proposing to subdivide a 25.3 acre parcel on Snow Hill Road into 10 lots. They are proposing a cluster subdivision with 9.4 acres of open space. The Board has had a pre-application sketch plan meeting, and a site walk was completed on April 14th. The land is heavily wooded and has a good slope to it.

Karen said it was clear that the road runs directly adjacent to the property on the left part of the way. Jean thought it was a very nice lot, but one concern is to make sure that everything possible be done to protect the lake. The road name must be approved by the Town Selectmen. She went on to say that there will be 9 four-bedroom lots and 1 two-bedroom lot. The two-bedroom will appear on lot 1.

Mr. Roger was then asked by Jean to tell the Board more about what he wants to do for utilities. She thought it would be better for them to go underground. Steve Roger

said it really wouldn’t make a difference whether it was above ground or below. The clearing of trees would be the same. He plans to keep the buffer by keeping a good percentage of the trees. It will be shown on the plan that will be signed and recorded. Karen said she lives in a subdivision that deals with the same as this. The association agreement isn’t always easy to enforce. Steve said there will be deed restrictions and a homeowner’s association. There’s not much else that he feels he can do. Jean wants to make sure that everything is protected. He said that if someone does come in and cut the buffer, they would be required to plant another tree in its place. Janet said that he must be very careful that he doesn’t get a lawsuit on his hands.

Steve said that the DEP will get involved. Karen said that if no one reports it, it wouldn’t work very well. The lots can be reduced to a half acre, although the Town doesn’t normally do this. It would let the people know that they don’t own the land to be able to cut down the trees. The owners will be shown that cutting down the trees may damage the quality of the lake. He has reservations about make the lots smaller than the one acre. It would be better to make it an easement area that is a no-cut area, rather than take it away from the property. They’ve made provisions that would be recorded in the registry, document something in the deed, and include the buffer as part of the easement. Most of the lots have drainage buffers, but a couple do not with the way the contours are set up. Karen wanted to know if these two lots posted the most threat, and he said it would be about the same. Only by natural means will something drain to a neighbor. Jean asked that he put something in a waiver for the underground utilities. This must be treated as a private road. Mr. Roger asked that they look at the notes 25-28 on page 3 of the notebook. They will be building the road to Town specifications, with a 10% grade. He’d like the Selectmen to consider it to eventually become a public read. It was then brought up by Jean that the maximum grade of a public road is 8%, as stated in the ordinance. Right-of –ways are being created on the ends of the properties to allow for further development. Rights will depend on whether it becomes a private road or a public one.

Karen wanted to know if there was an easement off of lot 6. Steve said it’s there to allow for future plans. Jean asked if he’s heard back from the Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife, and he has not. It’s very important that he does. There also shouldn’t be any problem with historic preservation. James wanted to know if environment impacts have been considered on the retention pond, and Steve said it’s hard to know that right now. Steve said that the land owners could always build a pond on their own lot. Jean asked if this was submitted to the DEP, and Steve said yes. Jean then asked Karen to read a letter given to the Board in regards to the subdivision.

“Dear Jean:

I was notified last week that a 10 lot cluster development subdivision is being planned for the old Hunnewell property nearly across Snow Hill Road from my driveway (Allen Road). Unfortunately, I am unable to attend tonight’s meeting. But, I have done a cursory review of the design plans, graciously supplied to me by the design engineer, and only have a few written comments.

I am familiar with Steve’s work and know that he does a fine job with this kind of development. However, I am concerned with this project’s impact on Sabbathday Lake. It is my understanding that Steve has proposed a combination of buffers and a wet pond/fire pond for this project to remove most of the sediment from the storm water runoff. While this may be the best practicle solution it will only provide protection to the lake as long as it is maintained properly. I would suggest that the Town be made a party to the maintenance agreement so that it will have the right to go in and fix problems, at their expense, if the home owners association is not taking proper care of it.

I walk Snow Hill Road regularly and can’t help but note the usual comments that you must hear on these types of projects: increased traffic and excessive speed. I am very familiar with the existing driveway to Lot 1, having gone in and out of it many times. It can be quite hazardous due to the limited sight distance to the north. I would suggest that Lot 1 take its access from the new road, rather than the existing location on Snow Hill Road. I don’t think this would be a great hardship on the developer and we would then not have an increase in curb cuts onto Snow Hill Rd.

I hope this letter provides constructive comments for the proposed development. It would have been much nicer, from my point of view, if this project had been proposed as a sending property under the new Transfer of Development Rights ordinance. But, we can’t have everything we want. Thank you for the Board’s time.”

Sincerely,

Norman G. Chamberlain II

13 Allen Road

New Gloucester, Maine 04260

Mr. Roger stated that he will gladly accept any constructive criticism. Jean wanted to know what it meant to say that things would have to be fixed at owner’s expense. Steve was reading it as the Town coming in to fix whatever is needed and then charging the homeowner’s association. Jean wanted to be very careful for the precedent set for other developers down the road. When proposing and easement area, they could include the Town as a 3rd party. Jean said that it’s up to the tax payers of the Town as to whether or not they will accept this as a public road.

Ruth wanted to know if the open space was put at the very beginning of the development, would that slow down the impact on the lake. Steve wasn’t sure how to answer that, but didn’t think that was a good idea. Janet wanted to address James’ comment on lot 2. James said that there doesn’t appear to be room for a well. Steve mentioned that on the plan there is a miniscule location for where the well can be located. The hydrologist kept a 100 foot radius of the location of the test pits. They thought they might ask for a waiver for that one lot only. Jean asked if there was any open space on that lot, and he said no. James said that the purpose of having two test pits shows that there a two locations of a septic. The well can not be within 100 feet of the septic. They will take one test pit from the well exclusion area per lot, to give a much larger window for the owners to place their wells.

Jean said that this was still preliminary and asked if there were any abutters who had any questions or concerns.

Steve Chandler (representing the Chandler Brothers) is an abutter. He wanted to make sure everyone was aware of everything that happens on adjacent parcels. He has used the old timber road that passes through the parcel on the plan. The road actually goes through many existing properties, and he may need access to it in the future and would like to make sure it will be given to him. Could a deal be struck to allow for this? It would be hard if they were over ridden in the future and not given access to it.

Ellie Fellers got up to speak about Sabbathday Lake, because she lives nearby. She was concerned about the health of Sabbathday Lake, and the water shed study. It would be good to do a water survey.

Cliff Foster said that he has no objections to the project, but would like a right-of-way over the piece of land that gives him access to timber. He stated that he would be willing to buy the land with a deed restriction, which would allow for his trucks to come in and out without problems.

Jean mentioned that she would love to see them work with things to keep forested land. She would like the Cumberland County Soil to double check the soil. She asked that they come back with a written request for the underground utilities. Also, submit the road name for the Selectman to vote on. James suggested that they change the name. Jean asked that the comments of abutters be taken into consideration. Jean then questioned whether or not the Board should schedule a public hearing. Karen commented that the application is very complete.

Motion: move to have a Public Hearing at the next town meeting. Karen, second Ruth. 5-0

Steve wanted to know if he was supposed to notify the abutters within 500 ft. and Jean said yes. It will also be notified in the Lewiston Sun Journal.

Maplewood Estates Major Subdivision

James explained how Mainely New Homes, Inc. is proposing to subdivide a 13-acre parcel on Route 100 north of the Upper Village. The proposal is for six cluster lots with some open space in the back. This is a pre-application submission.

Jean asked if lot 1 has an easement and Keith said yes. She wanted to know if the old railroad back would be removed, and they said no. One good thing is that this is not located near the Sabbathday Lake water shed. The road will be 50 ft. wide and maintained as a private road at all times. Janet then questioned as to why open space is always at the rear. Jean told her that it would not be cost effective to make the road even longer than necessary. Keith said that the plan is quite simple, and should not be an expensive subdivision. Janet wanted to know how much more it would cost to be a little more creative with the open space. Keith didn’t think with the lay out of the land that that would be a good idea, but they are open to the Board’s suggestions on all matters. Jean decided to schedule a site walk and remind him to notify the abutters. They need to submit the name of the road for approval from the Selectman. James will give them the form to fill out. The fire pond was placed where it was to go along with the CMP easement. Keith needs waivers for these three things: (1) reduced set-backs, (2) stone monuments, (3) and underground utilities. Keith mentioned that he does not have a problem with the buffers, but Jean warned him about neighbors who might have businesses with loud trucks, etc.

Keith wanted to know if the Board would require a hydrology and storm water study for the site walk. Jean said those things can only be decided on that at a Board meeting, not on the site walk.

Jean set the site walk for Wednesday, April 20, 2005.

Keith and the Board talked a little more about the buffers and the road that abutters could possible use. James said that there are no public access rights, only private access rights. Keith mentioned that the little roadway is not a range road. Jean told him that James would double check just to make sure.

Other Business

There was a lot of discussion as to when the Public Hearing would take place, due to a school district meeting.

Motion: move to reschedule the next meeting for Wednesday, May 4, 2005, at 7:30 p.m. Karen, second Ruth. 5-0

Motion: move to adjourn. Ruth, second Karen. 5-0

Motion: to adjourn. Karen, second Ruth. 4-0

X__________________________

Jean Libby, Chairman

title: April 5, 2005
html:
NEW GLOUCESTER PLANNING BOARD

Minutes of April 5, 2005

Members Present:

Jean Libby, Chairman

Karen Asselin, Vice Chairman

James Isaacson, Town Planner

Angie Elvin, Secretary

Ruth Waterhouse

Janet Smaldon

John Sumner - excused

Laurie Brady

Others Present:

Ellie Fellers

Michael Thompson

Review and Approval of Minutes for March 15, 2005

Motion: to accept the Minutes of March 15, 2005 with corrections. Ruth, second Karen. 5-0.

Thompson’s Bluegrass Festival

Jean asked Karen to take over this discussion because she considered herself to be an abutter. Karen agreed to do it for her.

James gave a synopsis on how Thompson’s Orchard is proposing to host their 2nd Annual Family bluegrass Music Festival on Gloucester Hill. It is a three day festival of music. A gazebo was built last year. Also, there is a rough camping area designated for people to come and stay, along with designated parking. James then asked Michael Thompson how it went.

Michael said that it all went very well, except for the rain. Everybody that was there had a great time regardless of the rain. Karen wanted to know if he’d added parking and Mike said that it remains the same. James stated that this is the same application that was used last year. Karen questioned the port-o-potties, and Ruth said she saw it on the drawings presented to the Board. Karen then asked about the times the bands would be playing. Mr. Thompson said it would be Friday (6 p.m. to 10 p.m.), Saturday (9 p.m. to 10 p.m.), and Sunday (9 .am. to 3 p.m.). Michael was asked as to whether or not he’s gotten any feedback from the festival last year, and he told them that it has all been good. Karen then wanted to know if he knew of anything else that might be subject to change, and the only thing he knew of was that some people might come a few days early to camp out. Karen asked whether or not the Board felt a site walk was necessary. Laurie didn’t feel that she needed to see it.

Motion: to waive the site walk. Janet, second Ruth. 4-0

Motion: to deem the application complete. Janet, second Ruth. 4-0

Karen then wanted to know if the Board felt the need for a Public Hearing. Ruth didn’t think that it was necessary, and Janet agreed. No one complained about it last year, and Laurie also stated how there was no need to hold hearing on the matter. Karen thought that the public should be able to come and voice their opinions, if there were any.

Motion: to waive the Public Hearing. Janet, second Ruth. 3-1 (Karen opposed)

Karen felt that there were some things that need to be considered regarding the application. She didn’t feel comfortable regarding the significant complaints and what that was considered. Do you go by one person complaining many times, or many people commenting a few times. Also, Karen asked the Board if they thought this should be an indefinite approval. Laurie stated that it should have to come before the Board each year for approval. Karen said that the scope of things might be changed and for that reason, it should be looked at. People might become uncomfortable if things are changed in the future. Laurie thought that it would grow each year. Ruth thought that the Thompson’s are organized enough that if things are changed, that they would come back to the Board. Michael said that he would be more than happy to pass on any changes to the Town and the Board. He is hoping that the festival will continue to grow. James then asked if they had checked the noise levels last year. Michael said that they had and were well within the levels. Karen reminded him that he must put up signs on the road to warn people driving on Gloucester Hill of the event.

Motion: approval of Thompson’s Bluegrass Festival with the conditions that (1) noise levels will be checked during the festival and adjusted accordingly, (2) no street parking on Gloucester Hill Road will be allowed, (3) temporary warning signs shall be posted on Gloucester Hill Road to warn on-coming traffic of the event, and (4) additional approval must be given by the Board if any changes are made. Ruth, second Janet. 4-0

Set Site Walks

Major Subdivision on Snow Hill Road: set for April 14th at 5:15 p.m.

Chandler House Bed and Breakfast: April 12, 2005 at 5:15 p.m.

Jean talked about her trip to Augusta with James and how the meetings went.

Jean and James are working on the Fire Protection Ordinance.

The Zoning Committee is working on a road plan.

The next meeting will consist of discussing accessory apartments.

Motion: to adjourn. Karen, second Ruth. 4-0

X__________________________

Jean Libby, Chairman

title: March 15, 2005
html:
NEW GLOUCESTER PLANNING BOARD

Minutes of March 15, 2005

Members Present:

Jean Libby, Chairman

Karen Asselin, Vice Chairman

James Isaacson, Town Planner

Angie Elvin, Secretary

Ruth Waterhouse

Janet Smaldon

John Sumner

Laurie Brady

Others Present:

Julia R. Appt

Jeremy S. Appt

Hilary Elvin

Will Haskell

Jim Vadas Jr.

Shannon K. Ehrich

AB Warren

Raylene Estabrook

A.H. Fleming


Review and Approval of Minutes for March 1, 2005

Motion: to accept the minutes of March, 1, 2005, with corrections. Ruth, second John. 6-0

Public Hearing – Clear Brook Estates Minor Subdivision

James explained how Mr. James Vadas is proposing to subdivide a 9.59 acre parcel on Morse Road into 4 lots, at 2 acres a piece. It’s on a new private road named “Clear Brook Trail”. Changes requested at the last meeting have been submitted. Jean said that a waiver was not requested for utilities to go above ground. Jim was not happy that this was not mentioned to him before. Karen said that it could be submitted, and Jean said it could be made a condition of approval

Public Hearing opened at 7:35 p.m.

Public Hearing closed at 7:36 p.m.

Jim wasn’t aware that it needed to be a waiver, but James said that it is located within the ordinance. Jean asked that it be put in writing and be submitted to the Board tonight and the waiver added to the plan. James said that the road name was approved the night before by the Board of Selectmen.

Motion: move to waiver underground utilities. Karen, second Ruth. 5-0 (Laurie abstains as an abutter)

Motion: to approve the application with the condition that the plan is amended to reflect the waiver of underground utilities. Karen, second Ruth. 5-0 (Laurie abstains as an abutter)

Public Hearing – Cobb’s Bridge Commons Major Subdivision

Jean first asked if there were any questions from the Planning Board on the submissions. She said that she had a small question. The boundary and topographic survey was not corrected on the plan and needs to be fixed. Their road name was also approved.

James then gave a synopsis on how A & R Builders are proposing to subdivide a 36.7 acre parcel on the very end of Cobb’s Bridge Road into 12 lots with a small amount of open space. A portion of it runs along Royal River. Each lot will be at least two acres in size. A small private road has been set and will be called “Rosewood Lane”.

Public Hearing opened at 7:46p.m.

Public Hearing closed at 7:47 p.m.
