Jean stated that this was a very complete application and Janet added that it should be a model. Karen agreed that there is not suitable land for a fire pond. She just wanted to know if the Board had what they needed to make a waiver, because she thought the letter that Will wrote was sufficient. Jean said that an adequate water supply must exist within the subdivision. James said that you could just put sprinklers in each home. Laurie wanted to know who would follow the selling of a house and the checking of the sprinkler system. How will we know if they still work? Jean said that a testing must be done by the sprinkler installation company. Al said that he believed that to be a suggestion or request by the fire chief. Karen wanted to know how it works for insurance purposes. Jean said that it’s like a fire alarm. No one knows if you’ve unplugged it or not. Karen asked where the nearest fire pond was, and was told that it is about two miles away. Will said that there is a significant amount of bedrock where a fire pond would have been. He wanted to know what else might be needed to move beyond this point. He wanted to know why he couldn’t write the letter himself. James said that he knows it doesn’t take a geologist to see that a fire pond can not exist in bedrock. The Board has a letter from the fire chief to waive the pond. Whether or not the sprinklers fail in the future and what should be done about it, is not up to the Board. Janet said that it should be up to the CEO. Karen stated that the Board must be careful about the precedent that it sets for the future. Will said that he’d have a soil specialist put his name on the request saying that the land will not support a fire pond. Jean said that it would be easier for the Board for the next time around, if a professional wrote the letter. Janet read about how the fire department has requested copies of the testing reports. Al stated that if the land can’t support a fire pond, and each house has an adequate water supply, the sprinklers do not have to be put in.

Motion: move to waive stone monuments and replace them with the bar, waive the fire pond subject to receiving a letter from a soil scientist stating that the soil will not support one. Karen, second Ruth. 6-0

Jean said that you do not have to put a sprinkler system in, as Al stated before. According to the ordinance, it is not a requirement. Al did say that they will be built into the building package. Jean said that if it is on the plan, then they will be held to it.

Motion: move to deem the application complete. Karen, second Ruth. 6-0

Motion: move to approve the application subject to receiving the letter from the soil scientist, conditional agreement of performance guarantee, DEP approval, and result of sprinkler testing being turned in to the fire department. Karen, second Ruth. 6-0

Karen wanted to know if any of the Auburn abutters were notified, and Will said that they notified them many times. We realize that other than traffic that this should not affect any other municipality. Will had some questions. He wanted to know in terms of getting the plans signed. The conditions must be finished before it can be signed. Will said that they have received comments back from the DEP. Jean said that if there are any major changes, it may have to come back before the Board. Will also mentioned that some of the shared driveways will become separate. James said that they just need to put this minor change on the plan.

Chandler House Bed & Breakfast Site Plan Review

James read how Alton Warren and Shannon Ehrich are proposing to open a 7 guest-room bed and breakfast at 337 Intervale Road, in the Historic Lower Village. There are no additions proposed to the structures on site. They plan to renovate the existing old house into a more suitable place for a bed and breakfast. A site plan and survey is currently being prepared, as well as the septic design. Alton said the soil tests were just taken and the results would not be in for another week and a half. Shannon questioned about the sprinklers, and Jean said that they do not have to do it. Jean mentioned that this house is in the Historic overlay. She wanted to know what exactly they plan to do. Do they want larger windows and fire ladders? Alton said that he spoke with the fire chief and putting in a sprinkler system would mean that they would not have to put in ladders. Jean went on the question about the banquet hall. Alton said that whoever rented the hall would bring the food. Jean said that the Board needs to look at the parking. There is plenty of room for parking. James asked how much parking that he is thinking about right now. Alton said hopefully at least five rooms rented at a time with one car per room, plus their two cars. Jean then said they need to calculate how much parking will be needed for a banquet (approximately 1 car per 3 people). Jean said that they will need to check on the buffering with the parking. The trees will provide a great buffer in the spring and summer. Future plans consist of putting up a small barn with a few horses. Shannon said that if a window needed to be changed for the fire marshal, they could do that. Jean said that it would need to be shown on the plan to match the existing ones very closely. Parking will be put between the out building and the barn. It will actually be gravel. State any materials that are used to change anything with the house. The railings will be made to look like the existing ones. They plan to put in a small wooden sign with a couple of small lights for people to find them after dark. Alton suggested that they put the light on a timer. John asked about erosion control and if anything should be done about oil leaking from cars. Jean mentioned that it should be fine. James said that this is one reason why a buffer is placed. Jean reminded them to go to James with any questions. The Board will need to do a site walk. Shannon asked if it would be possible to keep the parking lot for the banquet hall a grassy lawn. Parking will need to be organized to allow for people to enter and exit easily. Karen said that they will need a parking plan. Jean went back to the site walk and thought the Board should wait until the snow is melted. It will be on April 16th. The Board needs plans for parking lots, changes presented for windows, buffering, and. Shannon said that they would not let the banquets run late which would cut back on traffic during the evening and night time. She then wondered if the fire marshal should walk through now, and Jean thought that would be a good idea. Jean also said that they should work directly through James.

John questioned them and this is Alton and Shannon’s first time starting a bed and breakfast. Karen suggested that they give a site map to L.L. Bean. Alton said that he has already contacted Pineland and they are very excited. Both are from the area and are very excited.

Motion: move to adjourn. Ruth, second Janet. 6-0

X__________________________

Jean Libby, Chairman

title: March 1, 2005
html:
NEW GLOUCESTER PLANNING BOARD

Minutes of March, 2005

Members Present:

Jean Libby, Chairman

Karen Asselin, Vice Chairman

James Isaacson, Town Planner

Angie Elvin, Secretary

Ruth Waterhouse

Janet Smaldon

John Sumner

Excused Absence:

Laurie Brady

Others Present:

James Vadas, Jr.

Steve Roberge


Review and Approval of Minutes for January 18, 2005

Motion: to accept minutes with corrections. Ruth, second Karen. 5-0

Review and Approve of Minutes for February 1, 2005.

Motion: to accept as written. Ruth, second John. 5-0

Clear Brook Estates Minor Subdivision

James gave a synopsis on how James Vadas, Jr. is proposing a 4-lot minor subdivision off Morse Road. James Vadas has submitted a nitrate study, performance guarantee, the revised plan that shows flood plane elevation, 25 ft. no-cut buffer, and nitrate plumes. He has also submitted a cluster scenario. Jean wanted to discuss the site walk that took place on the property and asked for any comments. She thought they were nice lots and the brook was set far enough back. Janet had a question regarding the buffering, and Jean said that Mr. Vadas has agreed to the 25 ft. no-cut buffer. Karen then asked about the fire pond issue. Jean said that he has asked for a waiver. Jim Vadas mentioned that the fire pond would be absolutely impossible because the earth is just pure sand. Karen then wondered if he could get that stated in a letter. Jim said that he had already submitted one well before his first meeting with the Board. Janet wanted to know if there were any fire ponds in the nearby area. He said that there are a couple hydrants on the Morse Road but that is it. Karen asked what he thought of the cluster, and Jim said that he would rather not go with that plan. He wanted each house to have their two acres. The test pits are all fine, and the nitrates in the well have been checked. Jean thought that the plan should say “private road”. It must be drafted like section 8.1E, “where the subdivision streets are to remain private, the following words shall appear on the recorded plan: ‘all roads in the subdivision shall remain private roads to be maintained by the developer and shall not be accepted or maintained by the town…’” Jim said that he would have it put on the plan. Jean then told Jim that any waivers, that have been approved, must be written on the plan as well. Jean mentioned that Mr. Vadas has requested waivers for the stone monuments and firepond. The Board has received a letter already for the fire pond.

Motion: to waive stone monuments and fire pond based on a letter stating that the soil will not support a fire pond. Karen, second Ruth. 5-0

Jean asked what Jim had come up with for a road name. He said that he was thinking of “Clear Brook Trail”. There is now a condition that he finalizes the name of the road.

Move: to deem application complete. Karen. Ruth. 5-0

Move: to have a Public Hearing on March 15th. Karen, Ruth. 5-0

Snow Hill Major Subdivision

Donald Leavitt is proposing to subdivide a 25.33 acres parcel on Snow Hill Road into 10 lots. Steve Roberge is the design engineer for this project. He has submitted a conceptual plan. It gives many calculations for the 10 lots. They’ve put together the two types of development styles. The first is the traditional one. They are all minimum lot size. They have had people out to do wet land analyses. The land at this point is mostly undeveloped. A cluster subdivision is the second type. There would be small road frontage and everything would be shrunk down, although that road would stay the same. This would provide for access to abutting properties for those who might want to develop on either side of the proposed plan. Jean asked if it would be built to town specifications, and Mr. Roberge said that it would be. Jean felt it would be better if some houses could extend off a common driveway. Karen had a question regarding the lot with a house already built on it. She was told that all the property belongs to someone and it has not been split up yet. Jean said that she thinks the Board will push the cluster. The other issue that needs to be changed is the driveway access that is coming off the turnaround. The road will then be extended so that the driveway comes off the road before the actual turnaround. Steve would like to submit some preliminary materials for the next meeting on this subdivision. Jean asked if the abutters have been notified yet, and Steve said no. Karen mentioned that he might need an association agreement even if he decides not to make this a public road just to handle the common space. Steve said that they probably will. There are still phosphorus issues, along with fire pond and stone water control pond issues. Jean asked if he could guarantee that there will always be water for the fire department. Mr. Roberge said that it should, yet he can not guarantee, especially should there be a drought. It will actually be designed as a permanent pool of water.

John wanted to know what type of houses would be built in there. All that Steve could say at this point is that they will be residential. More information will come at a later date, possibly the next meeting. Jean said that any public road in this town is at the will of the people. Steve believes at this point that it will be a paved road.

Ruth wanted to know what the right of ways are for. It would allow people to come in from different ways if they want, for further development. Right now it would not be a road, but it would allow for connections with future developments. Karen thought it would be a good idea to state the conditions of the right of way. Steve then stated that if it is submitted and accepted as a public road, then access to the right of way will be given to any further developers. However, if the roads remain private, then access to the right of ways would have restrictions and subsequent developers would have to join the homeowners association. Ruth said that the plan needs to say “Notes and Conditions”. Jean said the town is dealing with a new law firm, and the words might not be necessary. Steve said that this is just the beginning and a lot more will be added to the plan. Jean is much more comfortable now that the two little lots are gone. Also, the site walk will need to be postponed due to the snow and abutters must be notified that the preliminary application is coming in. Karen wanted to know the time frame on the site walk. James said that it needs to be scheduled within 30 days of today’s meeting. If the weather poses a problem, the date can be postponed. Jean then wanted to know what would happen to the open space. It will be left to the lot owners in the homeowners association. Karen suggested that a site walk be scheduled at the next meeting, whether Steve can be there or not. Jean wants the site walk to be done for the Board’s own benefit, but they can not go out until the road is flagged. Jean told Steve to put any waivers on the plan, and would need two test pits to be done for every house lot. Steve will compile everything needed into a notebook for each person on the Board. Jean then asked for any more questions. There weren’t any, and both Jean and Steve felt that everything was headed in the right direction. Mr. Roberge is hoping to be back for the first meeting in April.

Cobb’s Bridge Commons Major Subdivision – Set Public Hearing

The Hearing was set for tonight, but A & R Builders could not make it.

Motion: to reschedule the Public Hearing for March 15th. Karen, second Janet. 5-0.

Other Business

1. James gave handouts for a workshop in Augusta. It is put on by the Maine Municipal Association.

2. The Zoning Committee is working on a road plan to bring more subdivisions together. There is also a traffic study being done of the Upper Village.

3. Also, the fire ordinance is being amended to allow for a little more leeway. Janet wanted to know if the Town had the authority to say that they wanted a fire pond placed somewhere and it would be done accordingly. James said that it has never been done.

Motion: to adjourn. Ruth, second John. 5-0

X__________________________

Jean Libby, Chairman

title: February 1, 2005
html:
NEW GLOUCESTER PLANNING BOARD

Minutes of February 1, 2005

Members Present:

Jean Libby, Chairman

Karen Asselin, Vice Chairman

James Isaacson, Town Planner

Angie Elvin, Secretary

Ruth Waterhouse

Laurie Brady

Janet Smaldon

Unexcused Absence:

John Sumner

Others Present:

Jeremy Appt

George Maschino

Will Haskell

Al Fleming

Raylene Estabrook

James Vadas


The minutes were not ready to review this meeting, due to some technical errors. They will be reviewed and corrected at the next meeting.

Cobb’s Bridge Commons Major Subdivision

James gave a synopsis on the Cobb’s Bridge Commons Major Subdivision. A & R Builders would like to divide the property into 12 lots. This includes some open space, but is not a cluster subdivision. The lots range in size from 2 acres to 4.6 acres. There is 6.1 acres of open space proposed. Also, the road will be a private 50-foot right-of-way. The Board did a site walk on this in early November. It was a very complete application.

Jean asked that those speaking go to the table and give their names. She then asked for comments on the site walk. Janet thought it looked beautiful. There are existing stone walls, along with a foundation from an old building. Ruth mentioned that there are a lot of big rocks that will be used. She also thought they would be proud of this development.

Jean asked that they change the phone service of Verizon to Pine Tree. Will Haskell said that she was right and it would be changed. Karen went on to ask if a letter had been received from the Fire Chief. James has spoken with the Fire Chief and he is very favorable to using sprinklers. The Board will need a letter from the engineer asking for the waiver for the fire pond. The pond would have to be near the road and that won’t happen with the rock. It is in the best interest of the people to at least have sprinklers. The Board can only waive a fire pond if adequate evidence is submitted to prove that it can not be sustained or that a sufficient water supply exists. Jean told them that the Fire Department should not have to check and maintain the sprinklers every year. Al Fleming stated how it is in the contract of the homeowner to maintain check their own sprinklers. It will be a private road. Will feels hard pressed to get a soil specialist to tell him that the soil will not support a fire pond. He said that he would make the request. Karen feels it’s an adequate water source. Jean speculated on how the Board could be certain the sprinklers would be maintained. Will then said that he would get a letter saying that a fire pond could not be supported next to Cobbs Bridge Road. Janet wanted to know what the guide lines to the sprinklers were, and she was told that is a state thing. Will said that sprinklers are very good because they require very low maintenance.

There needs to be a note on the plan there saying that the private road will be maintained by the land owners. Jean asked if James had shown the turnaround to the Fire Chief. He has not, but Will said it does meet the requirements. Any new or change of road name has to be voted for by the Board of Selectmen. Ruth reminded Will and Al that the plans must say “Notes and Conditions”. Will said they do not have any conditions yet, but it will certainly be added when they do. The typo on the acreage will be fixed to say 36.7 acres. Jean carefully checked abutters and thought there might be a problem with lot 69 on map 10. It’s not a big deal, but something that must be done. Karen then had a question concerning the receipts that they provided. She wasn’t doubting them, but how can you tell that it is real? Jean said that hers has a stamp, and Will said they’d be happy to submit the return receipts. Jean wanted to know if the Board was going to get a cleaner copy of the Declaration of Covenants and Restrictions. Al said they are working on the final copy now. Jean asked for any questions or comments. Will wanted to add that they’ve had a pre-application meeting with MDEP on the storm water permit to discuss the approach or storm water management. As far as the wetlands go, they will be filing a NRPA tier one application. Jean said that they’ve done a great job not to disturb the wetlands, and that was their intent. She then asked if they plan on putting in the trail right away, and Al said that was the full intention. They are very limited as to what they can cut down in the open space. Dead growth may be cleaned out a little bit. James thought that a no cut buffer restriction is more than what’s really necessary. Jean asked for any additional questions. Will wanted to know about the DEP process. Does the Board need final DEP permits in hand before they can give approval? James said that it is just best to get the DEP permits ahead of time. It could change something on their plan and slow them down. Karen said as soon as they get the DEP they should be able to start as opposed to having to wait for it. The Board needs to act on a waiver request if any, and they do have one. Will wanted to know if they could request a waiver altogether for the stone monuments and Jean said that he could. Also, it would be a lot easier if their utilities went underground. They will be meeting with Pinetree soon. Jean said to make sure that there are no trees near the connection of the power lines. Al said that there is going to be a rock wall constructed to continue off the one that already exists on the neighbor’s property. James said that they are lacking the nitrate study. Jean said that the Board needed to decide if they could move forward or not.

Motion: move to deem the preliminary application complete with the nitrate study being part of that. Karen, second Laurie. 5-0

The Board was not sure if a Public Hearing should be scheduled or not. Karen felt very comfortable with it. Jean thought it was very complete and it would be fine to schedule the hearing the first meeting in March.

Motion: move to schedule the Public Hearing for March 1st. Karen, second Laurie. 5-0

Karen asked if the Board wanted a motion regarding the DEP issue. She didn’t feel it was necessary. Will said the permits won’t be in hand by March 1st, and that is why they were hoping for approval. The approval is for storm water and wetlands. Karen said if they approve the final plan, they would be able to start as soon as they get the permit.

Clear Brook Estates Minor Subdivision

James described what might possibly take place here. James Vadas is proposing to subdivide a lot on Morse Road into four lots, behind Maschino’s Lumber.

Laurie Brady had to sit out on this one because she is an abutter.

Jean said that they are trying to put four homes between to businesses. The people need to be aware of this because they both abut the property. James said that the lots are actually quite a ways from the saw mill, so that shouldn’t be a problem. There is quite a buffer. George asked if there was a sound ordinance in the town, and do they have businesses in the town that were in effect before the ordinance. Jean said that he was one of them. He wanted to know if that could somehow have an affect on things. Jim said that there is already a house on lot one that has been sold. George said that there’s not question that sound is in effect here, but it shouldn’t affect Jim’s property. The road is almost 1200 ft. off Morse Road. They will be quite a ways from George’s mill. Jean asked if there was growth between Maschino Lumber and the tip of Jim’s skinny lot. Jim said that it will buffered with trees. They need a hydro geologic nitrate study. Jim said that all four test pits showing nothing but sand. Jean said they still need the nitrate study.

Ruth wanted to know if the road has already been built. Jim said that it has only been built in to the first house lot. Ruth wanted to know if the road had to go straight in, and Jim said in order to keep the plan that it would. A site walk has been planned for Saturday morning at 8:30. Jean asked if Jim wanted to cluster, he said he’s not opposed to it, but he’d have to redo all the plans. He needs to submit an alternative plan, even if he doesn’t plan to use it. Jean said that Jim should’ve gone over things with James before coming before the Board. George had a question about if he expanded, would the Town back him up or the people who just bought residential properties. He is just very concerned for his property and business because he has every intention of growing. He should be fine, but he would have to come back before the Board should anything change. Jim said that these lots are going to be in excess of over 600 ft. from George’s property. James said that the noise regulations that New Gloucester has measures the noise decibel at the property line. George wanted to be protected from anything that would prohibit him in the future, but the Board can not do much about that. James said that if he adds more kilns, a lot of things will change. Jim said that you would never know that there is a saw mill nearby when on the property. Karen wanted to wrap up the clustering. Jim needs to at least have a plan drawn up. He could get more lots, but he would have to purchase development rights. Jim didn’t have any interest in this. He ended up asking a few more questions to reiterate what they had already gone over about the cluster, but he didn’t see any benefit in it for him. Karen said they can’t waive it. Jim just needs to give a pencil drawing of what the cluster would look like. He also needs to give the nitrate study at the next meeting. James thought the flood plane should be shown on the plan. Should any part come near the property boundaries, anyone buying a lot will be aware of it. Jean said that she would set up a Public Hearing at the next meeting concerning this. The next meeting will be on February 15, 2005. Jim’s deadline is the 8th.

Motion: to adjourn. Karen, second Ruth. 5-0

X__________________________

Jean Libby, Chairman

title: January 18, 2005
html:
NEW GLOUCESTER PLANNING BOARD

Minutes of January 18, 2005

Members Present

Jean Libby, Chairman

Karen Asselin, Vice Chairman

James Isaacson, Town Planner

Angie Elvin, Secretary

Ruth Waterhouse

John Sumner

Janet Smaldon

Excused Absence

Laurie Brady

Others Present

Reg Jacqman

Michael Jacqman

Ryan Tripp

Motion: to accept the Minutes of December, 21, 2004, with corrections. Ruth, second Karen. 4-0 (Janet-abstained)

Public Hearing-Jacqmin Greenhouse Addition Site Plan

James gave a synopsis on how Reginald Jacqmin is proposing to construct a 24’x30’ greenhouse at 41 Intervale Road, in the Village and Historic District. This is for his own use, not for commercial. He has submitted an elevation sketch with materials listed on it.

Discussion: Jean opened the public hearing at 7:33 p.m. and closed it at 7:33 p.m. She also stated that should anyone show up to the meeting with something to say about the Greenhouse, it would be reopened. Jean then said that she would like to go over the lighting a little bit more. Reginald stated that the lights would be on only until 6 p.m. Jean thinks it is very bright and wanted something for the town to be able to fall back on should any complaints come in. Reg said that they would be glad to use winter shades. Karen then suggested a 90 day trial period with no restrictions. If there is a complaint during that time, the CEO will put time restrictions on the lighting. Karen then wanted to know when he planned to build it. Reginald Jacqmin said that if he got approval from the Board, he would start this week. Jean thought that the lights being turned off at 8 p.m. was suitable. Janet wanted to know if it could possibly be linked with the sunset. Reginald then stated that he needs at least 12 hours of light. Karen thinks that there should be a limit on the time frame for complaints. Jean agreed and said that there needs to be a condition written down. The Board could give him a year. John then said that the CEO could review everything. Karen thought it would be good to give the Jacqmins a year from the date of approval. Jean said that after the year, it would be over and done with.

Motion: Condition of Approval. Move that the Board approves the application subject to the condition that if any complaints are received on the lighting in the greenhouse within the first year from the date of the approval, the Town’s Code Enforcement Officer may set reasonable limitations on the lighting. Karen, second Ruth. 5-0

Tripp’s Trading Revised Site Plan Review

James described how Ryan Tripp is proposing to revise his approved site plan by rotating the building 90 degrees and rearranging the parking, on Lewiston Road north of the Upper Village. The Parking lot runs parallel to Route 100. He plans to keep the same set backs and add buffers.

Discussion: Jean asked why he plans to do that. Ryan said that he has a lot more back land than he does front land. Karen wanted to know more. He said that it would give him more land should he want to expand later on. He said the road front would stay the same. Jean said that she was really concerned with the mess of the driveway. She didn’t see any fencing until a short time ago, and wanted to know when he planned to start this. Jean then wanted to know who was going to build it and if he had the financing for the project. Ryan said that he has his own crew to build as soon as possible and the finances are there. Karen asked about parking. Is it going to be the same amount? Mr. Tripp said yes. Jean wants to know what he plans to put in the front portion. Ryan said that it is going to be the showroom. The parking in front will be parking for cars to sell. Jean reminded him that he can only have up to 10 cars. Jean said that he needs a setback for the cars near the road. Karen said that it has already been approved once and did not see why it couldn’t be approved a second time when nothing material was changed. Jean had a problem with what has been left open during the winter. She doesn’t feel that it is a good practice of erosion. Karen asked if it would be done by May. He said that the inside should be, and the rest shortly after that. Janet didn’t remember that much parking, but it is within the guidelines. Ryan said that it won’t all be used for parking. The first fifty feet will be parking lot and the rest is a driveway. James said that he has plenty of frontages. Jean said that the ditches need to stay. There will be a 5 foot buffer for cars on his side of the ditch. Janet wanted to know if he was going to double tier the 10 cars, using the 90 feet. Jean then said that he needed to be 15 feet from the road. Karen wanted to know if the Board could limit the time frame on this. James said that they should maintain the time frame of the original approval. It would need to be substantially complete, although the site work can’t be done until the weather clears. A limit should be put down. Jean thought that 3 months was good. She also said that he needs to work with James to find a way to prevent stuff from running off the site in the spring (by using seed and mulch). Ryan said that loam isn’t going to spread very good until it really warms up, but Jean said she’s not concerned about that yet. Something just has to be done about the runoff. The Board needs a letter of credit about it being done by May 26th. Also, the Board is going to stay within the year and extend it 30 days. Jean then asked for any concerns from the rest of the Board. John wanted to know about the runoff to the road by changing the building 90 degrees. Ryan said that it will be a lot better. Jean said that he needs good drainage. Any runoff must stay on the site. He could use crushed rock. She said that the new date will be July 1st. Janet wanted to know if there was anything that Ryan could do prior to April 15th, and James said that there was. James said that he and Debbie would take a look at the site and let Ryan know what could be done before hand. Janet said that there should be something for temporary thaw and erosion. Ryan should meet with James and the CEO before any building commences. Jean said that there are a lot of things that can not be done before the thaw because of the runoff. The Board will hold him to the completion date which is set to July 1st. A 15 foot buffer must be set and a letter of adequate financing be given to James. Vote: 5-0

Motion to Adjourn: Ruth, second Karen. 5-0

_______________________________________________________________________

X________________________________

Jean Libby, Chairman

title: December 21, 2004
html:
NEW GLOUCESTER PLANNING BOARD

Minutes of December 21, 2004

Members Present

Jean Libby, Chairman

Karen Asselin, Vice Chairman

James Isaacson, Town Planner

Angie Elvin, Secretary

Ruth Waterhouse

John Sumner

Laurie Brady

Unexcused Absence

Janet Smaldon

Others Present

Linda Chase

Tim Nolan

Keith Morse

Wayne Wood

Paul Pietropauli

Matt Trudel

Roger St. Pierre

Norm Groleau

Reg Jacqman

Michael Jacqman

Review and approval of Minutes for November 16, 2004. (The December 7th meeting was cancelled.)

Motion: to approve minutes with correction. Karen, Ruth second. 5-0

Discussion: Ruth gave suggestions for corrections. The Board announced that Don Mendell has resigned.

Jordan Field Subdivision

James gave a synopsis on how this is a 9 lot subdivision. They have submitted one copy of a conventional two acre lot scenario.

Discussion: Jean said that some Board members had done a site walk on the property before and wondered if there were any comments. Karen said that a fire pond waiver will be wanted. Jean said that they need to put everything in writing. Test pits- they are so close, does it run from one hole to the other? Jean really felt that was pushing it. Jean told him that the setting of the test pits was awful and asked that he strongly relay how displeased she was with it to the person who created them. Wayne said that he would pass that on. Jean wanted to know if lots 3 & 4 were coming off the turn around. She was told that if allowed to, they would be. Jean then asked Wayne if it was going to be a town road or a private road. He told her that as of right now it is a private road. Lot 3 can have a driveway long before the turn around. James said that if they plan on changing it to a town road, the turn around must be a t-hammer head with no driveways coming off of it. Karen was then asked to read a letter of concern

******* I was not given the letter to put in these minutes. Revisions will be made when I receive it at the next meeting and corrections are being made. Thank you!

Jean stated that the people buying the lots need to be aware that they are next to an active farm. Wayne said that what other towns have been doing is telling them in bold print on parcel concerned. Jean said that if you see the farm with snow now, you don’t realize what it really is. Karen wanted to know if the layout is shown. Wayne then said that any real estate agent is supposed to disclose that information. Jean then asked if that was true and she was told “yes”. Jean said that it says Gillespie Farms, but October Corporation actually owns it. An attorney named Paul then got up to represent October Corporation which is the owner of the land. They do business with Pineland Farms under the name of Gillespie Farms. Wayne suggested that they put Gillespie Farms in quotations to let everyone know that it an active farm under that name. Jean said that they should add that to the plan. She also said that she noticed a small portion (lot 38) was owned by Blueberry Acres Corporation. Wayne is responsible to let them know what is going on here. Paul said that the property at the southwest labeled McDonald is also part of October Corporation. Jean said that the waivers that have been requested were concerning stone monuments. Wayne had a question as to why anything set along the road is intended to be granite monuments. Jean clearly state that is what the ordinance says at this time.

James said some points are required to be stone and others iron pins. Along the roadways is required to be stone. The underground utilities are already partly above ground. They would much rather use poles than have to dig trenches. The only waiver would be from the road to pole 521. The following items are lacking: indication of water supply, open space restrictions, any covenants or deed restrictions on these lots, and hydro-geological study. James said that it just came in, and Jean said that it would be talked about tonight. She also said that she did not want to do anything about the fire pond at this time. It will not be addressed until there is more information from the applicant. Jean then asked for any questions or comments. Karen wanted to know about the stone monuments. Jean said that they should wait on that subject.

Motion: to waive stone monuments and also to waive underground utilities up to pole 52.1. Anything after that will be underground. Karen, Laurie second. 5-0

Discussion: Ruth wanted to clarify what was happening with the underground utilities. Jean then said that he is lacking quite a few items and does not feel that this is ready for a public hearing. The road needs to be engineered, a maintenance agreement submitted, notification of water supply given, and other things need to be submitted as well. James said that there can not be a public hearing until everything is presented to the Board.

Jacqmin Greenhouse Site Plan

James gave a synopsis on how Reggie Jacqmin is proposing to construct a 720 sq. ft. greenhouse on his property, adjacent to the garage. There are already a couple other green houses on his property. He lives at 41 Intervale Road, in the Historic District.

Discussion: Jean wanted to know if there would be bright lights at night that might possibly disturb neighbors. Reggie told her that any lights would only be on until 9 p.m. at which time they would be shut off. His vegetables need large quantities of light, but any lights would flood only the area of the green house. John wanted to know where exactly his house was located and he was told it was up near the corner, where a lot of construction is going on across the street. James said that they have submitted photos and the plans for the green house. The gardening is only for home use. Reggie said that it has been a hobby for him for the past 50 years. Jean asked if there were any questions. Karen thought that all the items listed except for exterior materials are able to be waived. Jean then wanted to know what he planned to do for erosion control. Reggie said that he needed something to retain the loam and uses PVC to get drained water. The lights will be used on days with fewer hours of light. Jean is not sure how much light will flood the neighbors. Karen thought this was something the Board might want to consider having a public hearing on. Jean thought so too, in order to make the neighbors aware of what is going on. Reggie said that very little of the actual green house will be seen. It’s blocked on most sides. Michael said that it is pretty bright across the street. Jean said that the town can not stop someone from putting up a light outside their house. Jean asked for a waiver. Reggie said the style is about the same as the other one they have.

Motion: to deem application complete subject to receiving a list of materials and plans for landscaping around the green house. Karen, Ruth second. 5-0

Discussion: John then asked if there would be loud fans. Reggie said they do have fans, but they are not noisy at all. You would need to be up close to hear it.

Motion: move to have a public hearing on January 18th. Karen, second Ruth. 5-0

Groleau Garage Addition Site Plan

James stated how Normand Groleau is proposing to construct 30’x40’ garage on his leased property at 121 Outlet Road.

Discussion: Jean wanted to know first off how they plan to get to the garage if the driveway stops long before the actual building. Roger told her how it would be a grassy path that would actually stay grass. Karen wanted to know how they would get to it in the winter. Do they plan to plow? Normand said that it would be used to store belongings over the winter because he is not here during that season. It will be used for storage. Karen wanted to know about the concrete they are planning to remove. Normand checked with the lady of Cumberland soil erosion and everything was fine. Karen asked if the area should be viewed by the board. Jean said that both Ruth and she had been to this property before. Laurie said that Debbie has been out there before and didn’t feel it was necessary to go. John wanted to know where the bay doors would be. Normand said that they would be on the right side. Jean asked who the property is leased from and Normand said that it was from the Shakers.

Motion: that Board does a site walk between now and the next meeting to review the property and take a look at the proposed location of the garage. 2 (Karen & John) – 3 (Jean, Laurie, & Ruth)

Discussion: Karen said that there are waivers on the storm water management.

Motion: move to waiver survey plan and two foot contours. Karen, Ruth second. 5-0

Discussion: Roger said that water run off will go towards the back of the lot and nowhere near the lake.

Motion: to deem the application complete. Karen, Laurie second. 5-0

Discussion: Ruth thought it would be a good idea for them to use of crushed stone. That’s what they normally ask of those living on the lake. Roger thought that the crushed stone would do a very good job.

Motion: move to waive the public hearing. Karen, Ruth second. 4-1 (John)

Motion: move to approve the application subject to the use crushed stone instead of the gutters. Karen, Ruth second. 5-0

Bailey Farm Minor Subdivision

James explained how Douglas McAtee is proposing a 3-lot minor subdivision on Sabbathday Road (the Old Route 26). This is a three lot subdivision on 6 ½ acres. One lot is an old farm house (in the middle). The other lot needs to be split in two pieces. They want to make lot 1 a commercial lot, but that will need to be stated on the deed. They did submit the ground water study, and because it’s proposed to be a commercial lot, the study should be revised. James said that he will get a list of the commercial uses permitted in that zone. This should reflect it.

Discussion: Jean said that this would need to come back before the Board. James said yes. It would then be a Site Plan Review. Matt Trudel is representing Doug McAtee. The Board still needs to see the deed to confirm who owns the lot. Jean said they still need the verification of right, title, and interest. Also, an indication of a water supply is needed. Matt said it should be there. Jean needs verification from a well driller even though she knows there is plenty of water over there. A letter of adequacy is needed. Jean also said that the fire pond needs to be addressed. Matt said that because this lot is going to be commercial, they planned to put in a sprinkler system. Jean mentioned the phosphorus study. James asked if there was a brook or drainage area behind lot 1. Matt thought that there was. James said that someone had a concern about the large drainage area and how wet it would be. Jean wants answers from the next person who represents Bailey Farm. Karen suggested that everything be present at next meeting to quickly move forward with it. Matt wanted a public hearing, but Jean wanted to go over all information first. The Board needs to take into consideration the wetlands. He needs to get the deed and Matt said that he would.

Briarwood Estates Major Subdivision

James gave a synopsis on how Fortin Construction is proposing a revision to the Open Space agreement with the NG Little League, per recommendation from the DEP.

Discussion: James said how the NG Little League may construct another ball field if they like. Jean read it as open space and it would remain open space. Karen said that the declarence at this point is Fortin Construction. If there’s a problem, the land would go to the people who own the property. James read it that should Little League fold thirty years from now, it will revert to Fortin Construction. Tim said that homeowners can not benefit from or have interest in the open space reverting back to the property. Karen wanted to know why they can not have an interest in it. Tim said that it is a DEP rule. Karen wanted to know what Fortin would do with it. Jean said it could be given to a land trust. Should anything happen, it will come back to the Board for review. Jean asked Linda Chase to stand up and voice what Little League thinks about this. Linda said that Little League and their attorneys will accept all plans made. Maintenance of the conservation easement will be corrected and given to the Board.

Motion: move to accept the changes. Karen, John second. 5-0

Public Hearing Opened at 8:55 p.m.

Public Hearing Closed at 8:56 p.m.

Other Business

TDR passed by 4 votes

Next meeting will be held on January 18, 2005. (Due to being short of staff)

Motion: to adjourn. Karen, John second. 5-0

X_____________________________

Jean Libby, Chairman

title: November 16, 2004
html:
NEW GLOUCESTER PLANNING BOARD

Minutes of November 16, 2004

Members Present

Jean Libby, Chairman

Karen Asselin, Vice Chairman

James Isaacson, Town Planner

Angie Elvin, Secretary

Ruth Waterhouse

Janet Smaldon

Members Absent

John Sumner

Donald Mendell

Laurie Brady

Others Present

Linda Chase

Tim Nolan

Don Fortin

Robert J. Cole

Keith Morse

Doug McAtee

Darrell Flanders

Mark Norton

Pat Norton

Troy Bauder

Tom Blake

Illegible

Motion: to approve the Minutes for November 2, 2004, with corrections. Ruth, second Karen. 4-0

Public Hearing – Briarwood Estates Major Subdivision

James gave a synopsis on the 23-lot subdivision on the Penney Rd. It is near the ball field.

Discussion: Jean asked his to go over the remaining items. He said that Gary has seen the fire pong and it is acceptable. The detention basin on Lot 1 has been revised. James had a concern on how the pond is going to be drained on the property abutting the drive. He talked to the engineer and it should be okay. Also, there is a defined wetland path through the lot and there’s a slower rate of discharge. James is concerned on whether or not it will increase the wetlands. He said that there’s no way to redirect it anywhere else. After speaking with the engineers, he believes that the rate of discharge will be quite a bit less. Jean asked if it meets the ordinance requirements, and James said yes. She then asked if there was any way that it could be made better, and James said no. Keith said he feels they are improving it a lot. They’re digging a ditch to control the runoff and concentrate it to the corner. They are doing their best, are well with in the law, and think it will really benefit the people who buy the land. Karen then mentioned how things were okay with the DEP. Jean asked that Linda be given the Briarwood’s Finding of Fact to read 11.2. it says, “Retention of Open Spaces, Buffers and Vegetated Areas and Natural or Historic Features. 32+ acres of open space will be permanently preserved through a conservation easement and owned by the New Gloucester Little League. Janet had a question as to why they are getting all 32 acres. Jean told her that there’s a possibility of another ball field going in. Janet was just concerned with the maintenance and what would need to be taken care of. It’s to remain open said Jean. Don Fortin made it clear that whatever Little League chooses to create, it must maintain. Jean mentioned that they will be limited as to what they can put in such as dugouts and a snack shack.

Then Karen wanted to know the impact on the schools. Don had called and got nothing. James had called his office and left information for Don, but he did not receive it. Jean just wants figures on the road. Karen then brought up how the Board knows that there’s a minimal impact on trash and other services. James said that it is hard to know exactly what everything will be. Jean did say that the average house does not pay for its services.

Public Hearing for Briarwood Estates: Open 7:55p.m.

Troy Bauder owns property nearby and is concerned as to where the storm water is going to go. Keith got up to show him on the plans how the proposed ditch would reduce the running water. Troy was also concerned for his neighbor, Mike Johnson, who owns property close by. Karen believes that it’s state law that you can not adversely impact another person’s property when doing a development, and Jean said the town has that at well. Mr. Morse said that Mr. Fortin does not take all of this lightly and they have improved the situation for the Johnson family. Troy understands how they’re doing things and agreed with it. He also wanted to know when the drainage ditch would be put in. Keith said that will still need to be excavated and they’re not too sure yet when it will be done. Troy said he was comfortable with what was said, but wanted to know about work hours and noise times allowed in New Gloucester. James stated that the quiet hours of anything abutting a residence is 8p.m. – 6 a.m. Jean then asked if there was anything else.

Tom Blake got up. He lives on Penney Road, across from Briarwood Estates. He was curious about the calculations that show that there’s enough water for the fire departments reservoir. Don said there’s a gallon requirement that they should be able to obtain, and they plan to have three to four times the minimum. Tom then wanted to know about possible seepage. Mr. Fortin does not think they’ve done any calculations on the elevation. Tim then said that they are going above the required amount on elevation, and Don is quite confident that they’ll see less water than originally thought. Keith said that they might need to blast ledge for depth in order to make plenty of room for draining water. Tom then went on to talk about the concern in site distance for the roadway and being just below the hill. Not many people will go the set 35mph. Jean thought the Planning Board might want to consider putting up a sign letting people be aware of the development nearby. Mr. Blake also wanted to move the set backs to their original 50 feet. Jean said they’ve already waived that situation and wanted to possibly add to the buffer. Don said add to the buffer that trees only need to be cut for site distance. Tom asked if the buffer was 25 feet, and Don explained how they were doing their best with the buffer. Jean asked where Tom’s driveway was and found out that it is right across from lot 22. Karen asked if he considered buying that lot and he said that he had originally. Jean asked if there were any more questions. There were not.

Public Hearing: Closed 8:15p.m.

Discussion: Jean said there’s a no cut buffer on lot’s 21 & 22, and asked for comments from the Board.

Motion: as a condition of approval for this there by a no 20 feet cut buffer on lots 21 & 22 with the exception of trees needed to be cut for site distance. Also, that there be put a sign on Penney Road letting people know about the private road. Karen, second Janet 4-0

(Ruth wanted to vote against until things were explained to her again)

Discussion: Jean asked for any information from the DEP. Don said they have not heard back yet, and it could take 6 to 8 weeks. He was hoping they could move on with the condition. Karen said they couldn’t make it conditional with out knowing the impact on the schools.

Motion: to deem the application complete subject to receiving the final DEP approval on the storm water plan, conservation easement, and also receiving of the letters regarding the impacts. Karen, second Janet. 3-1(Ruth)

Discussion: Jean wanted to know what the Board is waiting for from the DEP. James told her they’re waiting for the storm water management plan approval and the other is the acceptance of the open space agreement-that they accept being a third party to the conservation easement. It’s a requirement. Don knows they can not proceed without approval. Tim said they’ve been submitting forms and have yet to submit a final form. Jean wanted to know if Linda Chase was satisfied and she was. Keith, Don, and Tim all felt confident that things were going to work out fine. Jean asked for comments. Then she wondered about the schools, taxes, and services. James said it was a $1.30 per linear foot of road. Karen thought that the Board was supposed to notify the schools and police about the subdivision going in. James said that there is a lot of change going on in the town and it’s hard to tell them anything without knowing the impacts. New Gloucester doesn’t have local police and this won’t change our contract with the county police. Jean said the do need to contact the school though. She also said that Briarwood needs to be limited to the sale of 4 lots until all the required improvements and roads complete is complete or other guarantees are submitted and accepted by the Board.

Motion: to approve based on the findings James has along with the numbers calculated. Move to approve to the conditions talked about. Karen, second Janet. 3-1(Ruth)

Discussion: Keith wanted to know about the limiting of 4 lots. James said that is only until all improvements along with everything else has been submitted.

Public Hearing – Colex, LLC Garage and Office Site Plan

Jean mentioned that the Board has done a site walk on this property. James gave a synopsis on how Sundance Properties is proposing to construct an office and garage facility for an excavating business on the New Route 26 (Maine Street). He saw that they’ve shifted their plans a little to work more with the zoning. They are proposing a fire pond with a dry hydrant.

Discussion:Jean asked for any comments. Janet thought it is really important that the entrance to the facility be line up opposite with the old Route 26. Mr. Cole said that all the field planners are in agreement that this is the proper place for the property. Janet wondered if there should be flashing light as opposed to a stop sign at the end of the old Route 26. Mr. Cole said that the state already regulates the traffic flow and will know what is sufficient. Jean was concerned with how people will be able to enter his drive, and Mr. Cole said that it’s not very hard once you are used to it. Ruth wanted to know if it is really wide enough for a tractor trailer truck, and he said that it was. Jean thanked him for all his information and for working with the Board on any requirements. Mr. Cole now needs to check with the code enforcement officer to go over the plans. Karen asked about the fire pond. James said the chief has seen this and it is acceptable. Mr. Cole said he plans to have at least 10 feet of water in the pond at all times.

Public Hearing for Coles, LLC: Opened at 8:55p.m.

Darrell Flanders owns a junk yard nearby. How much are you planning to use? Mr. Cole said they have about 60 acres and will only be using the little corner that he indicated to Darrell. Mr. Flanders then wanted to know if they will be using a stone crusher, and Mr. Cole said they do plan to remove some ledge. Darrell said that he wanted to know if they would be using it on a routine basis, and he was told that that is not in the plans at this point. Jean asked what he meant by that, and he said that they may be to remove more ledge again at some point, but it will not be a gravel pit. Mr. Flanders said that he has no problem with this, and he’s just glad that they will not be using a stone crusher all the time.

Public Hearing Closed: 8:57p.m.

Discussion: Karen wanted to know if there were any waiver requests. Jean said that Mr. Cole is all set.

Motion: to determine the application complete subject to the final DOT approval of the entrance. Karen, second Janet.

Discussion: Mr. Cole was concerned that could take months because it’s a very slow process. James said that he could go ahead with the wooden structure and would need to wait before proceeding with the steel structure. James then said that the motion should be changed from “deem the application compete” to “a condition of approval.”

Amended Motion: move to deem the application complete subject to the still unknown. 4-0

Motion: move to approve the application with the condition that the entrance not be constructed until the final DOT approval of the entrance has been received. If it’s not approved, he would need to come back to the Board with the plans. Karen, second Ruth. 4-0

Discussion: Mr. Cole wanted to know if it was DOT or DEP. Jean said the is was DOT.

Bailey Farm Minor Subdivision

Douglas McAtee is proposing a 3-lot minor subdivision on the Old Route 26, near Buddy’s Store.

James asked Douglas McAtee to give the synopsis. He said he came for a sketch plan and brought all the requirements. They scheduled a site walk and the Board had asked for two more plans to be submitted (wet land mapping and contour lines) and they just got them done. Jean had a concerned about there being a lot of wetland. Doug said that there is a house on one of the lots. He sold two of the lots as one, made an agreement that when he got his lot subdivided, he would go back and buy one of the lots back for $1. The other man is has already started building and he does not know how that has been able to happen. Mr. McAtee said that the lot with a lot of water runoff has very good gravel and should be okay. Karen stated that the man building his house is not dealing with a subdivision yet, and will not until Doug gets his subdivision all set. James asked Doug about poorly drained soil. Doug said again that there is good ground soil and any wetlands are due to water runoff from the hill. James then said that they normally consider if there are wetlands, it is due to poorly drained soil. He thinks a net residential acreage calculation is needed, because he is very concerned about lot 3. Karen said they need to review lot 3 although the man already has a building permit. Doug said that he would do the net residential calculations on both of them. He then said he’s coming through two sales to create a subdivision. Jean is concerned about the ground water, and James said that he would need a nitrate study. Jean then said that he would need to address the fire pond. Doug asked if the Town really needed one more fire pond to try to maintain when there’s one nearby. Karen said that he would need to show that the soil is not adequate to hold a fire pond. Jean asked if was going underground or above ground for power. Doug said above ground. The utilities are already there because the three entrances are on Route 26. Karen said they need the history of sale, and Doug thought they had that. Jean said he must have it, but Doug said he does not own any of it yet. Jean then asked how he can possibly do this then if he doesn’t own it. He said he would explain again. The farmhouse is sold and the other two lots were sold as one and he has an agreement to buy one of the lots back for $1. Doug said the he is the representative on the application. He was told by Karen that they would need to see the man’s the deed. Doug thought they would have it. Jean said that she has the whole purchase and sale agreement in front of her. For proof, the Board needs to see that the man owns the land. Doug has a copy of the contract to be able to buy it back for $1, and he said that he could get the signature. Mr. Homequest is the one going through subdivision, not Mr. McAtee. Karen said the Board needs verification of right, title, and interest. Jean said they also need an indication of water supply. Doug wanted to know if there’s anything he will need besides the deed. Jean said he’ll need permission to be the representative. James said they’ll need to know his legal interest in this land. Doug said that he will get this right back to the Board. Karen then wanted to know if he comes back if the Board will potentially deem it complete and have a public hearing. Doug that tonight was supposed to be the public hearing. James said that he’ll be notified of when the public hearing would be. Doug was hoping that the Board might overlook the public hearing due to it being such a small subdivision. Karen said they generally do public hearings. Doug just needs to get all the things required by the Board.

Motion: to adjourn. Ruth, second Karen. 4-0.

Motion: to accept the minutes of October 14, 2004, with corrections. Ruth, second Karen. 5-0

Motion: to move to send TDR ordinance with changes to the Board of Selectmen. Karen, second Janet. 5-0

Briarwood Estates

James gave a synopsis on how Fortin Construction is proposing a 23-lot cluster subdivision on the Penny Road. Since last time, the Board requested a peer review to be done on the ground water assessment and nitrate impact study. The results showed that the ground water assessment was adequate although there were questions on the nitrate study.

Discussion: Jean said that one of the other open items was the conservation easement. Mr. Fortin has come to an agreement with Little League. She also asked that they add open septics to the open space, because a cluster requires two. If a private collection septic system is proposed for a single family cluster development, the applicant must show that at least one designated spot on each lot has adequate soils and suitable land for subversive waste disposal for each lot in accordance with Maine State Plumbing Code and that a second designated site on this parcel has sized location and soil characteristics of this system as the one originally proposed. Keith wanted to know if this was something that could be waived, but it could not. Jean said to just add “open septics” and it should be fine. Karen had a question on the conservation easement. “At any time of substantial improvement…” Don stated that they put that there in order to leave room for a little flexibility. Karen then asked James if they were to propose that, would the zoning ordinance cover it or not. James told everyone that any improvements made on open space needs to be brought before the Planning Board. Karen asked that Don just site more specifics. It was decided that they would site this part of the ordinance: 5.1.7 D1F. Karen then wanted to know that if after five years and there’s no more Little League, it reverts back to you (Don) or to the home owners and it has to be kept as a recreational facility. Don said they didn’t specify but just stated that it would revert back. Karen said to just let it revert back to the land owners without specifications at to what must be done with it. Tim then said that the covenant and restrictions must be part of that. Jean wanted to know about the Little League part. If the Little League in New Gloucester is gone, would it be the Town’s right to vote as to what would happen to the property? Kevin Sullivan then stood up to say that the way the Little League is affiliated with New Gloucester, should it fold for any reason, the equipment would revert back to the town. Little League itself does not own any land so this is new territory. What would happen to open space if it folded? That decision has not been set and it’s something that needs to be made. They still have five years to figure that out. Karen said that either way, it reverts back. She also said that in paragraph 4 they need to change it to say, “New Gloucester Little League, lot owner’s of Briarwood Estates…” Jean was trying to make sure that this is protecting people that need to be protected. If this goes back to the association, there’s nothing to keep them from kicking the Town out once the ball field is finished. Don asked if the Board wanted it to first revert back to the Town. Jean was not sure. The Town should have first say, but the Board has to be careful because it’s a tax payer’s issue. Don said that they could add that the Town has the option of voting to accept it and then revert back. Tim said that everything has to be approved. James noticed a few errors but said that he would send them on later. Jean thanked Linda for all her work. Jean said the next issue was fire pond and road maintenance. Don wasn’t sure about the fire ponds. James said that the Town has a separate easement used to maintain the area around the pond. James said that he would fax the information. Jean said that sections under 8.2 would have to be done. One is a list of construction cost and other estimates. Don, Tim, and Keith would have to contact James on how this is going to be done. The Board needs to know what it’s going to cost the schools with buses, etc. Don is going to work with James on the estimates. Jean went on to talk about the location of the fire pond. James said that the Fire Department has not yet been shown the location. Karen had another question on the road maintenance agreements. How do you plan to maintain the road if all the lots aren’t sold? Don said that he would maintain it, along with those who occupy the lots. Each will join the agreement as they move in. Don is willing to amend the document to make it clearer. Each home owner must sign the agreement for road maintenance when they receive their deed. James want to know about the performance guarantee. Don, Tim, and Keith have four to choose from. They just need to submit one that meets the standards of the ordinance and will be accepted by the Town.

Also, make sure they add the septics along with the wells for open spaces. James will get the fire pond information to the Fire Department.

James gave a synopsis on how Wade Trudel is proposing a 9-lot cluster subdivision on 23 acres on the Mayall Road, adjacent to Gillespie Farms. There is an existing house on lot number one, which consists of four acres. The rest of the lots will each be one acre.

Discussion: Jean said that one thing the Board has to have is a better layout of the plan, as requested in the ordinance. James said that the ordinance is meant to help them see the benefit of a cluster. It is not required, but suggested. Jean asked if Wade planned on making the road a public one, because if he did, he would need an engineer’s input. Mr. Trudel was okay with that. Jean mentioned the fire pond issue. Colex, LLC Garage and Office Facility Site Plan Review

James gave a synopsis on how Colex, LLC is proposing to locate their excavation business and construct a garage and offices on the new Route 26 near the Gray line. They’re proposing to do this in two phases. 1600ft. wooden structure this year and the steel structure next year.

Discussion: Karen asked about who was getting the gravel from excavation site. It sounded to her like it was the same site. Mr. Cole said that she was correct. All that he wanted at this point was a permit. Sundance Properties (he owns both Sundance and Colex) will lease the property to Colex. He was asked if any work would be done on the trucks at the property and Jean said that he would need a contract with a waste oil company for disposal purposes. Jean is concerned about this garage being over the aquifer. She then asked about the wash water. James told Robert Cole that a water cleansing system would be needed for the washing water. Jean asked about how bright the sign will be and what sort of lighting will be used. Robert stated that the sign and lights will not affect drivers or near by houses. Jean wanted to know if he planned on putting in a fire pond. Mr. Cole likes to contain water runoff, and he like the idea of a pond. He agreed that there will be a pond put in for the use of the Fire Department and Jean said that she wants the fire pond to be good for both Robert and the Fire Department. Mr. Cole said that there will be a storm water management control structure on the outside of the pond, but the final design is not done yet complete. Jean wanted to know the height of the garage. Mr. Cole said approximately 20’ (one story). What about zone lines and set backs Jean wanted to know. They need to be marked. The Board needs an erosion control plan, septic design, and an indication of your water supply. She asked if there were any more questions. Also, the public hearing is optional. James wanted to know if the storm plan B be completed by the next meeting? Mr. Cole said it would be. Jean then asked if there were any comments on the public hearing. Karen recommended having a meeting. Mr. Cole has applied to the state for permission to route to the new Route 26 due to limited access. He has only one access. Discussion: Jean said there are no waivers. Mr. Cole needs to notify the abutters. He said he would like to waiver anything he could although it was not in writing. Set backs would not be waived anyway said Jean. She asked Robert to work through James with all that he needed to do. Jean also said that the Board needs an agreement for oil pickup, and elevations for the building need to be put of the plan.

Cobbs Bridge Road Subdivision- Pre-application Sketch

James gave a synopsis on how A & R Builders is proposing a 12-lot subdivision with open space on the Cobbs Bridge Road at the Town line with Auburn. They have submitted two scenarios and prefer the conventional 2 acre lots as opposed to a cluster. The open space is along Royal River at the far end of the plots.

Discussion: Al said that they’re hoping to address the fire pond situation with sprinklers instead. Jean said that she’s sure they’re aware that there’s nothing in the ordinance that said that they can not do that. Al believes that this will benefit the homeowner more in the long run. Will thinks that the soil would be able to support a pond. One of the challenges with the site is its slopes. Trying to fit the pond in would be much more challenging. Karen and Jean wanted to know if it would be a public or private road. Al said that right now they are leaning towards a private road, but are considering going half and half. Will said that the front half of the parcel has a 60’ right of way where as the back has a 50’ right of way. Grade wise, Will believes they are approaching 10 with the 10% maximum slope on private and 8% on minor. They are certainly trying to hold to the standard, and Jean said that the Board is unable to waive the grade. Any road that is going to be presented to the Selectmen as a road has to be engineered. Ruth asked if they would have to have a turnaround and Jean said yes. Jean and Ruth also said that they would need to have general notes and conditions. Will reminded the Board that it is only a pre-application. Will said that there a two “T” turnarounds. Utilities are underground said Will. Jean stated that the open space will be owned by the land owners. They would prefer not to shrink down to one acre lots. There are some really nice level plots. Will asked about the soil survey requirements. Is the high intensity survey required? James said no. Only the medium is required. James doesn’t think that they’ll have a problem with the soil because he knows where the bad soil is in New Gloucester. Jean said that the Board needs to know how adequate the water supply is, and whether or not it can support all 12 houses. It must be submitted by a well driller. Al said with the standard two acre, lot number one becomes a much better lot as opposed to how it would be with a cluster. They believe the houses will be in the $400,000 and $450,000 range. The Fire Department maintains hydrant and line. The fire pond would be maintained by the land owner. Will said that fire ponds aren’t even allowed in his town and they have to use sprinklers.

Board needs to sign the Webb Minor Subdivision Plan

NEW GLOUCESTER PLANNING BOARD

Minutes of October 14, 2004

Public Hearing: Transfer of Development Rights

Members Present

Jean Libby, Chairman

Ruth Waterhouse

James Isaacson, Town Planner

Karen Asselin, Vice Chairman

John Sumner

Janet Smaldon

Angie Elvin, Secretary

Excused Absence

Laurie Brady
