Others Present

Dawn Herrick

Dave Sawyer

Ann Thaxter

Cotheal Linnell

Pamela E. Slye

Bruce Bridgham

Wayne Bridgham

David Clark

Alice Waterman

Ellie Fellers

B. Haskell

Owen Haskell

Illegible

Deb Cluchey

Jeremy Willis

Joseph Barth

Dianne Barth

Don Libby, Zoning Committee

Discussion: Jean opened up and asked James to give more information and a synopsis on the TDR Zones here in New Gloucester. It’s a land use tool that will allow the people to preserve certain areas in the town. Land owners are able to sell their development rights to someone else. Their land will be kept undeveloped forever. People in the blue zone on the map are able to purchase these rights because they’re in the receiving zone. It will allow development rights to be transferred from one part of the town to the other. Those with large tracts of land will be able to preserve it and still have economic benefits.

Article 9 from Ordinance implements this program. It gives the framework of how things must be done. Procedure: An application for TDR must be filled out by the landowner of an eligible sending site. Everything must be based on the submitted plot plan. Should you choose to proceed with TDR, you must submit the following: documentation of a title search on the property, a draft conservation easement covering the portion of land proportionate to the number of transferable development rights being severed from the land and available for transfer, and a survey of the property.

The qualifications for those within the sending zone consist of: minimum of 10 acres in common ownership, use of the land for active agriculture, animal husbandry, forestry and farming, and at least one development right exists based on the net residential density for the property.

Qualifications for those outside the sending zone will need: a minimum of 10 acres in common ownership, used for active agriculture or animal husbandry, for a minimum of 5 years immediately preceding an application for TDR.

Land owners will now know how many developments they have to sell.

Public Questions:

Cotheal Linnell: wanted to know how much it costs to print the brochure and send them out to the town. James said that it’s $3000 for the letter and $400 for postage. She asked where the funds come from, and he said it’s taken out of the TIF funds for the growth of New Gloucester. Ms. Linnell also stated that she researched and saw that Cape Elizabeth and Brunswick have dropped their TDR, and was concerned that New Gloucester’s isn’t going to work. James stated that the TDR can be successful, and he was heard saying, “We believe it will work.” We have an incentive and they do not.

Ann Thaxter: Heard that this would be a way for land owners to lower their tax costs. James told everyone that there would be some tax savings, but not very significant ones. Ann then asked about larger tracts of property. Tree growth is the lowest it can go, James told her. Then Ms. Thaxter wanted to know if James had looked at the number of eligibility in both zones. James said that there are more TDR than can be in the area. Not everyone is going to want to do this. We want to limit the growth area. There are about 7,000 transferable development rights. The Town can receive just under 3,000 of them. Ann said without looking at the receiving area, she is concerned how the growth is going to be controlled. Some areas are obviously not 10 acres. She thinks it would be interesting to figure out on the map where the bigger growth can happen. Also, the only places she’s seen TDRs are places with public water and sewage. James made it clear that a limit has been put on the number of TDRs and people will be restricted on the amount they can have. There has been an aquifer check. There could’ve been an issue on Chandler Mill Road and Bennett Road had it been at full capacity, but that has all been worked out. Places with impacts, such as these two roads, will be spread out more. Ann then asked about a developer going through the process of proposals of TDRs-Do they go through the Planning Board for that? James said that they would have to, and will be required to do a full nitrate study. Planning Board has the option to deny, but would rather ask the person to just reduce. Don Libby had a question for Ann. She had stated concern about the blue area, and he wanted her to expound on that. She is concerned about Route 100, curb corners, and sight distance. If you’re doubling cars coming on roadways, you need to be careful.

Owen Haskell: Is the blue area currently zoned for two acres lots? Yes, although the village zones consists of one acre zones. Owen asked about making ½ acre lots, and Jean said that they do not want to do that and she said that the Planning Board has never gone below an acre. Then Owen asked if the Town has any numbers of taxes that would compare with zones, such as tree growth. James said that tree growth is the lowest it can go.

Jeremy Willis: wondering about the tax treatment of costs or revenues from treating TDRs. Is the money he spends added to the tax process? Added or deducted? James said that he’s not sure, and Mr. Willis said that he would look it up. Jean said that would be an accounting/tax type issue. James said that purchasing a development in the blue zone does increase the value of their land for a development. Karen thought that it would be included in the basis of the property and thinks it’s an interesting question.

Pamela E. Slye: What do you mean by multi-family? James defined it as three or more family units. Ms. Slye wanted to know about sending and receiving plots being 10 acres. Is that 1-10 acre plot or collective of 5 here and 5 there? She was told by James that they must be contiguous.

Karen then had questions about existing open space. Is that something that could be transferred as a right? Don Libby and James both agreed that if they had reserved it, then yes. Karen then asked if somebody goes through the process with 10 rights and the Board only allows 5, what happens to the other 5? Can they sell them or is it in an easement that can never be undone? Don Libby then told everyone that that is why they make the situation clear, because in that case, it couldn’t be undone. You can’t go back on the easement, so the buyer would be told in order to fully understand everything. Jean said the point of this was to bring the development into a supportive infrastructure as opposed to spreading it out all over town. Karen said she wouldn’t be comfortable being stuck with an easement, and Mr. Libby said that’s where they had to draw the line: between the Town’s comfort and that of the land owner.

Cotheal Linnell: What is the white area? James said that it is in neither sending nor receiving zones. This was done for a couple of reasons: 1) growth area being compacted and 2) for future changes to either sending or receiving zone. (Zones might need to be expanded into the white zone) Don Libby added that they can track where developments are occurring. Cotheal asked if they’ve done a comparison study of this compared to setting up cluster developments which keep green space as open space. Jean said the point of this is to have open space and bring the infrastructure in. Ms. Linnell is concerned about the open space being given for homes to be built and Jean said a few will be. Don said that the Town wants to try to link its open space. James said that we’ve permanently preserved over 380 acres of land in this town. All but one subdivision has been in the blue zone. The Town has not been good about protecting land in the rural zones. TDR will help preserve that.

Owen Haskell: He believes that most of the aquifer protection is in the blue area. James said yes, and that the Town knows where the impacts will be in that zone. A water study was done to assess the impact of increase in density on the aquifer. The Town is prepared for that. Owen thought it would be wiser to specify a minimum density in aquifer with protection zone instead of leaving it up to future Planning Boards. The maximum without TDR is two acres, and if they do use TDR, it will be a maximum density of one acre. There is a limit and the water study was done at both densities. Don Libby said that everything has been reviewed by the Town Attorney. Also, he wanted to remind the public that the Town wants their input. The people employed by the Town can make mistakes, and it’s always good when the townspeople voice their thoughts and opinions. Soon after his statement, Jean reiterated that the Town is trying to keep its open space.

Jean closed the Public Hearing at 8:17 p.m.

Jean Libby, Chairman

-James gave a small summary on the 23-lot subdivision. He told everyone that there are now two roads – Briarwood Drive and Fernwood Lane (accessed by lots 21, 22, &23). There is also a question of two fire ponds.

Discussion: Jean suggested that they start by talking about the fire ponds. The fire department doesn’t want a tank in there, yet Keith mentioned his concern about who could refill a fire pond if it was emptied. He said that they need to be engineered. One on Briarwood is convenient, but a gallon calculation has not yet been done. Jean thought that the other fire pond looked like it was on a brook. Keith went on to say there was drainage on the other side of the road that would be accessible. They’ve had second thoughts on having aerial topography done. More accurate contouring is needed. Jean told them that two fire ponds are not required. Keith said that the pond should be suitable. He was told by James that the pond has to be able to hold water during a drought. Tim asked if they’d ever had a fire pond that incorporated part of an aerial stream as part of a recharge. James said that they’d done that prior to DEP regulating streams. Jean said it would’ve been ideal, but James said that DEP won’t let you touch it. They said they’d find a suitable place but Jean said they must do everything through James. She also told them that lot 21 looks like it has an entrance in another place and that they need to revise the map by correcting it. Also, she let them know that the Board did approve the side and front set backs. Keith thought the waiver was on all, including the rear. Jean made it clear that the rear wasn’t part of it. It’s still 30’, James said. Jean asked the Board to consider sending this to a geologist for peer review, and Karen wanted to know if that would ever do anything. James said it would be good to get a second opinion. Don Fortin said that he doesn’t have a problem with it being reviewed again. Janet wanted to know what would happen if they come back with a problem. Jean said they would have to address it, but they’re not going to go there.

Motion: to have a second opinion review with Gillespie at the expense of Tim, Don, and Keith. John, second Don. 6-0-0

Discussion: Keith asked if a set back was missing on some of the lots. Jean just said that there were problems with the map. The problem was it was not on every lot. Tim then requested a reduction on rear set backs except for lots 1 though 4. Don said that they’re just concerned about the leech field area. James questioned him on why the leech field matters in this situation, and Don told him that they need 25’ between the house and leech field. James is to contact geologist and forward the cost to the men. Jean suggested that they use the people the Town of New Gloucester uses. Karen was curious as to why they need the extra expense, and Jean was quick to mention how they must be very careful with the water situation. Jean asked that the rear set backs be changed from 30’ to 25’ (all except for lots 1 through 4). The people on the lots will realize others when bought.

Motion: vote to accept change in rear set backs. Don, second Jean. 4-2(Ruth, John)-0

Discussion: Janet wanted to know why all the set backs aren’t being changed. Jean told her that the others are with a cluster. Tim mentioned that septic is placed without looking where the house will be placed on the lot. Jean wanted to know where they are with the open space. They’re not dealing with anyone from recreation, but Tim said they’re trying to talk to Little League. Linda Chase got up to talk about how Little League is currently privately owned. They do have interest in property, and if the property was given to the town, Little League can use it. She knows the town must vote and there must be a written agreement. Linda wanted to know if it was voted upon by town, is it still considered open space. Jean asked if the recreation was interested in the open space, and Linda said yes. She’d given a letter to James. Tim talked concerning the conservation easement property – they would like to see their only obligation be to donate it to a qualifying entity. Karen agreed with Tim and said should anything happen, the land should go to a qualifying land trust. James said that there will be an association at that time, and asked Linda if Little League would be interested in all open space. Janet said why not bypass the town and go to the land trust. Little League voted to take all open space, said Linda. Jean told her to get a letter to James and get a definite plan. Don needs to get separate deeds. Don made it clear that there are no further subdivisions. James said that if part of it is open space, it will stay with other open spaces. Linda will take care of the letter by next week.

James had some questions about the nitrate map. He thought it might be difficult to locate wells on the lots. They can be built in open space, with restrictions. Jean said that they must get restrictions so they can put wells in out there if necessary. Don told her that there are no permanent dwellings in the open space. Tim asked if the reconfiguration of the lots worked. He was told by James that it was according to the law. Don then wanted to know if the underground utilities could be waived to aerial utilities. In needs to be in writing, Ruth said.

Motion: to waive underground utilities. Karen, second Ruth. 6-0-0

Discussion: Karen questioned there being no association but there’s a road. Jean told her that that has already been taken care of.

Public Concern: Lorraine Blake said that there was no mention tonight on the traffic concerns. She has two wells, and ran into water problems when her first one was dug. It’s legal, said Jean, and they are double checking the water situation. Tom Blake then got up to state his concern with the newly proposed shorter road. He has a little child getting on the school bus, and he knows traffic is going to increase.

Discussion: Jean wanted to know if the site distance had been checked on the lots on road, and Keith said he would do it. James went on to tell him that the estimated trips on Briarwood Drive are now under 200 trips per day. Don Fortin wanted to schedule a public hearing. Jean said they could do a public hearing on the preliminary, but is it necessary.

Motion: to deem the preliminary complete subject to receipt on conditions with open space, dedications, and restrictions of granting and reviewing the peer review.

*Note: Tim wants the public hearing on second meeting in October.

Other Business

Discussion: Jean wants to set a date for a public hearing for the transfer of development rights. She set it for October 14th, Thursday at 7:30 p.m.

Motion: to vote to set the date as a public hearing. Karen, second Janet. 6-0-0

Motion: to Adjourn: Don, second Karen. 6-0-0

Jean Libby, Chairman

X______________________________________

title: September 7, 2004
html:
NEW GLOUCESTER PLANNING BOARD

Minutes of September 7, 2004

Members Attending
Jean Libby, Chairman
Karen Asselin, Vice Chairman
Ruth Waterhouse
Janet Smaldon
Laurie Brady
John

James Isaacson, Town Planner

Others Present

Keith W. Morse

Tim Nolen

Pat Norton

Mark Norton

Brandie Bauder

Troy Bauder

Shelley Blake (and Isaac)

Vera Berry

Wendy Berrit

Joanne Hutchison

Michael Gram

Ellie Fellers

Topics: Brierwood Estates Major Preliminary Subdivision Review; Grant Foundation Expedited Site Plan Review; Clark House Relocation Site Plan Review; Town Garage Public Sand Storage Unit Site Plan Review; Review of New Subdivision Application Forms; Other Business

Brierwood Estates Major Preliminary Subdivision Review

James gave a synopsis on how Fortin Construction, Inc. is proposing a 23-lot subdivision on the Penny Road, where the Morrison ball field currently is located.

Discussion: Janet mentioned that the stream she saw was not located on the site map. John had a few questions about the wetlands, and Karen was concerned about the adequacy of water for wells, as was Jean. Jean also brought it to everyone’s attention that part of the land was dedicated to the town, therefore, the town must vote on what will happen to it.

The Board questioned Keith and the Broker on certain issues: Jean asked if they planned to get a DEP and they said they had applied by rule and did not hear back in 14 days. Keith reminded everyone that 15 lots are over 28.56 acres, not 30. James was concerned about the problems with the left over space and is going to look into it. The Broker made it clear that he thought Little League was going to take care of the ball field and he wants it to stay there. Jean asked about the open space and the Broker said he hasn’t heard from Little League. Jean made it clear that it’s at the will of the people as to whether anything can be done or not. Keith wants the extra land dedicated as common open spaces to the landowners, and they planned to keep the ball field. Proof of the evidence of water supply is needed. R. W. Gillespie (hydrologist) was hired to do a full study. Janet asked about another water issue, and Keith said they wanted to put in a 10,000-gallon tank of water for the sub-divisions. The Broker said this is probably their highest means of water for the lots. Keith said it would be easy access for fire trucks. Jean told them to make sure they build to town specifications. Karen asked if the road could be maintained by town for fire help even if it doesn’t become a public road, but she was told no. Fire Chief Gary stood up to say the tank needs to be as close to road as possible and asked them to see if the property will hold a fire pond right off. Broker asked if the fire pond could be put on open space and he was told “yes”. There was an issue with Lot 7 – it has a stream of wetlands running though it. Keith didn’t know about the 100’ buffer requirement; he thought it was 25’. He wanted to know if the board would consider a 25’ set back. Screen crossings will be put in and he also has credentials to delineate wetlands. The Broker mentioned shifting lots 8 and 9 towards 10. James agreed that the distance would protect the house. The Broker then asked if the set back should be 100’. James said that 25’ is adequate on side set back.

Motion: to vote to set a new distance by changing: front 50’ to 25’, side 30’ to 25’ and buffer 25’ from that area. Karen, second Ruth 6-0-0

*Notes and conditions on all plans need to be present next time.

Discussion: Traffic count: there needs to be less than 200 trips per day to have only one road. There are 23 lots and 21 lots on road. There will be approximately 209 trips per day. James told Keith and Broker that there needs to be two connections to the public road. Keith said that would be environmentally unsound. Karen mentioned that page 8-2 states that 200 trips or more must have two street connections. The Broker then stated that they could insert a private road between lots 22 and 23. Jean said that he would need to find a compromise with James. She then questioned what they would do for utilities. Keith said they would go underground.

Motion: To waive requirements for monuments and for contour lines. Karen, second John 6-0-0

Discussion: The Broker then questioned the Board about his work needing to be done by October 1st according to regulations, or they must wait until May. They would like a permit. Jean decided that a motion be made to say that they’re 100% responsible. Karen wanted to know what would be involved with the crossing. The Broker said they were planning to put in culverts.

Motion: to vote to allow them to go in there. Karen, second Laurie.

2 stream crossings near lots 5 and 7

Amend Motion: to vote to give approval only after they present everything to James. Karen, second Laurie. 4-1(John)-1(Ruth)

Public Concern: Tom Blake: lives near road from proposed development and is very concerned with the water issue, stream, and traffic flow near ball field.

Loraine Blake: concerned on the same issues as well

Grant Foundation Expedited Site Plan Review

James gave an overview on how Donald and Diantha Grant are proposing to place a foundation under their camp at 12B True’s Point Road, on Sabbathday Lake.

Discussion: We found out that the site is within 15’ of the shore. They are to bring in Cumberland County to check for erosion protection.

Motion: to vote to review grant under expedited review. Ruth, second John. 6-0-0

Discussion:Laurie asked why they weren’t expanding the foundation by 30%, and the man said that the owner was “Happy with what they have.”

Motion: to vote that they must be approved by C.C.S & W.C.D. Karen, second Laurie.

6-0-0

Clark House Relocation Site Plan Review

James gave a synopsis of how Alicia Clark proposes to relocate a house from Danville to her property on Intervale Road, in the Village and Historic Overlay Districts.

Discussion: John asked whether or not it would be their permanent residence, and the woman said yes.

Motion: to waive storm water management. Karen, second Ruth. 6-0-0

Discussion: Janet had a quick question.

Motion: to vote to make application complete. Karen, second Ruth. 6-0-0

Motion: John wanted a public hearing

Motion: to waive public hearing. John, second Karen. 4-1(Janet)-1(Ruth)

Motion: to vote to approve condition that apartment clause be removed from the application, and should they want to change that, they would need to come back later. John, second Laurie. 6-0-0

Town Garage Public Sand Storage Unit

James explained to the Board that the Town of New Gloucester is proposing to construct a 12’x12’ sand storage unit for the public’s use, at the Town Garage facility in the Upper Village.

Discussion: this would allow for public sand to be under cover. Bill wants to put up a 3-sided shelter. Jean and James stated that there’s a problem with the impervious surface. The Board decided not to vote yet until the issue with the impervious surface is settled.

Review of Subdivision Application Forms

Motion: to vote to accept the form. Karen, second John. 6-0-0

Other Business

Discussion: on development rights.

Motion: to vote to have Accessories Department send a letter to the selectmen. Karen, second Ruth. 6-0-0

Motion: to adjourn. Ruth, second Janet. 6-0-0

title: August 17, 2004
html:
NEW GLOUCESTER PLANNING BOARD

Minutes of August 17, 2004

Jean Libby, Chairman Ken Webb

Ruth Waterhouse Rodney Bergeron

Janet Smaldon

Don Mendell

Laurie Brady

John Sumner

James Isaacson, Town Planner

Topics: Webb Minor Subdivision and Bergeron Addition Site Plan Review

1. Motion: To approve the July 20, 2004 minutes with the following corrections: Correct the spelling on John Sumner’s name (Summer to Sumner) Page 2, the word “be” added in the discussion section of #5 and remove the word “used” and add the word “be” to the end of the same paragraph. Ruth, second John 6-0

2. Motion: To approve the August 3, 2004 minutes. Add Laurie Brady to the Members Attending and clarify the 3rd Motion vote on page 2. It should read 2-4-2 (2) Ruth and Janet (4) Karen,Don,Laurie and John (2) Jean, Ruth abstained and add Jean Libby, Chairman and submitted by Laurie Brady. Ruth, second Janet 6-0.

3. Webb Minor Subdivision. James explained that George Webb is proposing to subdivide Map 17, Lot3A (portion of) into 3 lots in an open space subdivision.

Discussion: Dick Sweet will fax a revised septic design on lot #3 and Lot #3 may cross individual property lines in a cluster division but not impact the subdivision in any way. No questions regarding the open space. Still missing the deed, a ground water supply test, and the deed describing the open space restrictions, the details on the driveway and the hammerhead for the fire department and revised nitrate study and how Mr. Webb will deal with the low CMP wires. (James will call CMP for Mr. Webb) If Lot 2A isn’t sold to the abutter it will go with Lot 2.

Motion: To waive the fire pond (based on The Board’s famous letter from Mr. Sweet) Ruth, Janet second Vote 5-1 John opposed

4. Bergeron Addition Site Plan Review. James explained that Rodney Bergeron is proposing to construct a small addition to his home at 63 Sunset Shores Road, on Sabbathday Lake. Mr. Bergeron described the 14’ x14’, one story, enclosed entryway with a closet off to one side, to be built for aesthetic purposes.

Motion: To review the project under “expedited review.” Don, Ruth second Vote 6-0

Motion: To act on the application to approve it with conditions of an 8’ or 4’ foundation, an enclosed, one story addition on the roadside entryway only, and abiding by the recommendation from the CCS&WCD. John, Ruth second Vote 6-0.

Other Business: Jean asked Ruth to take over the meeting so that she could make a motion.

title: August 3rd, 2004
html:
NEW GLOUCESTER PLANNING BOARD

Minutes of August 3, 2004

Jean Libby, Chairman Richard Reiss

Karen Asselin, Vice Chairman William Centamore

Ruth Waterhouse Wayne Wood

Janet Smaldon

Don Mendell

Laurie Brady

John Sumner

James Isaacson, Town Planner

Topics: Simpson Dock Site Plan Review-continued discussion; Review New Site Plan Application Forms

Simpson Dock Site Plan Review

James gave a synopsis of the Cumberland County Soil and Water Conservation District report that was provided to Mr. Gordon Simpson (the owner of the dock.) The CCSWCD,

Recommended that Mr. Simpson address the following concerns:

- Steep Slope that provides access to the lake has a high potential to erode

- Bare soil present at the water’s edge

- Storm water runoff from the roof of the shed

Discussion: Jean asked if the dock is even on Mr. Simpson’s property and if that needed to be cleared up before the board act on the application. James said that even if the dock is encroaching on the neighbor’s property Mr. Simpson may not need to come back before the board, but it could be a condition of approval. Jean asked if there were any site walk comments. There were none. Jean stated that we would not be acting on any waiver requests, but that we need the standard boundary survey.

Motion: To deem that the application is complete. Karen, second Ruth 7-0-0

Motion: To waive the public hearing. Karen, second Don 7-0-0

Motion: To act on the application providing the following conditions: Boundary survey, follow the 3 suggestions by the CCSWCD and that the location of the dock be verified before any permits are issued. Karen, second Ruth 7-0-0

This next item was added to the agenda today- Richard Reiss’s 4 lot subdivision

James explained that Richard Reiss’s 4 lot subdivision had been approved providing that the following Note and Condition be adhered to by Mr. Reiss before constructing any homes. 6. All new buildings to be built on these lots will need Planning Board Approval because of the Historic Overlay. The CEO had issued 3 building permits, in error, not realizing that this condition had not been met and Mr. Reiss started construction not realizing an error had been made.

Discussion: Jean stated that Mr. Reiss definitely needed to come back before the Planning Board before starting the construction. Karen asked if the Board could follow the expedited review and Jean said no. Jean asked if all the buildings were stick built. Wayne Wood said yes. Karen wanted to know where was the list of supplies and if this should be a public meeting. Jean explained that the Boards concern was the Historic Overlay because the subdivision had already been approved. The Board members requested information on the siding, windows, setbacks, colors, lot 4 septic design, chimney material, (the plans showed chimneys but Mr. Reiss said that there would not be any chimneys, but direct vent heating systems) Jean asked what the Board wanted to do. Karen said she would look at the Historic Overlay issues, but hesitantly because this item wasn’t on the agenda, and she wasn’t sure a public hearing would change anything, to do with the Historic Overlay issue. Janet said that she thought that the neighbors or other citizens might think that Mr. Reiss was getting away with something because they weren’t notified before the construction began. Karen asked if we the Board could decide not to include an item on the agenda and James said that items might be out on the agenda that day, if needed. Mr. Reiss requested to speak. He said he had been to all the other Planning Board meetings and had always provided everything that was required of him. He stated that he had spoken with Debbie (CEO) on several different occasions and that he was as surprised as all of us that he was at this Board Meeting tonight. He apologized for any infractions and said it was an honest mistake. Don was concerned about setting a precedent and Ruth agreed with Janet that the Board should be following the agenda.

Motion: To vote to add this issue regarding the 3 homes in the Historic Overlay in Mr. Reiss’s subdivision to the agenda. 5-2-0 Ruth and Janet opposed

Motion: To deem application complete with plans showing no chimneys. Karen, second Don 5-2-0 Ruth and Janet opposed

Motion: To have a public hearing on August 17 at the Planning Board Meeting. Janet, second John 2-3-2 (2) Ruth, Janet (3)Karen, Laurie, John (2) Jean, Ruth abstained

Motion: To approve application providing the materials are consistent with the homes in the area. Karen, second Laurie

Motion: To approve application providing the homes have vinyl siding, asphalt shingles, vinyl windows with grids, 6/6 and no chimneys. 4-2-1 Ruth and Janet opposed, John abstained

Review New Site Plan Application Forms

Discussion: James asked that the Board review the new application. Laurie mentioned a spelling error on page 2of 2 the word sown should be shown #2 Submission Requirements. Jean liked the form and especially the attachment explaining the form itself.

Motion: To accept the new Submission Checklist for Site Plan Review. Don, second John 7-0-0

Other Business

James mentioned that the Board needed to sign several plans and that Wayne Wood was waiting.

Motion: To adjourn. Ruth, second Karen. 7-0-0

title: July 6th, 2004
html:
New Gloucester Planning Board

Minutes of July 6, 2004

Members Attending: Others Present:

Jean Libby, Chairman Paul Ellis Rick Reiss

Karen Asselin, Vice Chairman Cliff Conway Jennifer Wayboer

Ruth Waterhouse Timothy Parks Ellie Fellers

Janet Smaldon Stephen Massing Laurie Kennedy

Don Mendell Trish Mulcahy John Holmes

Laurie Brady Reggie Jacqmin Robert Whitting

Debby Parks, CEO Michael Jacqmin John Palmitter

Nancy Capps Keith Morse

William Capps Don Fortin

Jana Scotia Tim Nolan

Arenda Chamberland Field Rider

Louise Phillips Matt Johnson

Wayne Wood Suzon Murray

Topics: Reiss Minor Subdivision, public hearing; Cobble Hill Estates, subdivision amendment; Whitney Single Lot Open Space Subdivision, site plan review; McAtee Minor Subdivision, on-going review; Murray Barn & Studio Apartment, site plan review; Johnson Home Addition, site plan review; Massing Dormer Addition, site plan review; Rider Barn, site plan review; Morrison Field Major Subdivision, preliminary sketch plan; MacDonald Minor Subdivision, signing of final plan.

1. Appointment of Officers

Motion: To select Jean Libby as Chair. Ruth, second Karen 5-0-1 (Jean).

Motion: To select Karen Asselin as Vice Chair. Ruth, second Jean 5-0-1 (Karen).

Motion: To select Don as CIP representative. Ruth, second Janet 5-0-1 (Don).

Motion: To select Jean as Zoning Board representative. Ruth, second Janet 5-0-1 (Jean)

2. Minutes of June 1, 2004

Motion: To approve the minutes of June 1, 2004 with the removal of “at the” in item 7, change “relocated” to “relocate” in item 8, insert the word “would” before decrease in item 5. Ruth, second Karen 5-0-1 (Laurie).

3. Minutes of June 15, 2004

Motion: To approve the minutes of June 15, 2004 with a change of PO to GPO in all of the sections referencing the Ground Water Protection Overlay District. Ruth, second Janet 5-0-1 (Laurie).

4. Reiss Minor Subdivision, Intervale Road, Village, RR and GPO Districts

Public Hearing: The public hearing was opened at 7:46. William Capps, a neighbor, spoke about his concern about additional runoff that the new homes may create towards his property. Wayne Wood commented that they discussed the issue with DOT and DOT indicated to Wayne that a culvert would not be needed. Rich Reiss, the developer, said he is willing to limit the home across the street from Mr. Capps’ to having a stone driveway and that he would be reducing the grade of that property as well. Wayne also pointed out that DOT would not approve the driveway if it felt it would increase runoff to neighboring properties. Jana Scotia, another neighbor, expressed her concern about losing the interurban trail. Mr. Capps spoke again to indicate that there was an elderly neighbor that lived nearby who had some concerns about the project, but she is unable to make the meetings. He asked the developer to consider going over to speak with her to help eliminate her concerns. Mr. Reiss agreed that he would be willing to do that. The public hearing was closed at 7:56.

Discussion: Don brought up the issue of the fire pond and said that it seems like the Board keeps getting the same letter stating that the soils are not suitable for a pond. He said he would rather make the developer put the pond in and then see what happens. Karen agreed that the letter from Mr. Sweet was getting redundant and she was also reluctant to rely on it in every case. Jean commented that the letters do state different facts and that they are signed by a certified engineer. She feels that the Board does not have the expertise to second guess these letters. Janet voiced her concern about the interurban trail and she stated that she felt that the Selectmen had copped out by not giving the Planning Board some direction. Jean commented that the letter submitted by the developer indicating his willingness to pay for the cost to move the trail to Town property should be sufficient for the selectman to act. She also pointed out that taking an easement on the trail would require a vote of the entire Town.

Motion: To waive stone monuments and a fire pond. Karen, Janet 4-2-0 (Don, Ruth).

Motion: To deem the application complete subject to receipt of the hydrogeological study, a copy of the deed, and a copy of the assessor’s maps showing abutting properties. Karen, second Don 5-0-1 (Ruth).

Motion: To approve the application based on the findings of fact provided and subject to 1) a requirement that the driveway of lot 2 be limited to gravel only, 2) reducing the grade of lot 2 by 1 foot to help prevent runoff to neighboring properties, 3) a requirement that the developer pay the costs to relocate the interurban trail to Town property if the selectman approve that action. Karen, second Janet 5-1-0 (Ruth).

5. Cobble Hill Estates Subdivision Amendment, RR and GPO Districts

Discussion: Jean pointed out that the phosphorous study prepared by Dick Sweet recommended that a 100 foot no cut buffer be put in place along the entire boundary with McKenney Drive. She also noted that a letter from a well driller verifying the adequacy of the water in the area was not in file. The letter from Dick Sweet stating that the soils in the area would not support a fire pond was commented on and Jean pointed out that it had a different set of facts than the last one the Board received.

Motion: To waive the requirement for a fire pond. Karen, second Ruth 6-0-0.

Motion: To deem the application complete. Karen, second Ruth. 6-0-0.

Motion: To hold a public hearing at the next meeting on July 20, 2004. Don, second Laurie. 6-0-0.

6. Whitney Single Lot Open Space Subdivision, FF and RP Districts

Discussion: Jean reported that the Board had done a site walk and found the area where the house would be to be flat with a steep embankment around the brook. A discussion was had about the building envelope for the house and the limits of the resource protection area. John Palmitter pointed out that they had added note 6 to the plan to prevent the driveway from being closer than 125 feet of the brook. Karen asked that the note be changed to state specifically that the driveway must come from Pond Road. Janet questioned the reliability of the soils test in the packet because it was from 1988, but Debbie Parks assured her that it was still valid since nothing had been done to change the soils. Jean stated that the best way to review the plan was as a site plan under article 7.4.2, rather than as an open space subdivision so that the requirements for the open space were not necessary. The contractor agreed to not cut anything more than what was needed for the house and he has indicated the maximum house size on the plan.

Motion: To waive the requirement for contour lines. Karen, second Ruth. 6-0-0.

Motion: To deem the application complete subject to the receipt of 1) a letter from a well driller certifying the adequacy of water in the area, 2) a change to note 6 to state specifically that the driveway will come off from Pond Road, 3) a note on the plan indicating that the developer will carefully monitor and control erosion during development. Karen, second Ruth. 6-0-0.

Motion: To approve the application under section 7.4.2 subject to the conditions stated above. Ruth, second Janet. 6-0-0.

7. McAtee Minor Subdivision, RC and GPO Districts

The applicant was not at the meeting and no new materials were provided so there was no discussion on this item.

8. No Baloney Pony Minor Subdivision

Discussion: Jean pointed out that the Board had done a site walk and that it was recommended that the developer consider a road maintenance agreement for the two lots not under review. Regarding the site under review, it was pointed out that a septic design or proof of the adequacy of the existing septic system was needed. The Board also requested that contours be put on the plan and that the wetlands are delineated.

9. Murray Barn & Studio Apartment Site Plan

Discussion: Jean reported that the Board did a site walk and there were no issues other than the drainage and possible wetlands. The applicant stated that she is building a fieldstone retaining wall to stop erosion and help with drainage. Jean asked what would be done for landscaping and the applicant stated that there would be a fenced in yard with a few hardwood trees. Ruth asked what the roofing materials would be and requested that that be added to the list of materials. Ruth was also concerned about the siding being proposed, but Jean pointed out that it fits with other structures in the area. Jean mentioned that the applicant will need to follow the best management practices for soil erosion during construction as well.

Motion: To waive the requirement for storm water management. Karen, second Ruth. 6-0-0.

Motion: To deem the application complete. Karen, second Ruth. 6-0-0.

Motion: To waive the public hearing. Don, second Ruth. 6-0-0.

Motion: To approve the application subject to approval of the subdivision. Karen, second Janet. 6-0-0.

At this time the Board re-opened the discussion of the No Baloney Pony Subdivision to discuss the need for a public hearing.

Motion: To hold a public hearing. Janet, second Ruth. 4-2-0 (Don, Jean).

10. Johnson Home Addition Site Plan, Lake and GPO Districts

Discussion: Jean reported that the Board had done a site walk and that there were no issues found.

Motion: To waive contour lines. Karen, second Don. 6-0-0.

Motion: To deem the application complete. Janet, second Ruth. 6-0-0.

Motion: To approve the application subject to the applicant following Best Management Practices for erosion control. Ruth, second Laurie. 6-0-0.

11. Massing Dormer Addition Expedited Site Plan Review, RR and Historic Overlay Districts

Discussion: The applicant reported that he was adding two dormers to the building. The one to the entryway will be supported by pillars.

Motion: To review under expedited review. Ruth, second Don. 6-0-0.

Motion: To approve the application subject to receipt of a septic plan. Karen, second Janet. 6-0-0.

12. Rider Barn Site Plan Review, RR and Historic Overlay Districts

Discussion: The applicant reported that the Barn is 16 feet high and that it would not have any utilities, water or power. The roof material is asphalt shingles. The building will sit on a bed of crushed stone in the same area that a barn used to be located on the property. Jean pointed out that the following submission items were missing: 1) list of abutters, 2) a soils map, 3) a materials list, 4) a landscaping plan.

Motion: To waive the boundary survey and contour lines. Karen, second Ruth. 6-0-0.

Motion: To waive the public hearing. Janet, second Ruth. 6-0-0.

Motion: To deem the application complete subject to the receipt of the items listed above. Karen, second Ruth. 6-0-0.

Motion: To approve the application subject to receipt of the missing items listed above. Ruth, second Karen. 6-0-0.

13. Morrison Field Major Subdivision, RR District

Discussion: The applicant noted that the plan submitted is preliminary and they would like to change the concept to have 23 of the lots have driveways off from the main road off Route 100, with the other two homes coming off a private road. The change would eliminate one of the entryways to the subdivision, if allowed, and it would preserve more land around the ball field. Jean asked who would own the ball field and the developer indicated that they would like to offer it to the Town. Currently the ball field is being included in the net residential acreage calculation, but it was unclear if they could still do that if they deed the field to the Town. The applicant stated that all roads would be built to Town standards and that two of the lots would be limited to low income housing. A site walk to view the development was scheduled for Wednesday, July 14th at 5:00.

14. Other Business

Jean pointed out the letter that was sent to Cyrus Thompson III in response to his letter to the Board and she introduced Laurie as a new member.

Karen asked that something be done to find someone to take over the minutes on a regular basis.

Motion: To have Jean contact the Town to hire someone to take the Board minutes. Ruth, second Janet. 6-0-0

15. Adjournment

Motion: To adjourn, Ruth, second Don, 6-0-0.

__________________________________

Jean Libby, Chairman

Respectfully Submitted

_________________________________

Karen Asselin

title: June 15th, 2004
html:
New Gloucester Planning Board

Minutes of June 15, 2004

Members Present: Others Attending:

Jean Libby, Chair Robert Whitney Michael Jacqmin

Ruth Waterhouse Trish Mulcahy Jim Mulcahy

Don Mendell Roger St Pierre Ronald Rogers

Janet Smaldon Rita McDonald Kristina Wayboer

Abby Lumsden Raymond Brackett Dan McDonald

Karen Asselin Wayne Wood Matt Johnson

(John Green, excused absence) Debby Parks Doug McAtee

James Isaacson, Planner Nancy Capps Lillian Nayder

Topics: Dan McDonald and Doug McAtee. Douglas Drive, McDonald subdivision, RR and GWP zones, public hearing and approval; Richard Reiss, by a representative, Intervale Road, minor subdivision review, V, RR, HO and PO zones, review and public comments; Robert Whitney with Doug McAtee, 111 Pond Road, single lot open space subdivision, RR and GWP zones, preliminary review; Normand and Michelle Groleau, 123 Outlet Road, Roger St Pierre representing, minor addition, Lake and GWP zones, expedited review; Matt Johnson and Lillian Nayder, 24 Lake View Drive, addition, Lake and GPW zones, preliminary review; Jim and Patricia Mulcahy, 199 Cobbs Bridge Road, No Baloney Pony minor subdivision, RR and HO zones, preliminary review; Doug McAtee, Route 26, minor subdivision, RC and GWP zones, preliminary review; signing of Patriot Estates plan

1. Minutes of June 1, 2004

Motion: To table the minutes of June 1, 2004, pending revising the order of topics, and changing the date of the public hearings to the fifteenth not sixteenth.

2. Dan McDonald and Doug McAtee. Douglas Drive, McDonald subdivision, RR and GWP zones

Public Hearing 7:36-7:38

Douglas Drive resident Ronald Rogers expressed his concerns over the present state of the road and the effects of increases traffic.

Discussion: A fire pond will be installed and must have at least a ten-foot access off the road, which must be maintained by the road association. The plan has been updated, but written approval from the fire chief must be obtained and an easement given to the town for access and maintenance of the hydrant.

Motion: To waive the requirements for stone monuments because of the expense involved and for utilities since all others in the vicinity are above ground. Abby, second Karen, 6-0-0.

This subdivision is an extension of Douglas drive, which is a private road reportedly with eroding shoulders. McDonald said he plans to build the extension to public road standards and a final cover to the existing road and add gravel to the shoulders of the existing road when the home have been constructed. He was warned that all of Douglas Drive would have to meet town standards if it is to be accepted by the town.

Ruth asked if the developer has submitted the required cluster plan. It was unclear whether this has been done, but the board agreed that a cluster would not be appropriate for the area

Motion: To waive the requirement of submission of a cluster plan. Abby, second Karen, 6-0-0.

Motion: To approve the application of Dan McDonald with the conditions that an easement to the town for the fire pond, a letter of approval by the fire chief and space for fire pond access put on the plan by the surveyor be completed, based on the finding of fact prepared by the town planner. Karen, second Abby, 6-0-0.

3. Richard Reiss. Representative, Intervale Road, minor subdivision, V, RR, HO and PO zones.

Discussion: The public hearing scheduled for this application could not be legally held because a notice had not appeared in the Lewiston Sun-Journal. It was rescheduled for July 6. Since the abutters had received notices several were present.

Motion: To accept comment from the public. Abby, second Ruth, 6-0-0.

Public Comments:

James described the project as a four-lot subdivision on 4.3 acres between Intervale Road and Rowe Station Road. One of the lots has a home that is being renovated, so three additional one-acre lots will be created, tow with access on Rowe Station Road.

Michael Jacqmin was concerned with the style of the homes. He was told that since the parcel is in the historic overlay all homes will undergo review to meet historic standards and that the existing home renovation has been approved already. Nancy Capps said that storm runoff from that site goes into her driveway and she is concerned that it not be increased. Wayne Wood said that the new driveway could be placed so that runoff would be picked up by the nearby ditch. She was also concerned with historic standards.

Discussion: A portion of the interurban trail crossed the corner of the property and to maintain the trail it needs to be relocated to the abutting town owned land. The decision on how to manage this is the responsibility of the Board of selectmen. Letters verifying ground water supply in the area, and from a geologist saying a fire pond is not feasible are needed. The septic plumes need to go on the plan. The only waiver request is for stone monuments. James said the fees must be paid.

Motion: To reschedule the public hearing for July 6, 2004. Karen, second Janet, 6-0-0.

4. Robert Whitney with Doug McAtee, 111 Pond Road, single lot open space subdivision, RR and GWP zones.

Discussion: Robert Whitney wants to split his eleven acre parcel abutting Westcott Brook into two lots.He cannot do this conventionally because the larger part of the lot is in resource protection.By creating a one-lot open space subdivision and making use of the provision in the ordinance allowing a more restrictive zone to encroach 50 feet into an adjacent zone he is able to get a building envelope. Abby mentioned that the board should pay special attention to protection of the brook since it is the main water supply for the lake.

Site Walk: A site walk was scheduled for Monday, June 21 at 5:30.

5. Normand and Michelle Groleau, 123 Outlet Road, Roger St Pierre representing, minor addition, Lake and GWP zones.

Discussion: The Groleaus want to add a dormer to a guest house on their property. A portion of the septic line needed to be replaced and that is the only proposed soil disturbance. Since the addition is less than 200 square feet the project qualifies for expedited review. The planner and code enforcement officer are both required to visit the site. Although Debbie had visited the site, James had not. Presumably James will do this in the future. Karen suggested that it undergo regular site review.

Motion: To consider the application under the provisions for expedited review. 5-1-0 (Karen)

Motion: To approve the application of Michelle and Normand Groleau for an addition to their guesthouse. Abby, second Ruth, 6-0-0.

6. Matt Johnson and Lillian Nayder, 24 Lake View Drive, addition, Lake and GPW zones.

Discussion: This is a 940 square-foot addition within a hundred feet of the shore and must undergo full review. This is less than the 30% allowed by shoreland zoning. DEP has been contacted and earlier buffer planting has been done.

Site Walk: A site walk was scheduled for Monday, June 21, at 6pm.

Motion: To waive a public hearing. Karen, second Don. 4-2-0 (Abby and Ruth)

7. Jim and Patricia Mulcahy, 199 Cobbs Bridge Road, No Baloney Pony minor subdivision, RR and HO zones

Note: Since James is an abutter, Debbie filled in as advisor.

Discussion. This is a four -lot subdivision with two homes on the homestead lot and two lots that have been sold. The creation of the fourth lot triggered the subdivision review. One of the lots is in the historic overlay district, and all four need septic information. Wayne wood advised that there are wetlands and these will be mapped. The applicants were also advised that they need to think about a fire pond. The plan was very confusing and the board will wait to see it for clarification before further discussion.

Site Walk: A site walk was scheduled for Wednesday, June 23, at 5:30

8. Doug McAtee, Route 26, minor subdivision, RC and GWP zones

Discussion: This parcel abuts Buddy's store with the original house in the middle, a lot to the south and another accessed by a right of way which is also available to the developer for future development. Doug was advised that since this is in the watershed a phosphorus study is required.

Site Walk: A site walk was scheduled for Monday, June 21 at 5pm.

9. Other Business.

Jean reminded the Board that there is an informational meeting on plans for the Upper Village at the Amvets Hall, Thursday, June 15, 2004

The plan for Patriot Estates was signed.

Jean read a letter from a resident concerning the adding of car sales to the Tripp approval.

10. Adjournment.

Motion: To adjourn, Abby, second Karen. 6-0-0.

__________________________

Jean Libby Chairman

__________________________

Respectfully submitted by

Abigail R Lumsden

title: June 1st, 2004
html:
New Gloucester Planning Board

Minutes of June 1, 2004

Members Present: Others Attending:

Jean Libby, Chair Kristina Wayboer Richard Reiss

Ruth Waterhouse Terry Sanborn Dan McDonald

Don Mendell (excused absence) Jim Vadas Doug McAtee

Janet Smaldon Cynthia Shaw Wayne Wood

Abby Lumsden Lewis Shaw Ryan Tripp

Karen Asselin Virginia Stone Ronald Tripp

John Green Cyrus W Thompson George Webb

James Isaacson, Planner William Lentamore William Hutchings

Mark Hassett

Topics: Jim Vadas, Penny Road, public hearing and approval of Patriot Estate subdivision; Ryan Tripp, Lewiston Road, commercial building approval; Daniel Macdonald, Douglas Drive, Macdonald subdivision review; George Webb, Church Road, minor subdivision preliminary review; William Hutchings, Bald Hill Road, site plan, review and approval of house; Mark Hassett, 353 Gloucester Hill Road, expedited review of garage; Richard Reiss, 48 Intervale Road, minor subdivision, preliminary review; Richard Reiss, 48 Intervale Road, expedited review of home addition.

1. Minutes

Motion: To accept the minutes ofMay 18, 2004 as written. Ruth, second, John, 5-0-1 (Karen, not present)

2. Jim Vadas and Terry Sanborn, Penny Road, public hearing and final approval of Patriot Estate subdivision, RR zone

Public Hearing, 7:33-7-34pm:

Jim described the project as a 3-lot subdivision served by a private road. There were no public comments.

Discussion: It was noted that a revised road agreement has been received and that the board felt that the road entrance on a curve warranted a warning sign on the eastbound side of Penny Road after consultation on its placement with the highway department.

Motion: To approve the application for Patriot Estates based on the findings of fact prepared by the planner with the condition that a warning sign be placed on the road. Karen, second Ruth, 6-0-0.

Motion: To table the Ryan Tripp application until the arrival of the applicant and take up the McDonald application. Abby, second Ruth, 6-0-0.

3. Daniel Macdonald with Doug McAtee, Douglas Drive, Macdonald subdivision, RR and GPO zones

Discussion: The road design has been submitted. The application is lacking a water supply report and a hammerhead at the end of the road if it is to be accepted as a town road. Doug said that the road will be continued for additional lots before that happens. A setback from the wetlands on lot #20 remains to be determined. The ordinance requires a 100-foot buffer unless there is a distinct demarcation. In this case there is a steep slope to the wet area.

Motion: To reduce the wetland buffer to 50 feet because of the distinct change in slope. Abby, second John, 6-0-0.

The present turnaround should be checked by the fire chief, and a report given to the planner. Written waivers are needed above ground utilities and stone monuments.

Motion: To deem the application complete with submissions of a report on the turnaround from the fire chief, the granting of waiver requests and the wetland buffer recorded on the plan. Abby, second John, 6-0-0.

Public Hearing: A hearing will be held at the June 15 meeting.

Motion: To untable the Tripp application. Abby, second Ruth, 6-0-0.

4. Ryan Tripp, Lewiston Road, commercial building. RC zone

Site Walk Report: The site is a straight section of Route 100 with a sloping field with drainage down near the boundaries, with some natural buffering from the adjacent homes. A raised section of the former interurban roadbed along the frontage will be removed.

Discussion: Ryan has now included car sales in his application. His hours in the existing smaller shop up the road are 10-6 and closed on Sundays. He plans to keep them the same in the new building. The lighting will be shielded motion detector type. A statement of right title or interest has not yet been received. The ordinance requires a 50-foot buffer between a business and existing homes. John said he feels the requirements should be made more clear and the board suggested white pines and lower shrubs. Karen asked if he plans to service cars and was told that he only will service his cars for sale. He will be using the oil for heat and will take other hazardous material to a recycler. He needs to carefully put the designated parking area on the plan adding a 5-foot grass buffer at the front. There will be only one entrance. Waivers for 2-foot contours, erosion control, and storm water are requested. The storm water provisions on the property appear to be adequate, and normal erosion controls must be followed during construction.

Motion: To waive the requirement for 2-foot contours. Karen, second John, 6-0-0.

Motion: To declare the application complete with a statement of legal interest, and a statement regarding the lighting. Abby, second Ruth, 6-0-0.

Motion: To approve the application since it meets the requirement of the ordinance and it appears all environmental concerns will have been addressed with the additional submissions, and furthers the development of the village area. Abby, second Ruth, 6-0-0.

5. George Webb, Church Road, minor 4-lot subdivision. RR zone

Site Walk Review: This is a sloping site that has been lumbered off. There is a power line across the property that will have to be changed, and the board noticed a small area of wetland close to the road.

Discussion: Since it may not be possible to have the power line moved, it is possible that a cluster plan could solve the issue and one will be prepared. The original plan had a right of way through one lot which decrease the lot size, and that has been changed. The wetlands have been mapped and another area has been found at the rear of the parcel. The board has agreed that a fire pond may be located across the road in the property belonging to the developer. The driveway locations and two-foot contours should be shown on the plan. The subdivision should be named.

Motion: To waive the requirement for two-foot contours in favor of five-foot ones. Abby, second John, 6-0-0.

6. William Hutchings, 56 Bald Hill Road, site plan review of home, Village and Historic zones

Discussion: This is a request for replacement of a mobile home with a stick built cape style ranch. It is reviewed for historical standards only. It will have vinyl clapboard siding and small paned windows with a black metal roof and brick chimney.

Motion: To approve the application of William Hutchings since it meets the historic standards of the ordinance. Abby, second Ruth, 6-0-0.

7. Mark Hassett, 353 Gloucester Hill Road, expedited review of garage, Village zone

Motion: To review the application of Mark Hassett under the provisions for expedited review. Abby, second John, 6-0-0.

Disussion: This garage is at the behind a home and will not be particularly obvious.

Motion: To approve the application of Mark Hassett, Abby, second John, 6-0-0.

8. Richard Reiss, 48 Intervale Road, 4-lot minor subdivision, preliminary review. Village, Historic and RR zones

Discussion: The property has access to both Intervale and Rowe Station roads. The existing house on the property will be accessed from Intervale and the new lots from Rowe Station. There are wetlands on the south side of the property with the interurban trail running through it. The possibility of relocated the trail will be examined. The net residential acreage needs to be calculated.. The houses will have to meet historic standards. The driveway cuts need to be shown on the plan, and a fire pond should be addressed. Waivers are being asked for stone monuments and underground utilities.

Site Walk. A site Walk was scheduled for Thursday, June 3, at 5:30.

Motion: To schedule a public hearing for June 15. Abby, second John, 6-0-0.

9. Richard Reiss, 48 Intervale Road, expedited review of home addition, Village, Historic and RR zones

Motion: To review the application of Richard Reiss under the provisions for expedited review. Abby, second Ruth, 6-0-0.

Discussion: This is reviewed for historical standards only. During a complete renovation, a dormer will be added to the rear of the building. The siding will be wooden clapboards with pilasters at the corners. There will be small paned windows and a metal roof.

Motion: To approve the application of Richard Reiss since it has been determined that it meets the historic standards of the ordinance. Abby, second Ruth, 6-0-0.

10. Other Business:

There will be a joint meeting to discuss Transfer of Development Rights at 7pm, on June 9 at the Meeting House

An informational meeting on possible plans for Upper Village at the Am Vets Hall on June 16, 7pm.

11. Adjournment.

Motion: To adjourn. Abby, second, Karen, 6-0-0.

__________________________

Jean Libby Chairman

Respectfully submitted by

__________________________
Abigail R Lumsden

title: May 18th, 2004
html:
New Gloucester Planning Board

Minutes of May 18, 2004

Members Present: Others Attending:

Jean Libby, Chair Dave Sanborn Carlton Wilcox

Ruth Waterhouse Susan Sanborn George Webb

Don Mendell (late) Jim Vadas John Palmiter

Janet Smaldon Terry Sanborn

Abby Lumsden Ryan Tripp

Karen Asselin (excused absence) Ronald Tripp

John Green Paul Gilbert

James Isaacson, Planner

Topics: Jim Vadas and Terry Sanborn, Penny Road, continued review of minor subdivision, Patriot Estates; David Sanborn, 158-160 Upper Village Street, re-approval of duplex; George Webb, Church Road, preliminary review of minor subdivision; Ryan Tripp, Lewiston Road, site plan review of commercial building

1. Minutes

Motion: To untable the minutes of April 20, 2004. Abby, second Ruth, 5-0-0

Motion: To accept the minutes ofApril 20 with Ruth as a second on a motion, and showing Don as a later excused absence. Ruth, second Janet, 4-0-1 (John)

Motion: To accept the minutes of May 6, 2004, adding buffer to the Vadas discussion. Ruth, second Janet, 5-0-0

(Don arrived)

2. Jim Vadas and Terry Sanborn, Penny Road, Patriot Estates, 3-lot minor subdivision, RR zone.

Discussion: James said all materials have been submitted and that the road is named Patriot Drive. This is a 3-lot subdivision with a private road on fairly level land with a stream on the back boundary.

Motion: To waive the requirement for a fire pond based on the Sweet Associate report that the land is not suitable for a sustainable pond. Abby, second John. 6-0-0.

John asked what alternatives for fire protection replace a pond. Carlton Wilcox questioned the validity of the Sweet report, and abutter Paul Gilbert said he wanted to hear about the project.

Jean said that the wording of article 4 in the road agreement should match the wording of note 9 on the plan, making it clear that the road is being constructed to private road standards and can never be a town road.

Motion: To deem the application for Patriot Estates complete.

Abby, second John. 6-0-0.

A public hearing was scheduled for the June1 meeting and the application was told to notify the abutters.

3. David Sanborn, 158-160 Upper Village Street, extension of the approval of a duplex approved for Jim Vadas in 2003.

Discussion: There are no changes proposed for the extension. Abby asked whether the proposed ordinance change to allow variation in setbacks in the historic district had been implemented since it would allow for a better appearance of the building and give the owner a more sensible arrangement. She was told it had not been and a 40 -foot setback is still required. Mr. Sanborn asked if he could build a single dwelling instead of a duplex and was told that he would have to come back to the board for an amendment since the historical appearance of the building would be changed.

Motion: To transfer and extend the application for a duplex on Upper Village Street from Jim Vadas to David Sanborn. Abby, second Ruth, 6-0-0.

4. Ryan Tripp, with Ronald Tripp, Lewiston Road, site plan review of commercial building in the RC district.

Discussion: Ryan Tripp proposes to move his business closer to the center of Upper Gloucester on a lot extending from Peacock Hill Road to Lewiston Road by building a 6,000 square-foot building on Lewiston Road. The plan showed a third lot in the center reached by a right of way from Lewiston Road. Abby questioned why this was not considered a subdivision and James said that it is not since one of the three lots is being conveyed to a close relative. Abby said that she still found it confusing. The senior Mr. Tripp agreed to remove that lot since he has no immediate plans to sell or use it. The right of way to through the new lot will be retained

Jean said that the parking area needs to be defined on the plan and that a 50-buffer has to be maintained to protect the adjoining residences. Verification of ownership and compliance with the sign ordinance need to be addressed.

Site Walk and Public Hearing: A site walk was set for Wednesday, June 19 at 6:30, with a public hearing at the next meeting.

5. Other business:

John apologized for his absences due to business commitments.

James alerted to board to an upcoming joint meeting on the Transfer of Development Rights to be scheduled soon.

There will be an informational meeting on proposals for development of the upper village at the Am Vets Hall on Lewiston Road on June 16.

6. Adjournment.

Motion: To adjourn. Abby, second John, 6-0-0.

__________________________

Jean Libby Chairman

__________________________

Respectfully submitted by

Abigail R Lumsden

title: May 6th, 2004
html:
New Gloucester Planning Board

Minutes of May 6, 2004

Members Present: Others Attending:

Jean Libby, Chair Jim Vadas

Ruth Waterhouse Terry Sanborn

Don Mendell

Janet Smaldon

Abby Lumsden

Karen Asselin

(John Green, excused absence)

James Isaacson, Planner

Topics: Jim Vadas and Terry Sanborn, review of application, Penny Road minor subdivision, Penney Road, RR zone; Todd Donnelly, signing of Promised Land subdivision revision.

1. Minutes

Minutes of April 6, 2004

Motion: To accept the minutes ofApril 6, 2004with the corrections of changing the word 'illegal' to 'without planning board approval' from the discussion of Promise Land, and removing the word sparsely from the site walk report. Ruth, second Karen, 6-0-0.

Minutes of April 20, 2004

Motion: Table pending a check on the second on the waiver for stone monuments. Ruth, second Janet, 6-0-0

2. Jim Vadas and Terry Sanborn, continued review of Penny Road minor subdivision, Penney Road, Map 4, Lot 47B, RR zone

Discussion:

Site walk report: Janet said that the sight distance available for lot one is not adequate and the driveway should come of the proposed private road.It was also stated that the lot is quite flat except at the rear of lot three, which slopes steeply down to a stream, so a stream buffer should be required.

It was noted that the right title or interest requirement had been fulfilled. The abutters within 500 hundred feet are still to be notified, a road agreement drawn up, and a note regarding the fact it will remain a private should be added to the plan. It was suggested but not required that a private road warning sign be place on Penny Road.

The waivers requests are for two foot contour lines, a hydrogeological study, and wetland mapping. The board agreed that there are no wetlands on the parcel, but that the plan should include a 75-foot for the brook. Jim will look into the suitability of the land for a fire pond and will submit a request for a waiver if one is not feasible.

Motion: To require a natural vegetated 75-foot buffer from the stream. Abby, second Ruth, 6-0-0.

It was mentioned that this should be shown on the plan.

Motion: To waive the requirement for two-foot contour lines, and put the 10-foot USGS contours on the plan. Karen, second Ruth, 6-0-0.

Motion: To waive underground utilities and stone monuments.

Abby, second Ruth, 6-0-0

3. Other Business

The amended plan for Promised Land was signed after adjournment.

4. Adjournment.

Motion: To adjourn Abby, second Karen. 6-0-0

Jean Libby Chairman

title: April 20th, 2004
html:
New Gloucester Planning Board

Minutes of April 20, 2004

Members Present: Others Attending:

Jean Libby, Chair Eleanor Fellers Joel Bucci

Ruth Waterhouse Debra Parks Todd Donnelly

(Don Mendell, unexcused absence) Mike Thompson Dennis McIntosh

Janet Smaldon Brian Thompson Jim Vadas

Abby Lumsden Leslie Weeks Ed Emery

Karen Asselin Beverly Cadigan

(John Green, excused absence) Heath Dolloff

James Isaacson, Planner Lauren Bucci

Topics: Post Office, Gilmore Road, variance and amendment for permeable area of lot; Mike and Brian Thompson, Blue Grass Festival, public hearing and approval; Todd Donnelly, McIntire Road, Promised Land Subdivision, amendment; Heath and Laura Dolloff, 94 Marston Road, expedited review and approval of an addition; Jim Vadas, Penny Road, minor subdivision, preliminary review and scheduling of site walk.; Janet Smaldon, 146 Cobbs Bridge Road, amendment to previous plan for renovations to an ell.

1. Post Office, 9 Gilmore Road, variance and amendment for permeable area of lot, RC and Historic overlay zones, no applicant present

Discussion: Before the meeting a meeting of the Zoning Board of Appeals was held at which a variance of for the percentage of impermeable area of the lot was granted to increase the paved area to 31. 93%. This was granted because of the safety issues at the end of the narrow entrance and the lack of space in which trucks are able to turn.

Motion: To deem the application complete. Karen, second Ruth. 5-0-0

Motion: To approve the application, Karen, second, Ruth 5-0-0

2. Minutes

Motion: To add the word off and adding t to the word owing and to table pending clarification of the Promised Land discussion. Ruth, second Karen, 5-0-0

3. Mike and Brian Thompson, Gloucester Hill Road, site plan review for Blue Grass Festival , RR ( Jean recused herself and Karen took the chair)

Public Hearing, 7:35-7:36

Mike described the festival saying it is planned for the last weekend in June and will host nine bands with an expected attendance of 2500-3000 people with free camping provided. There were no comments from the public.

Discussion: Mike and Brian had described the plans for such things as parking, solid waste disposal previously, and the board has found them satisfactory.

Motion: To deem the application complete. Abby, second Ruth, 4-0-0

Motion: To approve the application of Mike and Brian Thompson to hold a blue grass festival with the following conditions. Abby, second Janet, 3-1-0 (Ruth)

1. the permit is applicable for only one year

2. noise level at the property boundary will be checked and lowered to meet the standards of the ordinance if necessary.

3. warning signs will be posted on the road

4. there will be no parking on the road

The next two items were taken out of order.

4. Heath and Laura Dolloff, 94 Marston Road, request for expedited review of an addition to a home in the lake district

Discussion: This is small second story of less than 200 square feet with no excavation expected. There will be no disturbance of the well-vegetated bank on the lake side of the building.

Motion: To review this application under the standards for expedited review. Karen, second Janet, 5-0-0

Motion: To approve the application of Heath and Laura Dolloff with the condition that best management practices be applied for any soil disturbance. Abby, second Ruth, 5-0-0

5. Todd Donnelly, McIntire Road, Promised Land Subdivision, amendment to create an additional lot. RR zone.

Discussion: This application had been tabled at the previous meeting pending the opinion of the wording of note #6 which precluded any further division of the lots. The town attorney said that the plan can be amended provided all the owners agree. Written statements from all but one of the lot owners were included. Joel Bucci, the owner of lot 9 A, wanted clarification of the status of his lot before signing. The division will remove the 25-foot buffer at his lot lines in one area. James said that either the buffer can be replanted or the buffer on lot 9B can be enlarged. The owner will replant and sign the agreement.

Motion: To waive the site walk. Janet, second Ruth, 4-1-0 (Abby)

Motion: To grant waivers for stone monuments, 2-foot contour lines, hydrogeological assessment, road plan and road profile. Karen, no second, 5-0-0

Motion: To deem the application complete. Karen, second Ruth, 5-0-0

Motion: To waive a public hearing, Abby, second Karen, 5-0-0

Motion: To approve the application with the following conditions. Karen, second Janet, 5-0-0.

1. septic report for the new lot

2. change to note 6 on the plan, to read amendments can be done with planning board approval

3. a road agreement applies to all lot owners

4. the buffer on lot 9A will be replanted

5. A note saying the road will remain private

6. Jim Vadas, Penny Road, minor subdivision, preliminary review. RR zone

Discussion: Jim plans a three lot-subdivision with access to one lot from the road and the other two from a shared driveway. He was told that the project needs a name and evidence of right title or interest. He has asked waivers for 2-foot contours and a hydrogeological study. He said the lot is quite flat except for a steep bank to a brook at the rear of lot 3

Site Walk: A site walk was scheduled for Thursday, April 22, at 5pm

7. Janet Smaldon, 146 Cobbs Bridge Road, amendment to previous plan for renovations to an ell. RR and historic overlay districts

Discussion: The application was approved several years ago. The amendment is for a change in the roofline of an ell, made necessary to get adequate ceiling height on the second floor.

Motion: To approve the amendment to the plan of Janet Smaldon. Abby, second Karen, 4-0-0

Other Business:

Motion: To hold the next planning board meeting on Wednesday, May 5, in case the annual town meeting runs a second night. Ruth, second Karen, 5-0-0

8. Adjournment.

Motion: To adjourn Abby, second Karen, 5-0-0
