Topics: Ken Farrington, Lewiston Road, reconsideration of approval of Ken's Car Care; Mike Thompson, Gloucester Hill Road, review of Bluegrass Festival; Dennis Waterman, Ethel Sawyer Road, continued review of minor subdivision; Stephen Scotia, Rowe Station Road, review and approval of minor subdivision; Robert Ray, Sr. Cobbs Bridge Road, expedited review and approval of home improvements in historic district; Todd Donnelly, Promise Lane, review of subdivision amendment; Jeff Brinck, New England Organics, granted request for exemption from further site review for land applications of the product Fiberlime.

1. Minutes of March 16, 2004

Motion: To accept the minutes of March 16, 2004, with the addition of a motion to reconsider the application of Ken's Car Care made by Karen and seconded by John with a vote of 5-0-1 (Abby, not present)

2. Ken Farrington, Lewiston Road, reconsideration of approval of Ken's Car Care, RB1 Zone and GWP Overlay

Discussion: Ken Farrington was granted approval for car sales and a towing and storage facility in a building at the Oliver Store site on February 17, 2004.James received a second memo from town attorney Chris Neagle written March 18 saying that he had overlooked section 4.4.G12 of the ordinance, which prohibits commercial vehicle impoundment in the GWP overlay. It was noted that car sales are not mentioned in permitted uses and the original application came in as a multi-use commercial site, which does not specify the uses.

Ken said that since most of the town is in GWP, the ruling effectively prevents any owing facilities in town, in spite of the fact that a number of them do exist. Ruth questioned whether the use was grandfathered since Ted McDonald said the building has been used for similar purposes for many years, and said she felt that the town was not allowing development of small businesses.

Motion: To approve Ken's Car Service for car sales only, subject to the conditions stated in the original approval. Karen, second Abby, 6-0-

3. Mike Thompson, Gloucester Hill Road, continued review, site plan application for a Blue Grass Festival, RR Zone (Jean recused herself as an abutter, Karen acted as chairman)

Discussion: The new submissions include a more clearly defined plan for parking and camping. An overflow parking area at Hopco on Lewiston Road and additional camping behind Mike’s house will be available. A sparsely attended site walk had been conducted. Janet and Karen said the site was beautiful and "rolly" but should be fine if the parking and camping area is controlled. The visibility of the entrance was considered and a request for warning signs was suggested. Since the camping area is temporary and there is no additional charge for it, the campground requirements do not need to be met. No open campfires will be allowed.

The noise levels at the boundaries prescribed by the ordinance are 55 decibels before 8:00 and 45 after that. The Thompson’s will check the levels during rehearsals and adjust them if necessary. Since this type of festival is new to the town, the permit will be for only one year.

The Thompson’s would like to start advertising as soon as possible so it was agreed that they could do so in spite of the fact final approval will not be given until after a public hearing since any changes are expected to be minor.

Motion: To deem the application complete. Abby, second Ruth, 5-0-0

Motion: To hold a public hearing at the next meeting. Abby, second Don. 5-0-0

James will determine the abutters to be notified.

(Jean returned to the chair.)

4. Dennis Waterman, represented by Don Douglas, Ethel Sawyer Road, continued review of an after-the-fact minor subdivision, RR, FF, RP, RC and GPO zones

Discussion: A road agreement and profile has been submitted. A cross section of the road needs to be added. John Palmiter will locate the septic field and a determination of the plume will be made and an easement procured if necessary. Jean said the road must be built to town private road standards as far as the last house being reviewed, and that no further lots can be created without planning board approval.

5. Steven Scotia, Rowe Station Road, review of an after-the-fact minor subdivision, RR zone

Discussion: Janet stated she is an abutter with 45 acres of woods between her home and the subdivision.

Motion: Janet can participate in the review. Abby, Ruth, 5-0-1 (Janet)

This is a three-lot subdivision that did not undergo review because the code enforcement officer did not realize that the land has not been owned for five years. There is one lot off Scotia Drive that has been deeded to Mr. Scotia's daughter and two off Hobbs Drive with one house already built. Debbie apologized and said that all submissions were in order and are no problems with the land use. There are no wetlands on the property so a hydrogeological study is not needed. Jean said the only submissions needed are a test pit on lot #3 on the plan and a road agreement.

Motion: To waive a site walk. Karen, second Ruth, 4-2-0 (Janet and Abby)

Motion: To grant waivers for contour lines and stone monuments. Karen, second Ruth, 5-1-0 (Abby)

Motion: To declare the application complete with the additions on the plan. These include a test pit on lot 3, a road agreement for lots 2 and 3, a statement that the road will remain private, the waivers, and a statement that no more lots will be created without planning board approval.

Motion: To waive a public hearing. Ruth, second Karen, 4-0-1 (Abby)

Motion: To approve the application since the CEO says it meets the standards of the ordinance. Karen, Ruth, 6-0-1 (Abby)

6. Robert Ray, Sr., 102 Cobbs Bridge Road, expedited site review, home improvements, RR and Historic Overlay zones.

Discussion: This is a ranch house in the historic overlay. Mr. Ray plans to add a porch replace the windows and siding and do considerable landscaping, improving the appearance significantly. All submissions were in the packet. It was noted that the historical society had not been notified.

Motion: To review this application under the standards of expedited review. Abby, second Ruth, 6-0-0

Motion: To approve the application of Robert Ray, Sr., since the home is not historically significant and its appearance will be improved. Abby, second Ruth, 6-0-0

7. Todd Donnelly, Promise Lane, review of amendment to Promised Land Subdivision, RR zone

Discussion: This was originally a minor subdivision was created in 1989 by Dennis McIntosh, and amended in 1991. Some of the early lots were exempt from review because of the 40-acre remaining land, and some were apparently created illegally. The plan now appears to have 13 lots. Ted Donnelly wants to subdivide lot 9, which is four acres in area. The plan includes note #6 that states that not lot will ever by subdivided. It was decided to consult the town attorney to find out whether or not and how the plan can be amended, and whether the other lot owners need to agree to it. NO further action was taken.

8. Other business:

Jeff Brinck, request for exemption of individual site reviews for land applications of the product Fiberlime.

Discussion: Fiberlime is an odorless liming agent and soil conditioner made of lime, clay and cellulose. The material and protocol for its application is approved by DEP and the Department of Agriculture.

Motion: To exempt Fiberlime from site-specific review. Abby, Ruth, 6-0-0.

Ruth mentioned that all structures in the historic district should undergo review and she has noticed a deck that has not.

9. Adjournment.

Motion: To adjourn. Abby, second Ruth, 6-0-0

__________________________

Jean Libby Chairman

Respectfully submitted by

Abigail R Lumsden

title: March 16th, 2004
html:
New Gloucester Planning Board

Minutes of March 16, 2004

Members Attending: Others Present:

Jean Libby, Chairman Kenneth Farrington

Karen Asselin, Vice Chairman Mike Thompson

Ruth Waterhouse Brian Thompson

Janet Smaldon George Chianis

Don Mendell

John Green

James Isaacson, Planner

Absent:

Abigail Lumsden (excused absence)

Topics: Ken’s Car Care, reconsider prior approval; Thompson Blue Grass Festival, site plan review; Nextell Communications, re-approval of prior request.

1. Minutes of March 2, 2004.

Motion: To approve the minutes of March 2, 2004 with a correction of the name “Ellison” to “Ellingson” in item #5. Ruth, second John 6-0-0.

2. Reconsideration of Ken’s Car Care, Kenneth Farrington, Lewiston Road, RB-1 and Groundwater Protection Overlay District

James reported that he had reviewed the approval given by the Board previously and found that towing wrecked cars was not an allowable use in the Groundwater Protection Overlay District. According to the Town Attorney, a use of that nature is similar to a “junkyard” and is, therefore, not permitted. The applicant and several of the board members questioned the comparison of this to a junkyard. Jean pointed out that this seemed more like commercial vehicle storage and should be prohibited on that basis. Don said that he thought the ordinance contradicted itself because it prohibits storing some parked cars, yet he is allowed to have a used car lot. Jean asked the Town Planner to look into these distinctions further to provide additional guidance to the Board on what they can approve and the board agreed to withhold taking any action until that information was received.

3. Thompson Blue Grass Festival, Mike Thompson, Gloucester Hill Road, RR District

(Jean recused herself as an abutter and Karen took over as Chair for this item.) Mike Thompson is planning to host a family bluegrass festival from June 25 – June 27 at Thompson’s Orchards on Gloucester Hill Road. The Board had several questions regarding the festival, including the number of people expected to attend, whether or not there would be camp fires for the campers, the hours of operations, and the plans for parking and waste disposal. The applicant stated that they expected about 2,500 people. There would be no campfires and parking would be available on-site, as well as at Hopco Excavation if necessary. Karen asked them to measure precisely how much parking space was available to determine if it would meet the requirement of 1 space for every 3 attendees. The size of the area for each campsite was also questioned and it appears that 20,000 square feet is needed for each site, but James is checking the ordinance further on that point because that seemed rather large. Mike stated that the hours of operation of the festival would be from 5:00 p.m. – 10:00 p.m. Friday, 9:00 a.m. – 10:00 p.m. Saturday and 9:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. on Sunday. A discussion was had about the allowable hours of operation because the ordinance has restrictions on certain decibel level noises in that area. The applicant agreed to check the decibel level of the music to help clarify that point. The board asked for a clearer site plan designating the location and size of the areas for parking, bathrooms, stage, etc. A site walk was set for Monday, March 22nd at 4:55 p.m. No action was taken on the plan.

4. Nextel Communication, Site plan re-approval request, KISS-FM Radio Tower, Gloucester Hill Road, RR District

The representative for the applicant, George Chianis, reported that nothing was changed in the application since the last approval, but the approval had lapsed so a renewal was required in order to get the building permit.

Motion: To re-approve the application based on the finding that all of the circumstances of the original approval were still the same. John, second Ruth, 6-0-0.

5. Other Business

James reported that he had reviewed the Village Store Site Plan and that it was ready to be signed. He also asked if any board members had questions or changes to the findings of fact in used to support the approval. No one had any changes. The plan was signed after the meeting.

6. Adjournment

Motion: To adjourn, Ruth, second Don, 6-0-0.

Jean Libby, Chairman

Respectfully Submitted

_________________________________

Karen Asselin

Motion: To approve the minutes of February 3, 2004. Ruth, second Janet. 7-0-0

Motion: To approve the minutes of February 17, 2004, with the following corrections, that Debbie Parks was present as a town official and that the uses permitted at the Village Store are subject to those permitted in the zoning ordinance. Ruth, second Karen, 6-0-1. (John, not present)

2. Michael Brady, Brady's Village Store, Intervale Road, amendment of uses, Village and Historic Districts

Note: John recused himself as an abutter to the Brady Penny Store

Public Hearing 7:34-8:05

Mike described the changes he was asked to make as re-labeling the space designated as a beauty shop, and the additional upstairs area as an efficiency apartment or office, noting that it reduces the size of the existing apartment.

Attorney and neighbor Fred Lipp acted as spokesperson for the group of neighbors objecting to the proposal and handed two documents to the board reviewing the zoning ordinance and giving a rationale for historic preservation.

Other neighbors who spoke were Dick Stone, Jennifer Muldoon, Joanne Cole, Diane Stone, Andy Fillmore, Doug Smith, Ed Domas, Deb Smith and John Gundersdorf. Although most mentioned they looked forward to having a neighborhood store the things they were concerned with included traffic safety, sufficient parking, the presence of above ground tanks, water use and other environmental factors, light pollution, the fact that the uses are not specified exactly, and a mini mall effect.

Discussion:

Karen mentioned that the permitted uses are listed in the ordinance, and James said that the two-story building is exempt from requirements for vertical handicapped access, but still must comply with bathrooms and hallway width. Jean reviewed the uses allowed and it was determined that the only applicable uses would be as an apartment, or retail/office space. Another consideration is parking. One parking space for each 300 square feet of building area is required. Access safety was another concern. Although the state does not ban backing onto a street the zoning ordinance does. The code enforcement officer said that clause only refers to new projects where there is not an established historical use. Mike said he plans to assign two parking spaces on the lower level for each of the upstairs uses, leaving five for the two downstairs uses. Making a theoretical total of nine spaces that fit the nine by eighteen-foot standard or parking spaces. The board said that the plan should include the parking designations. There should be no more that one freestanding sign, with other signs on the building itself complying with the sign ordinance. There shall be no more exterior lighting.

The conditions for granting approval include the following additions to the plan:

1. re-labeling the spaces within the building to reflect the uses allowed (retail of office space)

2. designating the assigned parking spaces

3. no further freestanding signs, with signs on the building adhering to the zoning ordinance

4. no additional exterior lighting

Motion: To deem the application complete with the above conditions. Abby, Ruth, 6-0-0

Motion: To approve the amended application of Michael Brady for an additional use at the Brady Village Store for the reasons stated in the Finding of Fact prepared by the Planner, Abby, second Ruth, 5-1-0 (Don, wants possible uses better defined)

3. Timothy Parks, et al., Cobble Hill Estates, Cobble Hill Road, amendment to an existing subdivision, RR and GWP zones.

Site walk review: The board had conducted a site walk the previous Saturday and found the land to be quite level, with no particular environmental problems, although the unusual access parallel access for two of the lots from McKinney Drive was questioned. Surveyor John Palmiter said it was caused by the fact that the drive could not cross the open land of McKinney Estates so he created a right of way across the Ellis lot. The access is from McKinney Drive since is means a shorter road construction.

Discussion: This application is presented by three residents as a re-division of three lots of an older subdivision.The applicants presented a new revised sketch plan showing reshaped lots and a reduction of the driveway right of way from 60 to25 feet. Abby questioned the odd shape of lot 6-2,which is not allowed per section 11.5.G of the zoning ordinance. The applicants said that the odd lot shapes are a result of drawing new lot lines to meet the required setbacks for the existing homes. Surveyor John Palmiter will reshape the lots again when he is available. Dick Sweet said the hydrogeological studies are almost complete and he sees no problem. There are no wetlands. He mentioned that there must be a 50-foot buffer along the McKinney Estates open space, but that a drive can go through it. There is also a question of the accuracy of the southern line of the subdivision.

The applicants wish to have this application treated as a minor subdivision since it is created three new lots from a major subdivision. James said it is a matter of interpretation. The applicants hope to have a fire pond waived. They are also requesting waivers for stone monuments, underground utilities, and 2-foot contours. Beverly Cadigan, whose mother is an abutter, said that lot 5-2 has steep areas. Ten-foot contour lines were considered adequate. Karen said that that board should also waive the requirement for submission of a cluster plan to be absolutely correct.

Motion: To waive the requirements for underground utilities since poles are common in the area, stone monuments as an unnecessary expense, and two-foot contours since ten-foot ones will provide enough information. Abby, second John, 7-0-0.

The application will return with a plan showing contours, buildings on reshaped lots, along with septic plans and phosphorus control.

4. Dennis Waterman, Ethel Sawyer Road, after-the-fact minor subdivision, RR, RC, RP and GPO districts

Discussion: This is the return of an application presented over a year ago for an illegal subdivision that has been in existence for a number of years. It is along the banks of the Royal River on the extension of a private road of unknown characteristics. The two issues that the board can deal with are the road and nitrate plumes. Dick Sweet has done the nitrate study and said that one of the systems does not meet the standards of the ordinance, since the plume crosses the lot line. He said that the most inexpensive way to deal with the problem is for the owner to get an easement from the abutter.

Developer Don Belanger asked that the Board treat all applicants equally and require the same compliance for this subdivision as any other. He mentioned that the road length exceeds what is allowed. Jean said that little can be done in after-the-fact applications.

Site Walk: Since several members of the board have not seen the site, a visits was scheduled for Monday, March 8, at 5:30PM

Discussion: The Ellingsons want to add an 850 square-foot one and a half story addition and a rear deck to a small home built around 1900. They plan a new well and septic system. The siding, trim and windows will be similar to the existing building and they do not plan extensive landscaping.

Best management practices will be used for erosion control during construction and cutting of existing vegetation will be kept to a minimum.

Motion: To waive a site visit. John, second Karen, 6-1-0 (Abby)

Motion: To waive contour lines, and storm water management plan. Karen, John, 7-0-0.

Motion: To waive a public hearing, Karen, second John, 7-1-0 (Abby)

Motion: To deem the application complete. Karen, second Ruth, 6-0-1 (Abby)

Motion: To approve the application of Daniel Ellingson with appropriate erosion control since it meets the conditions of the ordinance. Karen, second John, 6-0-1 (Abby)

Karen will take the minutes at the next meeting, since Abby will be absent.

7. Adjournment.

Motion: To adjourn. Karen, second John. 6-0-0

3. Village Store site plan amendment. Intervale Road. Mike Brady with Debbie Parks

A number of nearby residents were in attendance, since the original application has been a concern.

James had suggested in his memo that the board might take the opportunity to request a safer parking space plan, since several of the present ones must back onto Intervale Road to leave. Mike was resistant to this, since he already had approval for the necessary number of spaces, and did not want to make unnecessary changes. James said he had not measured the parking area and that the plan is not drawn to scale. The board also questioned the labeling on the uses with in the building. The beauty shop had been relabeled as retail space and the new space upstairs as an apartment. Debbie said that any change in use would have to be approved by her and would be in accordance with the conditions of the application. There will be no additional lighting and any signs will be attached to the building.

Motion: To deem the application complete with the conditions that the parking be reworked to provide better safety and relabeling the uses of the sections of the building. Karen, second Ruth, 6-0-0

Motion: To schedule a public hearing on March 3, 2004. Karen, second Don. 5-1-0 (Ruth)

4. Adjournment.

Motion: To adjourn. Karen, second Don. 6-0-0

Jean Libby Chairman

title: Vital Records: Birth, Marriage, and Death
html:
How do I obtain copies of birth, death, fetal death, marriage, divorce, and domestic partnership records?

By law, Maine birth records less than 75 years old, marriage records less than 50 years old, death records less than 25 years old and fetal deaths less than 50 years old are considered to be private. In order to inspect these documents, or to obtain copies, an individual must prove that they are permitted by law to do so. Those authorized to view or obtain a copy of a vital record include:

  • The person named on the record,
  • The person's spouse or registered domestic partner,
  • The parent(s) named on the record,
  • Descendants of the person named on the record (including children, grandchildren, and great grandchildren to the most remote degree),
  • The legal custodian, guardian, or authorized representative of the person named on the record, and
  • Genealogists who have a researcher card issued by the Maine Center for Disease Control and Prevention, Data, Research and Vital Statistics.

Effective July 12, 2010, all individuals requesting copies of these records must present positive identification and, if requesting the record of a parent or grandparent and you are not a registered genealogist, proof of direct lineage.

Registered genealogists may only obtain a non-certified copy of a record, unless they can meet the above requirements for obtaining a certified copy. They may only view or obtain a copy of a birth, death, or marriage record.

Why do I need to present positive identification when requesting a record?

While most requests for vital records are honest attempts to obtain one's own personal documentation, some are not; some are attempts to obtain information and documents needed to assume another person's identity. These documents can be used to obtain a driver's license, state photo ID, social security card, and passport under the assumed name, opening the door to credit card, bank and tax fraud; mail theft, and social security and insurance fraud. The requirement that you provide positive identification when requesting a copy of a record helps to protect you and your family from this type of crime.

What are acceptable forms of identification?
Acceptable forms of identification include a driver's license, passport or other government issued photo identification.

What if I do not have an acceptable photo ID?
If you do not have acceptable photo identification, you may present two items with your name on it from the following list: a utility bill, a bank statement, a car registration, a copy of an income tax return, a personal check with address, a previously issued vital record or marriage license, a letter from a government agency requesting a vital record (for example, the Maine Department of Health and Human Services), a Department of Corrections identification card, a Social Security card, a DD214, a hospital birth worksheet, a license or rental agreement, a pay stub (W-2), a voter registration card, a Social Security disability award letter, a Medicare or Medicaid insurance card, and a school or employee photo ID. Other forms of identification listing your name, date of birth, and address may also be considered.

How would a person demonstrate direct lineage?
In order to prove direct lineage when requesting records concerning your parents or grandparents, a copy of your birth certificate will identify your parents. If your parents were married, this document can be used to obtain a copy of your parents' marriage record, which should identify your grandparents.

Other acceptable proof of direct lineage could include a hospital or physician's record of birth or death, a baptismal record, school enrollment records, military records, court records, a family bible record; a newspaper engagement, marriage or birth announcement; an obituary, a U.S. Census enumeration record, an insurance application, or an affidavit.

How do I obtain a genealogical researcher ID card?
In order to obtain a genealogical research ID card you have to apply to the Maine Center for Disease Control and Prevention, Data, Research and Vital Statistics. You can find a link for the application on the Vital Records website listed as Genealogical Research Application.

Click below for the forms needed to request certificates:
Request Birth, Death or Marriage Certificate
Mail requests to:
Town of New Gloucester
385 Intervale Road
New Gloucester, Maine 04260
Please make all checks payable to the Town of New Gloucester and also enclose a stamped, self addressed return envelope.
Birth Certificates:
Birth certificates may be obtained from:
The town in which the child was born, (the Town in which the mother of the child was living at the time of the birth) or from the office of State Vital Records located in Augusta, ME.
The fee for a certified copy of a birth certificate is $15.00 for the first copy and $6.00 for any additional copies obtained at the same time.
Marriage Certificates:
A marriage license is obtained from the Town Clerk. Residents of the State can file their intentions and obtain a marriage license in the town in which at least one of them resides. Both the bride and groom must be present when they apply, to sign the application and the license.
If both parties reside outside the State of Maine, they may file in any town in Maine. Once their intentions are filed and the license is issued, they are free to marry anywhere in the State.
If married previously, applicants must present a certified copy of their divorce decree or former spouse's death certificate.
The license is issued on the same day that the application is filed. It is valid for 90 days after date of issue. The cost of the license is $40.00 per couple.
Following the ceremony, the license is permanently filed with the Town Clerk's office and the State of Maine. Certified copies can be obtained for a fee of $15.00 for the first copy and $6.00 for each additional copy.
Death Certificates:
Death certificates can be obtained from the Town where the person resided at the time of death or place of burial. Confidential information on the death certificate, including the cause of death, is available only to persons who have a direct legitimate interest in the matter recorded.
The fee for a certified copy of a death certificate is $15.00 for the first copy and $6.00 for any additional copies obtained at the same time.
Non-Certified Copies
Birth records 75 years or older, marriage records 50 years or older, death records 25 years or older and fetal deaths 50 years or older are considered public records and informational copies can be issued to anyone requesting them. The cost for a non-certified copy of a vital record is $10.00 and is stamped "not for legal purposes".

Town of New Gloucester

Employment Opportunity

Public Works Mechanic

Do you like problem solving? Do you enjoy the benefits of a built in three (3) day weekend? Do you thrive when provided autonomy for your role? If so, the Public Works Mechanic position could be right for you!

The Town of New Gloucester, Maine, Public Works Department, seeks to immediately fill our full-time Mechanic position. This position performs maintenance, Maine State inspections and repairs on all Town vehicles and equipment and requires knowledge of diagnostic analysis equipment, automotive and equipment repair, including gasoline and diesel engines, vehicles, heavy trucks, fire and rescue vehicles, and construction equipment. The ideal candidate for this position is a proactive and creative individual who can balance the maintenance preparation of town owned equipment, as well as unexpected and necessary repairs.

Qualifications for this position include: high school diploma or equivalent; a minimum of a Class B Maine driver’s license; must have, or have ability to obtain within three months, a State of Maine inspection license Class A, D, E & T; and experience in the maintenance, repair and operation of heavy and lighter trucks and other motorized equipment.

Salary range is $29.00-$32.00 per hour. A generous benefit package is available for this position including Maine State Retirement (MePERS Pension System) or 401K Retirement Program, Vacation Time, Sick time, Personal Days, 13 Paid Holidays, and a four-day Monday through Thursday work schedule. The full job description is available on our website www.newgloucester.com.

Pre-employment physical and CDL drug and alcohol screening are required for this position. To apply, please submit resume via email to smyers@newgloucester.com or by mail to Town of New Gloucester, Attn: Sharlene Myers, 385 Intervale Road, New Gloucester, ME 04260. Position will remain open until suitable candidate is found. The Town of New Gloucester is an equal opportunity employer.

New Gloucester Board of Assessment Review
html:
The Board of Assessment Review Committee is a new committee to New Gloucester.

At the June 9, 2026 Election, the Town approved a Board of Assessment Review Ordinance. This ordinance is to establish administrative procedures to review appeals from decisions made by the Assessors or Select Board on requests for property tax abatements and determinations that are necessary with respect to tax assessments according to the general laws of the State of Maine.

The Board shall consist of five (5) members. Members shall be residents of the Town of New Gloucester, at least 18 years of age and citizens of the United States at all times during their terms, and shall not be municipal officers or spouses of municipal officers or employees of the Town. Members shall be appointed by the Select Board. Initial appointees terms shall be: two (2) members for three-years; two (2) members for two-years; and one (1) members for one-year.

Please complete the Board and Committee application if you would like to serve on the Board of Assessment Review Committee.

title: Absentee Ballots for November 3rd Election
html:
ABSENTEE BALLOTS for November 3rd Election

Absentee Ballots are now available.

If you want to vote Absentee for the upcoming November 3rd Election, you may do one of the following:

  • Go to the Secretary of State website and request your ballot through the online portal
    • https://absenteeballotrequest.sos.maine.gov/. The Town receives the application from the State and will mail out your Absentee Ballots.
  • Print and fill out the Absentee Ballot Form (click here) and mail or bring to Town Office. Once received, we will issue the ballots.
  • Call the Town Office (207) 926-4126 x 1 and request over the phone (we must talk to the voter who is requesting a ballot). The Town will mail out your absentee ballot.

Automatic Absentee Ballot Request

The State now has a way to Absentee Vote each election and not make a request each time to do so. You may now fill out a form once at Town Hall (must be done in person) and Absentee Ballots will automatically be mailed to you for each Election. No phone calls. No filling out forms each time.
